jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Agentic Test Intelligence
jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As Staff Product Manager, Test & Code Coverage, you'll build product capabilities from initial discovery through launch and adoption. You'll help engineering teams understand why pipelines fail, improve test automation, and use code coverage to make better decisions about software quality and risk.

You'll turn a technically complex problem space into a focused strategy, roadmap, and developer experience. Working closely with Engineering and Design, you'll explore how agents can diagnose failures, recommend next steps, and help teams recover safely. The goal isn't to add artificial intelligence (AI) for its own sake. It's to reduce manual work and help developers get back to a safe, shippable state without losing trust or control.

At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. You'll contribute to that mission by making testing and coverage insights more useful across the software development lifecycle.

What you'll do

• Define and communicate the Test & Code Coverage product vision, strategy, and outcome-focused roadmap, from discovery through a minimum viable product, beta, launch, and continued iteration.

• Identify customer problems across pipeline failure diagnosis, test automation, test optimization, code coverage, and recovery. Build the case for investment, prioritize foundational and customer-facing work, and reshape or stop initiatives that aren't creating value.

• Work with Engineering to understand pipeline failures caused by flaky tests, testing gaps, environment issues, configuration problems, and coverage blind spots. Connect code changes, tests, pipeline behavior, historical patterns, and risk to help developers find a diagnosis and an actionable next step.

• Work directly with customers to understand how they author, maintain, select, prioritize, and debug tests. Connect test selection, test impact analysis, code coverage, and pipeline intelligence to reduce flaky tests, shorten feedback loops, and focus testing effort where it lowers the most risk.

• Partner with Engineering and Design to prototype agent-driven workflows for failure diagnosis, test authoring and repair, optimization, coverage analysis, and recovery. Make actions reviewable through evidence, confidence, human approval, and safe paths to propose code changes and merge requests. Use AI tools in your own product work to investigate problems, explore code and data, prototype concepts, and accelerate learning.

• Define and measure outcomes such as time to diagnose, time to recover, failure recurrence, test signal quality, and developer confidence. Validate problems and solutions with customers and learn from production usage.

• Partner across Product, Engineering, Design, Quality, Developer Experience, Customer Success, Support, and Product Marketing to connect testing insights with code review, pipelines, and release decisions. Turn customer evidence into clear narratives that support adoption and future investment.

• Lead through clear written communication, prioritization, and product judgment. Influence senior stakeholders, establish repeatable discovery and measurement practices, and mentor other product managers.

What you'll bring

• Experience owning complex technical products, platforms, or developer workflows at Staff, Senior Staff, Principal, or equivalent scope, including building a new product or capability from initial validation through launch and adoption.

• Strong product fundamentals in customer discovery, problem framing, prioritization, roadmap development, outcome measurement, and iterative delivery.

• Technical fluency in one or more relevant areas, such as software testing, test automation, code coverage, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), developer tools, DevOps, developer experience, quality engineering, or software delivery.

• An understanding of how engineering teams build, test, review, and ship software, and the ability to work with engineers on test architecture, pipeline behavior, code changes, data, integrations, reliability, and scale.

• Experience diagnosing technical problems and turning complex, noisy signals into clear user experiences and actionable workflows.

• Experience exploring AI or agent-driven solutions for developer workflows, with the judgment to distinguish useful automation from unsafe or low-confidence actions.

• Experience using customer conversations to understand problems and inform product decisions, communicating clearly in writing and conversation, and influencing across functions with shared ownership. You can work directly with developers, quality engineers, platform teams, engineering leaders, and executives, and move between strategy and implementation detail.

About the team

Our work brings together Product, Engineering, and Design, with input from Quality, Developer Experience, Customer Success, Support, and Product Marketing. We work directly with developers, quality engineers, and engineering leaders to understand their testing practices, validate ideas, and learn from how they use the product.

We give Engineering and Design clear customer context and room to shape solutions. Our decisions draw on customer evidence and measurable outcomes, and we revisit approaches that aren't creating value. You'll contribute to how we discover problems, prioritize work, and measure progress, as well as sharing product management practices with other product managers.

As part of GitLab's all-remote organization, we collaborate asynchronously across regions. Our work emphasizes transparency, written communication, and clear decision-making.

The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity. Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary.

$168,000—$285,600 USD

jobs.title: Director, HRBP - GTM
jobs.description:
THE TEAM

The People Team at Chainalysis is dedicated to enabling growth, building an inclusive environment, and providing the support that helps our employees do the best work of their careers. Chainalysis is at a defining moment, transforming from a product-based company to an intelligence platform AI native company. The People Team plays a critical role in ensuring our organization evolves as fast as our technology.



Our Go-To-Market organization, spanning Sales, Sales Engineering (Solution Architects), Customer Success, Partnerships, and Revenue Operations, is the engine driving that momentum. As we scale, our GTM teams need an HR Business Partner who operates with the same speed, intensity, and bias for action that defines the business itself.




THE ROLE

As Director, HR Business Partner, Go-To-Market, you will be the strategic people partner embedded directly within our GTM leadership team. This is a high-impact, individual contributor role at the Director level. You will not manage a team, but you will be expected to operate with the authority, judgment, and executive presence of a senior leader. You will own the full scope of people strategy for GTM end-to-end: from organizational design and talent planning to performance management, employee relations, and change management. You are the single point of accountability for translating business priorities into people initiatives that accelerate revenue growth.



A trusted, high-impact partnership with the COO will be critical to success in this role, one in which the HR Business Partner’s voice is heard, ideas are valued, and creative thinking shapes consequential people and business decisions. You are essential to GTM success.  With a significant body of work ahead, this is not a role for the faint of heart; it requires the imagination, resourcefulness, resilience, and influence to turn ambitious priorities into meaningful results.



Their role demands an execution-oriented leader, someone who doesn't wait for direction, moves fast, takes risks, is willing to make mistakes, drives outcomes with urgency, and brings a relentless focus on getting things done. You thrive in high-growth, high-change environments and are energized by the pace and complexity of a scaling GTM organization. You are equally comfortable coaching a CRO or COO through a sensitive org restructure as you are rolling up your sleeves to build a new compensation framework or run a talent calibration session from scratch.  Your opinion matters, have one.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU'LL:


DRIVE GTM PEOPLE STRATEGY WITH SPEED AND PRECISION

 - Own and execute the end-to-end people strategy for the Go-To-Market organization, directly partnering with the COO, CRO, and CCO to align talent priorities with revenue targets.

 - Lead organizational design efforts to ensure the GTM structure scales efficiently, proactively identifying gaps, redundancies, and opportunities to optimize team composition as the business evolves.

 - Develop and execute workforce planning strategies that anticipate hiring needs, succession gaps, and capability builds across Sales, Sales Engineering, Customer Success, Partnerships, and Revenue Operations.

 - Operate as a true business partner, not a support function. Bring data, recommendations, and a point of view to every leadership conversation, and hold leaders accountable to people's commitments.




OWN TALENT MANAGEMENT AND PERFORMANCE EXECUTION

jobs.title: Sr Imaging Scientist
jobs.description:
Job Description

Primary Function of Position

The Sr. Scientist, Imaging Science is responsible for the technical and scientific foundation of Intuitive's fluorescence imaging programs, spanning the clinical studies that establish agent performance and the imaging systems that deliver it. The position is accountable for maintaining alignment between the detection performance established through system characterization and the performance measured in clinical study.

The position requires depth across the full breadth of imaging science, from the definition and justification of clinical endpoints through the test methodology used to characterize imaging system and agent performance. Clinical development sits at the center of the position, bridging in two directions: toward Regulatory Affairs, where endpoints and imaging methodology must be defensible to health authorities, and toward Engineering, where the imaging systems of the future must resolve the imaging agents of today. The successful candidate will be equally effective in both. Near-term emphasis is on the scientific basis of Intuitive's registrational programs. As those study designs are finalized, responsibilities transition toward agent-device compatibility across current and future Intuitive platforms, ecosystem development, and computational tooling. The Principal Scientist partners with Clinical Development, Biostatistics, Regulatory Affairs, Imaging Systems Engineering, Software, Data Management, and external collaborators.

Roles and Responsibilities

Clinical Study Design and Imaging Data Interpretation

• Define primary, key secondary, and exploratory endpoints for imaging agent trials, and develop the clinical and literature justification supporting their performance thresholds.
• Partner with pathologists, surgeons, and investigators on the interpretation of imaging data by having a solid understanding of surgical, radiologic, and pathologic workflows.
• Develop study operations manuals focused on correlative analysis between intraoperative imaging and histopathology, including specimen mapping and the criteria by which fluorescence signal is matched to pathologic outcome.
• Develop imaging charters and fluorescence assessment procedures, establishing objective protocol-defined read criteria and a defensible reference standard.
• Oversee blinded independent central image review and reader agreement analyses, and lead scientific review of imaging data infrastructure, including database design, eCRF build, and data quality ahead of database lock.

Regulatory Strategy and Submissions

• Author imaging content for protocols, statistical analysis plans, briefing books, and clinical study reports, and maintain consistency of imaging and endpoint definitions across submission documents.
• Prepare technical content for health authority meetings and submissions, and contribute to responses to Agency questions and information requests.
• Translate health authority feedback into study design and documentation, and assess the applicability of regulatory guidance and precedent approvals to imaging agent programs.

Imaging Systems and Agent Performance

• Characterize agent performance on Intuitive platforms, including excitation and emission spectral matching, camera sensitivity, working distance, depth of detection, and signal-to-background ratio under clinically representative conditions.
• Design and execute bench and phantom studies establishing limit of detection, linearity, and reproducibility, and develop the tissue-mimicking models and fluorophore standards those studies require.
• Partner with Engineering and external collaborators on illumination, optical filter selection, sensor configuration, and display rendering, and define imaging system requirements for future platforms so next-generation systems can detect our agents.
• Work with Software Engineering on image processing and visualization algorithms, and assess how software and firmware changes affect agent detection and the clinical interpretation of fluorescence.
• Develop engineering test methods, protocols, and acceptance criteria, and contribute to design inputs, verification and validation, and design control documentation for agent-device combinations.
• Develop computational and machine learning approaches that accelerate image analysis, system characterization, and development timelines.

Qualifications

• PhD in biomedical optics, medical imaging, biomedical engineering, electrical engineering, medical physics, or a related field.
• Minimum 5 years of drug development experience, including direct contribution to programs advancing through clinical development toward regulatory submission.
• Demonstrated depth in optical or molecular imaging, including quantitative evaluation of detection performance against histopathology or an equivalent reference standard.
• Hands-on experience characterizing imaging system performance, including phantom design, spectral measurement, and sensitivity or limit-of-detection testing.
• Experience contributing to the design of clinical studies of imaging products, including endpoint definition and diagnostic performance measures.
• Proficiency in diagnostic accuracy methodology, including sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, reference standard design, verification bias, and reader variability, together with the ability to critically review a statistical analysis plan.
• Experience supporting regulatory activities, including authoring technical content for health authority submissions and meeting materials.
• Working knowledge of the therapeutic and surgical context in which the agent is used, sufficient to evaluate whether a proposed endpoint is clinically meaningful.

Preferred Qualifications

• Drug development experience overlapping with imaging hardware or device development.
• Experience with fluorescence-guided surgery, near-infrared imaging, or endoscopic and robotic imaging platforms.
• Familiarity with design controls and verification and validation processes.
• Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, or equivalent for image analysis, and experience applying machine learning to medical image data.
• Experience developing products in urologic oncology, urology, and/or genitourinary pathology therapeutic areas. Experience with prostatectomy preferred.

Due to the nature of our business and the role, please note that Intuitive and/or your customer(s) may require that you show current proof of vaccination against certain diseases including COVID-19.  Details can vary by role.

For any Intuitive role subject to export controls, final offers are contingent upon obtaining an approved export license and/or an executed TCP prior to the prospective employee’s start date, which may or may not be flexible, and within a timeframe that does not unreasonably impede the hiring need. jobs.title: PCS Lead Engineer, Power Generation
jobs.description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE ENERGY TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

 - Put solar, storage and gas in the ground at an install rate no one in the construction market has hit. We are building generation across multiple gigawatt sites at once, on a schedule traditional EPC delivery cannot meet.

 - Secure supply at a scale and timeline the supply chain cannot meet, and reshore it ourselves. Cells, containers, transformers and turbines are all constrained, so we qualify new suppliers and stand up domestic capacity instead of waiting in line.

 - Make solar, gas and storage combine into power steady enough to run AI workloads. A training run does not tolerate a dip, so the hybrid plant has to behave like firm generation even when the resource behind it does not.

 - Clear balancing authority certification, firm load rights, permits and interconnection against long clocks and a shifting policy environment. These approvals sit on the critical path to every gigawatt, so we work them years ahead of the build.


ROLE SCOPE

 - Own the power conversion layer across storage and solar, PCS and inverter topology, DC architecture, filtering and the conversion interface to MV collection, as one standard repeated across concurrent gigawatt sites.

 - Write the PCS and inverter specification vendors bid against, qualify platforms on measured behavior rather than datasheet, and hold OEM engineering to the spec through factory witness testing, site acceptance and warranty.

 - Set the converter-level control requirements that let the plant hold firm load, grid-forming and grid-following operation, ride-through, step-load response and reactive capability, and hand a defensible interface to the storage, controls and protection leads.

 - Lead conversion-side energization and commissioning in the field, through first charge and discharge, islanding and transfer tests, and step-load testing against real AI load profiles.

 - Root-cause converter trips, derates and firmware regressions across the fleet, and fold every fix back into the standard design so the next site does not repeat it.

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c.

 - You've taken power conversion from specification to energized and dispatching on grid-scale storage or solar, and you can name the sites and the megawatts.

 - You've written an inverter or PCS specification that a vendor bid against, then held that vendor to it when their standard product did not meet it.

 - You've debugged converter behavior in the field from scope traces, power quality captures and event records, and changed a setting or a firmware build as a result.

 - You've specified or validated grid-forming operation on a plant that has to survive islanded, and you know where the vendor datasheet stops matching the hardware.

 - You've carried a failure from a field symptom to a change in the standard design, not just to a site-level workaround.

 - You write clearly enough that an OEM engineer, a commissioning agent and a CEO each get the decision they need out of the same document.

 - Bonus: Grid-forming control and EMT validation (PSCAD, EMTP, PLECS). Converter design at the hardware level (magnetics, thermal, SiC and IGBT device selection). BESS and inverter certification (UL 1741 SA and SB, IEEE 1547, UL 9540A). Named PCS platforms (Power Electronics, SMA, EPC Power, Sungrow, Tesla). Behind-the-meter and islanded microgrid operation. Professional Engineer license.



We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. · Uses department’s resources efficiently; participates in efforts to reduce costs and streamline work processes.

Education:

jobs.title: Growth Creative Lead, Art Director
jobs.description:
About Ruggable:

Ruggable is a leading direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand based in Los Angeles, California with an extraordinary track record of high, profitable growth. We pride ourselves on having an extremely loyal customer base and a talented team made up of genuinely caring people who take action and deliver results. We are venture-backed and own a patented washable rug design that's disrupting the home décor industry. Our mission is to empower our customers to live vibrantly with beautiful products that don't compromise on function. If you're passionate about consumer products, e-commerce, and high-growth start-ups, keep reading!

Job Summary:

Ruggable is building an evergreen creative dream team that makes entertaining & compelling work across paid advertising, organic social, email, and the website. We’re looking for a Growth Creative Lead with strong art direction and design roots who can turn customer insights into ideas and stories people want to watch, share, and act on.

You’re a maker yourself, or you’ve spent enough time working alongside makers to know how great content gets made. You’re connected to the creative community in Los Angeles, enthusiastic about interior design, and fluent in how storytelling changes across short and long-form channels.

You’ll partner closely with Creative Strategy, Brand & Marketing leadership to turn insights into repeatable content engines, understand the metrics behind creative performance, and find new ways to scale products and ideas that are gaining traction. You’ll help lead the visual development of evergreen campaigns and content series from concept through production and channel-specific execution. This is a hands-on role: you should be comfortable making work yourself, directing others, and giving clear feedback to creators, designers, editors, and production partners. TLDR: You should be as interested in why a six second hook works as you are in what makes a room worth looking at.

What You’ll Do:

• Concept, make, and art direct creative across paid advertising, organic social, email, and the website, adapting ideas for both short and long-form formats.

• Partner with Creative Strategy to turn customer insights, product opportunities, and cultural observations into repeatable content series and creative tests.

• Use performance metrics to understand which ideas are working, improve the work, and scale creative around products gaining traction.

• Bring an informed point of view on interiors, design, and how people live with Ruggable products. Translate that perspective into stories that build our franchise muscle so they feel useful, inspiring, and specific.

• Translate concepts and scripts into storyboards, shot lists, and visual references that give creators and production partners a clear direction.

• Partner with Brand to help stage and style rooms for shoots or CGI initiatives, making thoughtful choices about furniture, props, lighting, and rug placement so the product feels desirable and believable in a real home.

• Tap into and build relationships with LA makers, creators, and production talent who can bring fresh skills and perspectives to the work.

• Lead visual development from concept through shoot, edit, sound and delivery. Make work yourself when that’s the best way to move an idea forward.

• Partner with the senior writer and videographers on hooks, scripts, and storytelling, then guide designers, editors, creators, and production partners through execution.

• Work with channel partners to tailor creative to where it will appear and use what the team learns to shape the next round of work.

What You’ll Need to Have:

Required:

• 7+ years of experience in strong art direction and design craft, with a portfolio spanning social-first video, digital campaigns, and work made for different channels and formats.

• Highly skilled in Figma

• A maker’s mindset. You can develop an idea, create or prototype parts of it yourself, and guide it through production and edit.

• Experience directing creators, designers, editors, agencies, and production partners, with a talent for giving clear, useful feedback that makes the work stronger.

• A genuine interest in interiors and design, and a point of view on how to make spaces, products, and the people who live with them compelling on screen.

• Fluency in short and long-form storytelling, including how an idea should change for the channel and audience.

• An understanding of creative performance metrics and experience using results to improve work, develop new variations, and scale promising ideas.

• Familiarity with the Los Angeles maker and creator landscape, with the ability to find and collaborate with talent whose perspectives strengthen the work.

• The judgment to balance creative ambition with the pace of an evergreen team, and the curiosity to keep learning what resonates with customers.

Preferred:

• You may have held a title such as Art Director, Senior Art Director, Associate Creative Director, or Creative Lead. The strength and range and breath of ideas in your work matter more than the exact title.

• Interest and background mentoring or managing others

• In-house experience

Compensation & Location Details:

• $140,000-$165,000 per year base salary based on experience

• An annual bonus percentage that varies based on level of role

• Employer matching (up to 3% of base salary) for company sponsored 401K plan

• This role requires onsite (2-3 days per week) in our Torrance, CA Location

At Ruggable, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages. Ruggable is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.description:

Who You Are

• As a Sales Advisor, you'll be passionate about fashion and everything we create in-store.
• Motivated by giving customers a great experience.
• You should also be communicative, creative and curious, motivated, flexible, decisive, and action-oriented.
• You should also enjoy working in a collaborative and dynamic environment.
• You have sales experience working in a dynamic and collaborative environment that you can apply to your role

Why You'll Love Working at H&M

• We value diverse backgrounds, including but not limited to race, ethnicity, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, and disability
• We pride ourselves on being a values-driven organization, guided by our 7 unique values that have been part of our success story for over 75 years

• You'll be able to express your personal style with our employee discount at H&M, & Other Stories, and COS

Job Status: Hourly, Non-Exempt

EEOC Code: SLS

Compensation: Sales Associates Pay Rate $13.25 per hour**

*This job posting highlights the most critical responsibilities and requirements of the job and is not all-inclusive. There may be additional duties, and responsibilities assigned for this job at the company's discretion.

**H&M, in good faith, has assessed this posted range of compensation as the accurate range for this role and location at the time of this posting. H&M may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on candidate qualifications. This range may be modified in the future.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. If you require assistance or accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us at https://hm.ethicspoint.com, and use Ask a Question.

Benefits:

We offer all our employees at H&M Group attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. Brands covered by the discount are H&M (Beauty and Move included), COS, Weekday, Monki, H&M HOME, & Other Stories, ARKET, Afound. In addition to our staff discount, all our employees are included in our H&M Incentive Program – HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here.

In addition to our global benefits, all our local markets offer different competitive perks and benefits. Please note that they may differ between employment type and countries.

Inclusion & Diversity:

H&M is a part of H&M Group. At H&M Group, we’re determined to create and maintain inclusive, diverse and equitable workplaces throughout our organization. Our teams should consist of a variety of people that share and combine their knowledge, experience and ideas. Having a diverse workforce leads to a positive impact on how we address challenges, on what we perceive possible and on how we choose to relate to our colleagues and customers all over the world. Hence, all diversity dimensions are considered in our recruitment process.

We strive to have a fair and equal process and therefore kindly ask you not to attach a cover letter in your application as they often contain information that easily can trigger unintentional biases.

Company Description:

H&M is a fashion brand that offers the latest styles and inspiration, from fashion pieces and unique designer collaborations to affordable wardrobe essentials. Our business idea is fashion & quality at the best price in a sustainable way. Learn more about H&M here.

H&M Fashion USA, Inc. – Maki Assessment Tool:

We use an online assessment tool called Maki for skills-based selection of applicants for sales advisor positions within some of our stores. Maki is not an automated decision-making tool. Rather, it is a tool that uses an AI-created avatar to present to you a set of multiple-choice questions. These questions are prepared by the H&M hiring team to assess candidates’ ability to perform the duties of the position for which they are applying. The assessment calculates your total score based on predefined point values provided by our H&M team. The hiring team will review your whole application, including your assessment score, to decide whether to advance each candidate to the next stage. Doing the assessment is optional. If you choose to complete the assessment, your score will be one factor that the hiring team considers.

If you have any difficulties or concerns with the online assessment method, you can request an alternative method of assessment by contacting recruitment_support@hm.com. Choosing an alternative method will not affect your chances of being considered for the position, nor does any assessment method provide an advantage or disadvantage in the selection process. You will have the opportunity to provide optional feedback immediately after the assessment and you may always ask questions.

When you take the assessment, we collect your responses and use this information to evaluate your suitability for the role to which you have applied. The answers are saved in your applicant profile. We do not sell the information captured in the questionnaire and do not use any personal information to train any AI models. Our applicant tracking system provider has access to this information but is contractually prohibited from using it for any other purpose.

During this process, we may collect information from you through cookies, with your consent. This may include details such as your electronic network activity information (IP address, timestamps, and device identifiers). This information is accessible to our hiring team but is otherwise kept confidential. For more information, please refer to our Cookie Notice.

We retain this information for 3 years in your applicant file and use it as set forth in our Applicant Privacy Notice. For more information on how your personal data is processed by us, please refer to our Applicant Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Counsel, Federal Government Contracting
jobs.description:
At Accenture Federal Services, nothing matters more than helping the US federal government make the nation stronger and safer and life better for people. Our 13,000+ people are united in a shared purpose to pursue the limitless potential of technology and ingenuity for clients across defense, national security, public safety, civilian, and military health organizations.

Join Accenture Federal Services, a technology company within global Accenture. Recognized as a Glassdoor Top 100 Best Place to Work, we offer a collaborative and caring community where you feel like you belong and are empowered to grow, learn and thrive through hands-on experience, certifications, industry training and more.

Join us to drive positive, lasting change that moves missions and the government forward!

You are

An experienced federal contracts attorney and strategic legal advisor to Business and Sales leadership in shaping and executing Accenture Federal Services’ (AFS) market-facing strategies.  This attorney will focus on U.S. federal procurements and government contracting matters, supporting the company’s federal business from opportunity identification and capture through proposal, contract award, performance, modification, and closeout. The role will work closely with business leaders, sales and capture teams, contracts professionals, finance, security, compliance, procurement, and other corporate functions to identify and manage legal and regulatory risks while enabling the company to pursue and deliver innovative technology and consulting solutions to federal customers.

This manager-level counsel position will be a practical, business-oriented attorney who understands that the role of in-house counsel is not simply to identify legal issues, but to help the business understand its options, make informed decisions, and execute effectively. The successful candidate will become a trusted partner to the company’s federal business. Rather than serving solely as a contract reviewer, this attorney will be embedded in the business and will help teams identify issues early, understand practical options, structure transactions appropriately, and move opportunities forward while protecting the company’s interests. The ideal candidate is comfortable operating in situations where the answer is not simply "yes" or "no" and can distinguish between legal requirements, contractual obligations, business preferences, and manageable commercial risk.

The Work

• Advise on Federal Procurements: Provide legal counsel throughout the federal procurement lifecycle.

• Partner with the Business: Serve as a trusted legal advisor to sales, business development, capture, contracts, and delivery teams, providing practical, business-oriented advice that enables the company to pursue and perform federal business effectively.

• Draft and Negotiate Agreements: Review, draft, and negotiate federal contracts, subcontracts, teaming agreements, NDAs, licenses, statements of work, and other agreements supporting federal business.

• Manage Federal Contracting Risk: Identify and advise on legal and contractual risks involving FAR and agency-specific requirements, and federal contracting compliance matters.

• Support Cross-Functional Operations: Collaborate with corporate functions peers on issues arising from federal contracts and procurements.

• Provide Strategic Guidance: Translate complex federal procurement requirements into clear, actionable advice; develop practical contracting guidance; and advise business leaders on risk-based approaches to achieving commercial objectives.

• Support a Scalable Legal Function: Develop and improve processes that enable business and contracts teams to efficiently manage federal procurement and contracting requirements while maintaining legal and compliance controls.

What you need

• U.S. Citizenship.

• Juris Doctor from an accredited law school and eligibility for admission as Virginia Corporate Counsel.

• 5+ years of experience at a law firm, U.S. government, or in-house legal department

• 3+ years of relevant legal experience, including substantial experience with U.S. federal government contracts and procurement.

• Strong working knowledge of the FAR and applicable federal agency supplements, particularly the DFARS where applicable.

• Experience reviewing and negotiating federal contracts, solicitations, teaming agreements, subcontracts, and related commercial agreements.

• Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to explain complex legal requirements clearly to business stakeholders.

• Strong business judgment and the ability to identify material risks without unnecessarily impeding business objectives.

• Ability to work independently in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment and manage multiple priorities.

jobs.description:
This is a U.S. based position. All of the programs we support require U.S. citizenship to be eligible for employment. All work must be conducted within the continental U.S.

Who we are:

Raft (https://TeamRaft.com) is a customer-obsessed non-traditional defense tech company dedicated to empowering U.S. military and government agencies with cutting-edge AI/ML and data solutions. We are a leader in autonomous data fusion and Agentic AI, with a purposeful focus on Distributed Data Systems, Platforms at Scale, and Complex Application Development. With headquarters in McLean, VA, our range of clients includes innovative federal and public agencies leveraging design thinking, cutting-edge tech stack, and cloud-native ecosystem. We build digital solutions that impact the lives of millions of Americans.

About the role:

As a Senior Director of Command and Control, you will bridge the gap between warfighters and engineers by bringing deep operational command and control expertise to Raft's most important customer engagements.

This Field CTO role is focused on command and control innovation in the Pacific, with an emphasis on identifying operational challenges, evaluating potential solutions, and helping rapidly deliver capabilities that improve mission execution.

You will work directly with operational users and senior leaders to understand how they execute the mission, identify opportunities to improve their workflows, and translate those needs into capabilities that can be delivered through MAKA Edge or other available platforms and technologies. When an operational team needs a new dashboard, form, database, workflow, application, automation, or data integration, you will help define the problem and work with Raft's product and engineering teams and experts across PACAF to determine the best way to deliver the capability.

You will also help evaluate emerging government and commercial technologies for potential operational use. Where a third-party application or capability provides value, you will work with the appropriate technical teams and mission partners to determine how it can be integrated into the appropriate operational environment and connected to existing data, applications, and workflows.

This is not a software engineering role. Your value comes from a deep understanding of command and control, air operations, operational planning, and how technology can improve mission execution. You will provide the operational context that enables engineers and product teams to build and integrate the right capabilities, while keeping the focus on real mission needs and measurable operational outcomes.

What You'll Do

• Lead C2 innovation efforts focused on solving high-value operational challenges across PACAF and the broader Indo-Pacific theater.

• Build strong working relationships across PACAF headquarters, Air Operations Centers, operational units, and Joint mission partners to understand operational priorities and identify opportunities for digital modernization.

• Conduct mission discovery with operators and leaders to identify problems that can be addressed through software, data, artificial intelligence, automation, or improved integration.

• Translate operational requirements into clear problem statements, priorities, and desired mission outcomes that product, design, and engineering teams can act upon.

• Identify repetitive, manual, disconnected, or data-intensive C2 processes that can be simplified or automated.

• Help determine the most appropriate technical approach for solving operational problems, whether through MAKA Edge, another Raft platform, an existing government environment, or a third-party capability.

• Work alongside Raft product and engineering teams throughout development and integration, providing operational context, validating requirements, gathering user feedback, and ensuring capabilities solve the intended mission problem.

• Help establish and prioritize capability roadmaps based on mission value, operational demand, user adoption, and technical feasibility.

• Facilitate operational discovery sessions, demonstrations, experimentation, and user feedback sessions focused on solving specific mission problems.

• Identify emerging commercial and government technologies that may provide operational value to PACAF and other mission partners.

• Evaluate third-party applications and capabilities based on their ability to improve mission outcomes and, when appropriate, help determine how they can be integrated into existing operational environments.

• Champion an open-architecture approach in which capabilities developed by Raft, government organizations, and other commercial technology companies can operate together within a coherent mission environment.

• Help move promising concepts from operational need to prototype to fielded capability through rapid experimentation and iteration.

• Measure the adoption and operational impact of delivered capabilities and use those results to inform future priorities.

• Represent Raft in engagements with senior Air Force, Joint, and mission-partner stakeholders.

• Maintain awareness of emerging developments in command and control, battle management, data, artificial intelligence, and digital modernization and identify opportunities to apply those capabilities to operational problems.

• Partner with Raft leadership, product, engineering, and delivery teams to ensure customer efforts remain aligned with mission priorities and Raft's broader product strategy.

What we are looking for:

• 20+ years of leadership experience in U.S. military operations, preferably including senior leadership positions within the U.S. Air Force.

• Extensive experience in command and control, air operations, operational planning, battle management, or related mission areas.

• Deep understanding of Air Force and Joint command and control, including how headquarters staffs, Air Operations Centers, operational units, and Joint partners plan and execute operations.

• Demonstrated ability to understand complex operational problems, identify the underlying mission need, and develop practical approaches to improve mission execution.

• Experience leading organizations and initiatives involving operational innovation, modernization, or the introduction of new capabilities.

• Proven ability to build trusted relationships with senior military and civilian leaders and operate effectively across organizational boundaries.

• Ability to translate operational concepts and user needs into clear requirements that software product and engineering teams can understand and act upon.

• Technical fluency sufficient to understand and communicate about modern software, data platforms, cloud environments, applications, artificial intelligence, APIs, and system integration at a conceptual level. You do not need to write code or design technical architectures.

• Intellectual curiosity about emerging technology and an ability to evaluate technology based on the operational problem it solves rather than the technology itself.

• Strong executive communication and presentation skills.

• Ability to operate independently in complex and ambiguous environments and turn broad mission needs into executable actions.

• A bias toward action, experimentation, collaboration, and measurable mission outcomes.

Highly preferred:

• Senior-level leadership experience within Pacific Air Forces or the Indo-Pacific theater.

• Significant experience with Air Operations Centers, theater-level C2, air component operations, or Joint command and control.

• Operational aviation experience.

• Experience developing or implementing new operational concepts, capabilities, or processes within the Air Force.

• Familiarity with distributed operations, Agile Combat Employment, Joint All-Domain Command and Control, theater battle management, and related modernization initiatives.

• Experience working across Air Force, Joint, allied, and partner organizations.

• Experience evaluating, experimenting with, or introducing commercial technology into operational military environments.

Clearance Requirements:

• Active Top Secret clearance

• Must be eligible for Sensitive Compartmented Information access as required

Salary Range: $225,000.00 - $265,000.00

Work Type:

• Honolulu, Hawaii / Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam area

• Primarily on-site with PACAF and mission partners.

• Periodic travel throughout the Indo-Pacific region and to Raft locations within the continental United States may be required.

What we will offer you:

• Highly competitive salary

• Fully covered healthcare, dental, and vision coverage

• 401(k) and company match

• Take as you need PTO + 11 paid holidays

• Education & training benefits

• Generous Referral Bonuses

• And More!

Our Vision Statement:

We bridge the gap between humans and data through radical transparency and our obsession with the mission.

Our Customer Obsession:

We will approach every deliverable like it's a product. We will adopt a customer-obsessed mentality. As we grow, and our footprint becomes larger, teams and employees will treat each other not only as teammates but customers. We must live the customer-obsessed mindset, always. This will help us scale and it will translate to the interactions that our Rafters have with their clients and other product teams that they integrate with. Our culture will enable our success and set us apart from other companies.

How do we get there?

Public-sector modernization is critical for us to live in a better world. We, at Raft, want to innovate and solve complex problems. And, if we are successful, our generation and the ones that follow us will live in a delightful, efficient, and accessible world where out-of-box thinking, and collaboration is a norm.

Raft’s core philosophy is Ubuntu: I Am, Because We are. We support our “nadi” by elevating the other Rafters. We celebrate each other and our cognitive and cultural diversity. We are devoted to our practice of innovation and collaboration.

jobs.title: Microgrid Architect Lead, Power Generation
jobs.description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE POWER GENERATION TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

 - Build an islanded grid at gigawatt scale, from a blank sheet. Generation, storage and compute running with no utility behind them, where the machine you design is the only thing holding frequency. No playbook exists at this size, so the architecture you set becomes the reference.

 - Get power online in months, not years. Interconnection queues are measured in years and we do not have them. Generating our own power is how a site goes from signed lease to live compute inside six months, and the power system is the long pole in that plan.

 - Make one power block, then build it a thousand times. A repeatable block and cluster unit, validated once and stamped across the fleet, is the only route to the scale we are targeting. Every bespoke site is schedule we do not get back.

 - Design a grid whose largest load answers back. Compute is not passive demand here. Load behaviour, curtailment and shedding are design variables you negotiate and specify, a lever almost no power system engineer has ever been handed.
   


ROLE SCOPE

 - Own the system design basis for the islanded grid, fixing voltage levels, topology, grounding, redundancy boundaries and the repeatable block and cluster unit, with v1 and the site and block single-lines issued inside six months.

 - Treat the block as a product rather than a project, holding one standard design across sites, driving out the variation that turns a repeatable build back into bespoke engineering, and freezing the design early enough that procurement and construction are never absorbing late change.

 - Write the internal grid code that every generator, BESS, inverter, transformer and ITR must meet, own the conformance evidence that proves compliance before equipment ships rather than after it lands, and own the technical content of generation and electrical equipment specifications and the technical evaluation of bids, with v0.1 in vendors' hands before the first major RFP.

 - Build the model of record yourself and own the study register, producing the first-pass generation, BESS and reserve sizing and the first load flow, short circuit and transient stability results, then accepting or rejecting every vendor and EPC study against it.

 - Set the stability and protection philosophy, covering the loss-of-largest-unit contingency, reserve policy and a load shedding scheme with compute as a participating resource, and negotiate the load behaviour specification with the compute side that everything downstream depends on.

 - Own the phasing rule, so whether the next block can be energised safely is your call at every intermediate build state, and set the prioritised study roadmap that says which studies must be in hand before long-lead procurement commits.

 - Close the loop from the field back into the standard, going to site to see how the design is actually built and operated, and folding every commissioning finding and every installer workaround into the next revision so block fifty goes in faster and cleaner than block one.

 - Hire the specialists behind you in sequence: a protection and HV substation engineer, a studies and EMT engineer to take modelling off your desk, and the operations counterpart who will own dispatch, reserves and switching orders long before commissioning.

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c.

 - You have delivered a real islanded or very weak-grid power system at 100MW or more, on an island or remote utility, a mining or LNG captive plant, an OEM power systems group, or a specialist islanded-systems practice. A grid-tied microgrid is not the same problem.

 - You build the models with your own hands, deep EMT work in PSCAD or equivalent alongside RMS, and you have personally produced the load flow, short circuit and stability results that decisions were made on.

 - You have designed around grid-forming inverter control and inverter-dominated protection, where there is little or no synchronous machine underneath you to hide behind.

 - You have personally owned a system design basis that vendors were held to, and you have rejected a vendor or EPC study that did not meet it.

 - You have been in the room when an island went dark, and you were the one who had to explain why.

 - You set standards that OEMs and EPCs actually comply with, GE, Caterpillar, Tesla and their equivalents, on technical authority rather than headcount or a title.

 - You have designed something that got built many times over, and you hold the discipline that comes with it: you freeze a design, you say no to the change that would have been a small improvement and a large disruption, and you have watched what a late revision does to a supply chain.

 - You spend time where the work happens, and the standards you write are shaped by what you saw installers and operators actually do rather than by what the drawing assumed they would.

 - Bonus: ERCOT market and interconnection dynamics. GW-scale HV substation design (230kV and above). Professional Engineer licence. Toyota Production System or lean practice applied to design and build (standard work, built-in quality, design freeze discipline). Load shedding and dispatch schemes that treat flexible load as a participating resource. Utility control room and switching order design.



We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.



You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application--  someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Orbit
jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As Principal Product Manager, Orbit, you'll define the vision, strategy, and roadmap for GitLab's software lifecycle context graph. Orbit connects source code and software development lifecycle data into a structured map of systems, relationships, dependencies, and ownership. You'll help engineers, software leaders, and artificial intelligence (AI) agents understand how teams build software and how changes affect the systems around it.

You'll shape Orbit from its underlying graph model and query experiences through customer value, pricing, packaging, launch, and adoption. This role combines technical product leadership with building a business around software lifecycle context. You'll balance foundational platform work with near-term customer needs, working directly with technical customers and senior Engineering and Design leaders.

You'll join Anand Ahire's product organization and partner across Product, Engineering, Design, Product Marketing, Sales, Solutions Engineering, and Customer Success, including the teams building GitLab Duo and the broader AI-powered development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) platform.

What you'll do

• Define Orbit's multi-year vision and roadmap across graph models and ontology, ingestion and indexing, query and retrieval, developer and agent interfaces, governance, and enterprise readiness. Shape how Orbit works across GitLab.com, Self-Managed, Dedicated, GitLab Duo Agent Platform, MCP-based external agents, APIs, and developer tooling.

• Turn complex platform opportunities into customer problems, measurable outcomes, and investment decisions. Use evidence to decide where to invest, iterate, partner, or stop.

• Partner with Engineering and Design on architecture and implementation tradeoffs across graph data models, indexing, query systems, application programming interfaces (APIs), Model Context Protocol (MCP), authorization, and scale.

• Use AI tools such as Claude Code and GitLab to investigate problems, explore code and data, prototype concepts, and create or review merge requests when that's the fastest way to learn.

• Lead discovery with developers, engineering leaders, platform teams, security teams, and technical executives to validate needs around dependencies, ownership, change impact, vulnerability exposure, pipeline health, and software delivery risk. Build repeatable feedback into roadmap decisions and help customers understand the value of connected graph context over disconnected searches or API calls.

• Define target customers, priority use cases, differentiated value, and the path to product-market fit. Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Pricing, and Finance on positioning, packaging, pricing, launch, adoption, and expansion.

• Develop business cases and track adoption, retention, usage, customer value, and revenue outcomes. Support executive briefings, analyst conversations, customer workshops, and field enablement.

• Align teams and executive leaders around clear recommendations and tradeoffs without relying on direct authority. Mentor other product managers, share practical frameworks, and represent GitLab's product vision in customer and industry conversations.

What you'll bring

About the Role:

As the General Ledger Senior Accountant, you'll be the go-to person for everything related to Prepaid Expenses and Leases. On a typical day, you'll review new lease agreements to determine accounting implications, reconcile monthly lease journal entries back to Lease Query, and collaborate closely with Project Managers, Finance, Procurement, and Operations to identify when leases are expected to commence. You'll also own the reconciliation of the prepaid expenses sub-ledger to the general ledger, prepare Prepaids waterfalls across Crusoe's consolidated entities, and manual prepaid reconciliations to keep everything accurate and audit-ready.

Beyond the day-to-day mechanics, you'll play a key role in the monthly close process, preparing journal entries, supporting fluctuation analysis, and partnering with the Cloud Operations, Data Infrastructure teams and various Accounting functions on new leases, modifications and prepaids. You'll thrive in this role if you're detail-oriented, comfortable working with large volumes of data, and energized by finding smarter, more efficient ways to get things done. This position is ideal for someone who can work independently, take ownership of their responsibilities, and stay a step ahead in a fast-paced, rapidly evolving environment while also lending support on audits, due diligence, and other projects as they arise.



 

What You'll Be Working On:

 - Review new lease agreements and lease modifications and input them into LeaseQuery

 - Track and reconcile lease activity on a month-to-month basis

 - Project Managers, Finance, Procurement, and Operations to identify when leases are expected to commence

 - Reconcile Lease Liabilities and ROU Asset balances from LeaseQuery to general ledger

 - Reconcile the prepaid expenses sub-ledger to the general ledger

 - Prepare and reconcile monthly and year-to-date Prepaid asset waterfalls across Crusoe's consolidated legal entities

 - Prepare and record monthly close journal entries

 - Support monthly reporting and fluctuation analysis

 - Collaborate with the Cloud Operations, Data Infrastructure teams and various Accounting functions on leases and prepaid expenses

 - Support audit and due diligence requests as needed

 - Perform other duties as assigned



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - 4-6 years of general ledger accounting experience

 - Experience with leases accounting

 - Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field

 - Solid understanding of GAAP

 - Working knowledge of internal controls and accounting best practices

 - Understanding of consolidations, joint ventures, and intercompany transactions

 - Exposure to and understanding of month-end financial reporting processes



Bonus Points

 - Keen attention to detail, even when moving quickly

 - Ability to work with and manipulate large volumes of data

 - Comfort working independently, taking ownership, and adapting in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment

 - A forward-thinking mindset- able to anticipate issues before they arise and proactively identify solutions

jobs.title: ABA Supervisor
jobs.description:
Title: Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) Hybrid Remote

Location: Naperville, IL and Surrounding Areas (Hybrid Option Available)

At Cortica, our Board-Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs) use a strength-based, holistic approach to clinical programming for children with autism and other neurodevelopmental differences. Our valued BCBAs are leaders who make a difference and create a supportive environment where all clinicians in our transdisciplinary team can thrive, grow, and make a meaningful, long-term impact for families.

You’ll provide groundbreaking, neurodiversity-affirming care, while enjoying the flexibility and support you deserve.

Why Choose Cortica?

We’re excited to support your continued professional development, growth, well-being, and ability to make a meaningful impact as part of a transdisciplinary team. That's why our compensation and benefits package has been designed to support you personally and professionally:

• Earning Potential (Salary +Productivity Bonus): $91,000- $114,000

• Plus earn up to an additional 10% of your monthly salary with our second bonus – that’s right, TWO bonuses to increase your earning potential!

• Generous Time Off to Recharge and Maintain Work-Life Balance: Up to 22 days off in your first year, increasing to 26 days after 12 months.

• Flexible Hybrid Role: We offer remote flexibility, allowing you to balance your clinical work and administrative tasks on your terms. Telehealth is determined by the BCBA when it's clinically effective for the client and BT.

• CEU Stipend: $2,000 annually to support your continued professional development.

• License Reimbursement: We cover the cost of your BCBA license renewal.

• 401(k) Matching: Helping you plan for your future with matching contributions.

• Comprehensive Health Coverage: Including medical, dental, vision, life, disability insurance, plus pet insurance—because we care about your entire family, furry friends included!

• Set Scheduling: Predictable work hours help you balance your work and personal life.

Your Role and Impact

As a BCBA at Cortica, you’ll play a pivotal role in overseeing neurodiversity-affirming clinical programming for patients receiving ABA treatment. You'll lead a team of behavior technicians (BTs), empowering them to make a lasting difference in the lives of children with developmental differences.

What you’ll love about this role:

• Achievable Targets: You’ll average 26 billable hours per week, with reduced targets during shorter weeks to ensure a manageable workload.

• Industry-Leading Dual Bonus Program: Enjoy two separate bonus opportunities that reward your impact and leadership.

- Productivity Bonus: Increase your earning potential through flexible productivity incentives designed to reward additional billable hours while maintaining work-life balance.

-ABA Caseload Bonus: Earn additional monthly bonus opportunities based on ABA direct service hours billed and converted within your POD, with bonus potential up to 10% of monthly base salary.

• Growth and Advancement Opportunities: You'll have the chance to advance through BCBA levels I, II, III, and IV, increasing your leadership impact along the way. At BCBA levels III and IV, productivity targets are reduced to 22, allowing you to focus on developing leadership skills, cultivating other talents, and exploring broader professional interests.

• Autonomy over Your Schedule: You’ll have full control over when and where you supervise your cases, empowering you to design a schedule that works for you.

• Administrative Support: Focus on what you do best—clinical care—while our dedicated team handles scheduling, billing, and credentialing, leaving you with more time to focus on your work and patients.

Qualifications and Requirements

• Master’s degree in human services or a related field.

• Current BCBA (Board-Certified Behavior Analyst) Certification required.

What Makes Cortica Different from Other ABA Companies?

At Cortica, we believe in going beyond traditional ABA practices to offer a more comprehensive, patient-centered approach that is different from other ABA companies:

• A Transdisciplinary Approach to Care: Unlike many ABA companies that focus solely on behavior therapy, Cortica offers a holistic, multidisciplinary model of care. Our team includes experts from a wide range of fields—occupational therapy, speech pathology, pediatrics, and more—allowing us to address the whole child and deliver more integrated, effective care.

• Focus on Collaboration: At Cortica, we don’t just implement therapy—we collaborate with families, caregivers, and other clinicians to create individualized care plans that empower everyone involved. This approach ensures that each child’s unique needs are met, and that the entire team is aligned in their goals for success.

• Quality Over Quantity: We take pride in value-based care partnerships with health plans that prioritize quality over quantity. Our patients benefit from the time we dedicate to collaborative, integrated care, and our clinicians are supported with more time for thoughtful clinical decision-making. Unlike other providers, we are reimbursed based on outcomes, not just the number of sessions delivered.

By joining Cortica, you’ll be part of a team that’s redefining ABA therapy—combining compassion, innovation, and collaboration to deliver results that matter.

Ready to make a difference? Apply today to learn more.

Cortica is an Equal Opportunity Employer. This posting is not intended to be an exhaustive list of duties. Please review the full job description here: Job Description.

jobs.description:
About NexHealth

Our healthcare system remains frustratingly analog. When you live in a world of one-tap car rides, instant meal delivery, and unlimited streaming, why do you still have to call to schedule a doctor’s appointment and fill out a clipboard in the waiting room?

NexHealth’s mission is to accelerate innovation in healthcare by connecting patients, providers, and developers. We’re building the infrastructure layer for modern healthcare, connecting thousands of fragmented, on-premise, and closed EHR systems into a single, modern platform that powers software, APIs, payments, and patient experiences across the ecosystem.

• Founded: 2017

• Headquarters: San Francisco, CA

• Funding: $177M Series C

• Employees: 200+

• Trusted by tens of thousands of providers and hundreds of health-tech developers — forging the infrastructure layer that modern healthcare needs

About the Role

As our Senior Accounting Manager, you’ll own the accuracy and speed of NexHealth’s books and reinvent how that work gets done. You’ll bring the discipline of a mature close and pair it with modern data and AI tooling, so that a fast, auditable close becomes the default rather than a monthly sprint. This role is a fit for an accountant who has run a strong close before and wants to build the next version of it.

What You’ll Do

• Own the month-end close end to end, including the calendar, owners, dependencies, and sign-off, and drive it toward a 4-business-day close

• Lead our offshore accounting team: set priorities, review their work, and hand off close tasks, reconciliations, and recurring accounting work with clear checklists and turnaround expectations

• Own the quality of GAAP financial statements across every account by setting review standards for flux analysis and balance sheet reconciliations

• Design and ship automation and AI agents for core accounting work, such as reconciliations, flux commentary, journal entry preparation, anomaly detection, and close tracking

• Own payroll accounting and operations in Rippling, including international hires through our employer of record partner, with accurate accruals, reconciliations, and strong payroll controls

• Partner on equity management in Carta, including grant and exercise processing, cap table reconciliation to the general ledger, and stock-based compensation

• Build financial and operational reporting and dashboards in Sigma that leadership uses to run the business

• Partner with Data Science to build and improve our finance data warehouse in Snowflake, so reconciliations, close checks, and reporting run on trusted, reconcilable data

• Lead audit readiness with our external auditors: build the schedules, keep workpapers current, and close auditor requests on time without a last-minute scramble

• Surface risks, control gaps, and process issues early, and document decisions so the team and the systems you build can scale

What You’ll Bring

• Strong experience running the month-end close at a scaling SaaS, payments, or technology company, with solid working knowledge of US GAAP, accruals, and multi-entity accounting

• An active CPA license

• Experience leading offshore or distributed accounting teams across time zones, including setting clear standards and reviewing work for quality

• A track record of building automation with LLMs or agentic workflow tools; you can walk us through something you built and the impact it had

• Strong grasp of internal controls, data completeness, and audit trail design, with processes built to hold up as transaction volume and complexity grow

• Strong SQL skills and hands-on experience with Snowflake or a similar data warehouse; you write your own queries rather than waiting on a data request

• Hands-on experience with NetSuite, plus payroll (Rippling or similar), spend management (Ramp or similar), BI (Sigma, Looker, or similar), and cap table (Carta or similar) platforms

• Comfort with technical accounting research, getting to the root of an issue and turning conclusions into practical policies and entries

• Sound judgment with imperfect data: you make the call, keep the close moving, then fix the underlying data so the issue doesn’t come back

• Clear communication with Data Science, Engineering, Revenue Operations, and Finance partners, adapting to technical and leadership audiences and documenting decisions so others can learn how things work

• A drive to rethink how corporate accounting works with LLMs and agentic workflows, paired with a willingness to take on the unglamorous problems that make the business run better

Bonus Points For

• Big 4 or other public accounting experience

• Experience at a fast-growing SaaS business through multiple stages of scale

• Experience with payroll accounting for international teams through an employer of record

Compensation

Actual salaries will vary depending on factors including but not limited to location, experience, and performance. The range listed is just the base salary component of NexHealth’s total compensation package for employees. Other benefits may include stock options, an unlimited paid time off policy, and up to 100% coverage on medical, vision and dental insurance.

NexHealth Compensation Range

$112,000—$150,000 USD

Benefits

• Full Medical, Dental, and Vision (up to 100% covered)

• 401K and commuter benefits

• Flexible PTO

• High-impact work that directly improves the healthcare experience for millions

Our Values

• Solve the customer’s problems, not yours When making decisions, think from the perspective of the customer. It’s easy to make decisions that make our lives simpler, but not the customers.

• Do the things others are not willing to do As a Nexer, always go after the hardest problems. Pursue things at the highest quality. Move at the fastest pace.

• Take ownership Act like a founder. Own your roles, destinies, mistakes, behavior, and our mission. The buck stops with each of us - no blaming or excuses.

• Say what’s on your mind, with positive intent Be direct, proactive, transparent, and frequent in your communication.

• Default trust As a Nexer, you do not have to earn trust, trust is given to you by default. If we by default trust each other, our speed of communication, feedback, information sharing, and overall improvements will be a lot faster.

• Think in first principles We first identify the problem and then break it down to its fundamentals before diving into solutions. We constantly ask “why” to validate our assumptions.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We provide reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities to participate in the application or interview process. Contact talent@nexhealth.com to request assistance.
