jobs.description:
Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

Director/Client Partner - Google, Enterprise AI

Remote – United States

Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

Scope of the Role

The race to production AI is creating unprecedented demand for trusted partners who can help enterprises deploy, scale, and operationalize AI solutions. As one of the world's most influential technology companies, Google sits at the center of that transformation. Innodata is investing heavily in expanding our strategic relationship with Google, and we are seeking a Director / Client Partner to lead that growth. This is a senior, high-impact account leadership position focused on expanding and deepening Innodata's relationship across Google's AI, Cloud, Data, Product, Engineering, and Operations organizations. You will own the account strategy, executive relationships, revenue growth, and commercial success of one of Innodata's most important strategic accounts. Success in this role requires a unique combination of executive presence, consultative selling, account expansion expertise, and a deep understanding of AI, data engineering, cloud, and digital transformation services. You will partner closely with Google's stakeholders as well as Innodata's solution architects, delivery leaders, and AI experts to identify opportunities, shape solutions, and drive meaningful business outcomes. Your goal will be to expand Innodata's Enterprise AI footprint across Google, transform existing relationships into larger strategic engagements, and identify new production AI workloads that create long-term value for both organizations.

What You'll Own:

• Own the overall Google Enterprise AI account strategy, growth plan, pipeline, bookings, forecasting, and revenue performance.

• Develop and execute account expansion strategies that uncover new opportunities across Google's AI, Cloud, Data, Product, Engineering, Operations, and Trust & Safety organizations.

• Build and maintain executive-level relationships with key stakeholders across the Google ecosystem.

• Identify, qualify, and close complex professional services and AI transformation engagements valued at $2M+ while contributing to long-term account growth.

• Drive expansion into new production AI initiatives, including Generative AI, Agentic AI, AI evaluation, data engineering, analytics, and managed AI services.

• Collaborate with solution architects, data scientists, engineering leaders, and delivery teams to design workshops, pilots, proofs of concept, and production-scale programs.

• Position and cross-sell Innodata's capabilities across AI-powered data engineering, GenAI application development, GenBI, RAG and context engineering, AI evaluation, HITL workflows, and managed production support.

• Lead commercial negotiations, proposal development, opportunity qualification, and contract discussions with senior stakeholders.

• Build a multi-threaded account presence across technical, business, procurement, and executive teams to accelerate growth and strengthen strategic partnerships.

• Serve as the voice of the customer internally, helping shape Innodata's Enterprise AI offerings and long-term go-to-market strategy.

You'll Thrive in This Role If You Have:

• 10+ years of experience in enterprise technology, AI, data engineering, cloud, analytics, software engineering services, or digital transformation sales and account management.

• 5+ years of experience managing and growing large strategic technology accounts, ideally within major technology companies or hyperscaler environments.

• A demonstrated track record of growing accounts to $5M-$10M+ in annual revenue and closing complex services engagements exceeding $2M.

• Experience selling AI, data engineering, analytics, cloud, digital transformation, or managed services solutions.

• Strong executive presence and the ability to engage senior leaders across business and technical organizations.

• Expertise in account planning, opportunity qualification, forecasting, and complex commercial negotiations.

• The ability to navigate multiple stakeholder groups including Engineering, Product, AI/ML, Data, Operations, Procurement, and executive leadership.

• A Bachelor's degree is required; an MBA or Master's degree is preferred.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Existing relationships within Google across Cloud, AI/ML, Data Engineering, Product, Operations, Analytics, or Procurement teams.

• Prior experience selling AI, engineering, consulting, or managed services directly into Google.

• Working knowledge of Google Cloud technologies including Vertex AI, Gemini, BigQuery, Looker, and broader Google Cloud Data & AI solutions.

• Experience with Agentic AI, Generative AI, AI evaluation frameworks, data engineering programs, or managed AI operations.

• Familiarity with Google's procurement processes, vendor ecosystem, and partner landscape.

• Experience converting existing delivery engagements into larger transformation programs and recurring managed-services revenue streams

jobs.title: Scientist II, Drug Product Design & Development
jobs.description:
The Drug Product Design and Development (DPDD) group within AbbVie’s Synthetic Molecule CMC organization designs and develops drug products that enable the delivery of candidate synthetic molecules across clinical development, from proof-of-concept and pivotal studies through life-cycle innovation. DPDD collaborates with cross-functional teams to establish integrated, phase-appropriate drug product development strategies; design and execute studies that deliver bioavailable, stable, and manufacturable drug products; and ensure the timely delivery of clinical supplies. The group also optimizes formulations and manufacturing processes to produce commercially viable drug products for late stage clinical studies that meet patient needs, and support the consistent manufacture of high-quality products.

AbbVie’s DPDD organization is seeking a highly motivated, talented Scientist II with experience in developing drug products to join our team in North Chicago, IL. The successful candidate will partner with project leads and cross-functional teams to develop drug delivery and formulation strategies; design, characterize, and build understanding of formulations and processes; and advance the biopharmaceutical characterization of clinical formulations. In this role, the candidate will serve as an integral member of the drug product team, executing activities that support formulation design and drug product process development. The candidate is also expected to foster productive collaborations and communicate effectively with scientific teams and cross-functional stakeholders.

Responsibilities

• Plans and executes formulation feasibility, optimization, and supporting studies for project goals. Continuously seeks to improve existing formulation techniques and processes.
• Demonstrate strong proficiency in analytical techniques for physicochemical characterization of drug substances and drug products, including HPLC, X-ray diffraction, particle size distribution (PSD) analysis, and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC).
• Innovates and implements new experimental protocols based on good scientific understanding and acts as a resource for others.
• Interprets data in the framework of the project and modifies experimental plans when required.
• Applies theoretical framework to solve moderately complex formulation and development problems.
• Makes scientific contributions to development reports, technical summaries, and supporting documents.
• Communicates formulation recommendations clearly in a scientifically sound in a project team meeting setting.
• Collaborates across CMC functions to advance project execution.
• Executes biopharmaceutics related assays for guiding the formulation selection and derisking of clinical products, including oral dosage forms and long-acting injectables.
• Interface with drug product development teams to ensure that biopharmaceutical and physicochemical considerations are incorporated into formulation design.
• Collaborate with other functions within AbbVie to align a broad range of strategies that directly support drug discovery and development programs.
• Ensure compliance with AbbVie safety, good laboratory practices, quality and regulatory policies and government regulations.

• BS or equivalent education with typically 7 or more years of experience or MS or equivalent education with typically 5 or more years of experience, preferably in Pharmaceutics, Chemistry, Physical Pharmacy, Biopharmaceutical Sciences, Material Sciences, Biomedical Engineering, or Chemical Engineering.

jobs.title: Lead Battery Disassembly Technician
jobs.description:
About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.

Supervisor Responsibility:

This role provides technical guidance, training, and mentorship to Battery Disassembly Technicians on the floor. It does not have hiring, firing, or performance review authority; it is an individual contributor position, not a people-management role.

Position Summary:

Redwood Materials is seeking a Lead Battery Disassembly Technician to perform the full scope of safe, efficient, and high-quality disassembly of EV battery packs and modules within a high-volume manufacturing environment, while serving as the floor-level subject matter expert and trainer for the team. The position requires strict adherence to high-voltage safety protocols, standardized work instructions, and continuous process improvement, and is responsible for training and mentoring technicians, verifying the quality and safety of completed work, and escalating non-routine issues to Supervision and Engineering. The Lead also monitors day-to-day compliance with floor conduct standards — including break/lunch adherence and personal device use — and serves as the floor-level point of contact for operational questions when Supervision or Management is offsite, escalating any issue outside established procedure. This is an individual contributor role that does not carry formal hiring, firing, or performance management authority.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Leadership, Training & Mentorship:

• Serve as the floor-level subject matter expert on disassembly procedures, high-voltage safety, LOTO, and rigging/lifting operations. Train, mentor, and onboard new and existing technicians on standardized work instructions, safety protocols, and proper use of tools and material handling equipment. Verify the quality, safety, and completeness of teammates' disassembly and rigging work, and coach corrective action where gaps are identified. Monitors adherence to floor conduct standards (behavioral etiquette, break/lunch scheduling, personal device use) and escalates repeated or serious violations to Supervision. Acts as the floor-level point of contact for routine operational questions when Supervision or Management is offsite, escalating decisions outside standard procedure.

EV Battery Pack & Module Disassembly:

• Perform controlled disassembly of EV and stationary storage battery packs, modules, and subcomponents in accordance with established work instructions and safety procedures. Safely isolate, and when deemed necessary, de-energize and verify absence of voltage prior to handling high-voltage systems. Disassemble battery systems down to module and component level, including removal of BMS components, wiring harnesses, busbars, cooling systems, and structural elements. Identify, sort, and route components for reuse, recycling, or disposal in alignment with production and environmental standards. Handle lithium-ion battery materials, including damaged or degraded units, using approved containment and safety methods. Serve as the escalation point for non-routine or first-time disassembly scenarios, providing hands-on guidance to less experienced technicians.

High Voltage Safety & Material Handling:

• Strictly follow all high-voltage safety protocols, lockout/tagout (LOTO), and PPE requirements when working with energized or potentially energized systems. Utilize appropriate insulated tools and electrical testing equipment (e.g., multimeters) to verify system status. Safely transport and store battery packs, modules, and hazardous materials using approved material handling equipment. Respond to thermal, electrical, or chemical hazards in accordance with emergency procedures and EHS guidelines. Must meet all requirements for use of a full-face respirator, including medical clearance and fit testing, in accordance with OSHA and company standards. Audit teammates’ adherence to high-voltage safety protocols, LOTO, and PPE requirements, and coach corrective action on any gaps.

Production Operations & Process Flow

• Execute standardized work in a high-throughput production environment, meeting or exceeding daily and hourly disassembly targets. Maintain workflow efficiency by adhering to takt time, minimizing bottlenecks, and supporting continuous flow operations. Track and document production output, material disposition, and process data accurately within required systems (e.g., Excel, in house tracking). Identify process inefficiencies and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives to optimize safety, quality, and throughput. Lead root-cause discussions on throughput, quality, or safety misses and drive corrective actions with supervision and Engineering.

Tooling & Technical Skills:

• Utilize a range of hand tools, power tools, and electrical diagnostic equipment in a safe and effective manner. Demonstrate working knowledge of mechanical fastening systems, electrical connections, and component-level disassembly techniques. Perform basic electrical verification and troubleshooting as needed during disassembly operations. Maintain tools and equipment in proper working conditions and report any deficiencies. Train technicians on proper tool use, mechanical fastening systems, electrical diagnostic equipment, and component-level disassembly techniques.

Cross-Functional Support & Field Operations:

• Collaborate with Manufacturing, Engineering, EHS, and Maintenance teams to improve disassembly processes and safety controls. Support field operations as required (up to 10% travel) for battery system decommissioning, including on-site disassembly and material recovery. Work with internal and external teams to safely process large-scale energy storage systems in non-production environments. Act as the team’s primary point of contact for Manufacturing, Engineering, EHS, and Maintenance on process and safety improvements, and represent the technician team in cross-functional planning.

Rigging, Lifting & Heavy Material Handling:

• Perform rigging and controlled lifting of large-format EV battery packs and energy storage systems using approved lifting devices and techniques. Operate a variety of material handling equipment, including forklifts (sit-down, stand-up, pallet jacks), hoists, cranes, and other lifting apparatus to safely move high-voltage assemblies. Inspect rigging equipment (slings, chains, shackles, lifting fixtures) prior to use and ensure compliance with established safety standards and load ratings. Execute lifts in accordance with defined rigging plans, center-of-gravity considerations, and facility safety procedures to prevent load shift or damage. Coordinate with team members during lifts to ensure safe positioning, communication, and control of suspended loads. Prior rigging and heavy material handling experience is strongly preferred; however, training and certification will be provided for candidates with foundational mechanical aptitude. Review and sign off on rigging plans and lift execution for complex or high-risk lifts, and certify newly trained technicians on rigging fundamentals.

General Manufacturing Expectations:

• Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment in alignment with 5S standards. Perform repetitive physical tasks, including lifting 30–50 lbs and standing for extended periods (up to 12-hour shifts). Operate material handling equipment and mechanical lifts (training provided). Adapt to dynamic work conditions, including indoor and outdoor environments and varying temperatures. Ensure shift readiness through proper workstation setup, organization, and handoff communication. Model shift-readiness and 5S standards for the team, and coach less experienced technicians on workstation organization and handoff communication.

Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities:

• 4-6 years of battery disassembly or related high-voltage/mechanical experience, with demonstrated proficiency across all disassembly work instructions.

• Demonstrated ability to train, coach, and explain technical procedures to technicians at varying skill levels.

• Requirements to participate high voltage training and certifications.

• Operate a variety of material handling equipment and mechanical lifts (training provided).

• Perform repetitive lifting (30-50lbs) and support ergonomic and 5S improvement initiatives.

• Ensure shift readiness by preparing and organizing workstations for incoming teams.

• Thrive in dynamic environments, including outdoor and variable-temperature conditions.

• Ability to travel up to 10% of the time to support field decommissioning work, including guiding technicians through unfamiliar, on-site scenarios.

• Strong communication skills for shift handoffs, cross-functional coordination, and technical escalation to supervision and Engineering.

• Stand and perform physical tasks for the majority of a 12-hour shift in both indoor and outdoor environments.

The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.

We collect your PI for our purposes, including performing services and operations related to your potential employment. If you have additional privacy-related questions, please contact us at privacy@redwoodmaterials.com.

jobs.title: Revenue Operations Support Analyst
jobs.description:
ABOUT KOJO

It's time to build. Whether it's creating more housing, upgrading our infrastructure, or adapting to climate change, one thing is clear: the construction industry is at the center of solving our biggest problems. We’re making buildings cheaper and easier to build by transforming the way commercial construction companies buy their materials. Join us.

Founded in 2018, Kojo is now one of the fastest-growing construction technology companies in the world. Construction accounts for $10 trillion in global spend annually and we can’t live without its output - our roads, schools, hospitals, and offices. Despite this, there’s been very little innovation over the past 70 years in how materials - which constitute up to 40% of project costs - are bought and sold. This is our opportunity.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Kojo's Sales and Customer Success teams run on Salesforce, and when something in that world needs a hand — a quote that has to be built by hand, an account that needs to move, a duplicate that needs merging, a report that doesn't add up — the request lands in one queue. You'll be the first person to pick it up.

The most important part of the job is custom quotes. Most agreements go out on a standard template a rep can send alone. The ones that don't — a mid-term expansion co-termed to an existing subscription, a split payment schedule, a multi-year deal paid upfront, a contract that has to list every module with its own dates and price, an amendment to something already signed — come to you. You'll get the opportunity and quote right, generate the order form, edit it where the template can't, and get it out through DocuSign, quickly and correctly.

Around that core you'll work the rest of the RevOps queue: account ownership and routing changes, duplicate merges, small Salesforce fixes, data questions, and tool questions. You'll report to the Revenue Operations Coordinator, and the two of you will run the queue together — you resolving what can be resolved directly, escalating what needs deeper Salesforce work, and both of you turning the patterns you see into fixes so the same request stops coming back.

Commercial decisions — pricing, discounts, non-standard terms — belong to the go-to-market organization, Sales and Customer Success. Your role is to make sure what they've agreed is captured accurately, approved where it needs to be, and reflected exactly in what the customer signs and in Salesforce afterwards.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Efficiently shipping custom quotes and order forms. This is the most important part of your role. Take a rep's request — a co-term with a prorated amount, a custom payment schedule, a one-time fee on a multi-year term, a multi-entity or module-level contract, an entity or start-date change, a rider or addendum, a credit — and turn it into a correct opportunity, quote, order form and DocuSign envelope. Same day where the deal needs it. Work with the RevOps Coordinate to iterate SFDC and DocuSign to accelerate our ability to ship an accurate quote. You ensure the GTM team is focused on the customer and not the critical CRM data we need to onboard, recognize revenue, and bill customer accurately.

 - Quotes and DocuSign when they misbehave. Diagnose why a generated agreement came out wrong — quote not syncing, billing or shipping details missing, products missing or duplicated, a price not reading through, no signature field, a Closed Won that won't save — work with the revenue operations coordinator to identify how SFDC should be updated, and / or show the rep how to avoid it next time.

 - The approval layer. Understand Kojo’s deal policies and how they show up in the SFDC deal flow. Keep approval status accurate, and confirm the right approvals are in place before an envelope goes out.

 - The rest of the queue. Account ownership and routing changes, inbound credits, duplicate account and contact merges, picklist and field tweaks, user access issues, renewal record discrepancies, cancellation processing, and answering questions about RevOps-owned tools, and knowing which tools are not owned by RevOps and routing the question to the owner of that tool. Triage fast, resolve what you can, escalate cleanly, and keep the requester informed.

 - The record after signature. Make sure term dates, amounts, products, and credits in Salesforce match the signed agreement to the day, that the renewal opportunities that should exist do exist, and that cancellations and amendments leave clean data behind.

 - Making requests disappear. Spot the recurring patterns in the queue and create business requirements to reduce the incidence of the recurring pattern in the future. Work with the Coordinator who will perform the configuration and development work to turn those business requirements into a template fix, a field, a validation rule, a small flow, or a how-to that lets reps self-serve.


ABOUT YOU


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 - Revenue operations or deal desk experience: 2+ years at a B2B SaaS company in a seat where quotes, orders, or Salesforce requests came to you — deal desk, sales operations, revenue operations, order management, or Salesforce support.

 - Hands-on in Salesforce: you're fluent in the Opportunity → Quote → Product data model, comfortable with reports, list views, and bulk updates, and you've made real configuration changes — fields, picklists, validation rules, page layouts, simple flows — in an org other people depended on. Salesforce Administrator certification, or experience that clearly stands in for it.

 - DocuSign beyond the send button: templates, merge fields and tabs, routing, reminders and expiry. Experience with DocuSign for Salesforce or Gen for Salesforce is a strong advantage.

 - Contract math as a reflex: prorations, co-terms, day counts, split payment schedules, multi-year totals — and the habit of stating your convention before your number.

 - Precision with documents: you can edit an order form in Word so the language, table, and totals are exactly right, and you notice when they aren't.

 - Precise written English: you'll write to reps, CSMs, and customers all day. Spoken English sufficient for a daily working session with the team.

 - A queue temperament: organized, quick to acknowledge, quick to close the loop, and able to tell a rep at quarter-end that a document isn't ready yet — with the reason and the fastest path forward.

 - Based in Latin America, with at least four hours of daily overlap with US Central time and flexibility in the final week of each quarter.


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Admin exposure to the GTM tools around Salesforce — Chili Piper, Outreach, ZoomInfo, Gong.

 - Exposure to how a signed contract becomes an invoice (Stripe or another billing platform).

 - A recurring manual request you turned into a template, automation, or how-to — and what it removed.

 - Experience supporting construction, manufacturing, or another industrial market.


WHAT YOU CARE ABOUT

 - Accountability: when an order form goes out wrong or a record doesn't match the paper, you treat it as yours to fix — and then you fix the reason it happened.

 - Impact: you sequence the queue by what unblocks a deal and what protects a customer relationship, not by what arrived first.

 - Intentional Communication: you write with the right context and no ambiguity — to a rep who's stuck, a CSM mid-renewal, or a customer reading an order form.

 - Collaboration: you check with the rep, the CSM, and the Coordinator before you build, so the contract that goes out is the one everyone thinks went out.


WORKING AT KOJO

Salary: Your salary will be dependent upon many factors, including your experience level, skillset, market dynamics and balancing internal equity relative to other Kojo employees. The compensation and benefits information that we provide is based on Kojo’s good-faith estimate as of the date of the job posting and may be modified in the future.

Benefits: This position is also eligible for a new hire equity grant and all US-based full time employees are eligible for our full suite of perks and benefits. For more information about our perks and benefits, check out https://www.usekojo.com/careers https://usekojo.com/careers.

Location: Kojo’s team members work from home 100% of the time across North and South America. If applicable, we’ll identify the travel and/or location-specific requirements of a position in the text above. Otherwise, team members can expect to work business hours congruent with their local time zone and remotely.

Inclusive Workplace: Kojo values diverse perspectives and is committed to building an inclusive workplace. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and do not discriminate on the basis of sex, race, color, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, citizenship, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We strongly encourage people from underrepresented groups to apply.



Scam Notice: Please be aware that there are individuals and organizations that may attempt to scam job seekers by offering fraudulent employment opportunities in the name of Kojo. These scams may involve fake job postings, unsolicited emails, or messages claiming to be from our recruiters or hiring managers. Kojo will never ask for any personal account information, such credit card details or bank account numbers, during the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Don't See Your Role? Let's Connect.
jobs.description:
Terra AI is building a new category at the intersection of artificial intelligence, geoscience, and critical resource development.

As global demand for copper, lithium, nickel, rare earth elements, geothermal energy, and other strategic resources accelerates, the mining and subsurface industries face a growing challenge: traditional exploration methods remain slow, expensive, and highly uncertain. Terra AI was founded to help solve this problem by redefining how critical resources are discovered, evaluated, and developed.

By combining advanced machine learning, probabilistic modeling, and deep geoscience expertise, Terra AI helps exploration and mining companies make faster, more informed subsurface decisions with greater confidence and capital efficiency. The company’s platform integrates geological, geophysical, and drilling data into intelligent systems designed to improve targeting accuracy, accelerate discovery timelines, and reduce exploration risk.

Backed by leading investors including Khosla Ventures and working alongside strategic industry partners including Rio Tinto, Ero Copper, and Ramaco Resources, Terra AI is emerging as one of the more closely watched AI-native companies operating within the mining and critical minerals sector.

Terra AI’s mission is to define the new global standard for data-driven critical resource development — breaking the cost and time curve required to support electrification, energy security, and the global energy transition.

The company operates with a strong partnership mentality, combining technical rigor, candid communication, continual learning, and environmental stewardship to help modern exploration teams solve some of the world’s most important resource challenges.

Terra AI | General Interest Application


GREAT PEOPLE DON'T ALWAYS FIT NEATLY INTO A JOB DESCRIPTION.

At Terra AI, we're building something ambitious: using artificial intelligence and geoscience to transform how we understand the Earth's subsurface and discover the resources that power our world.

We're bringing together people with different backgrounds, experiences, and ways of thinking to tackle challenges that have traditionally been difficult, expensive, and uncertain.

And while we may not have the perfect opening for you today, that doesn't mean we shouldn't get to know each other.


WHO WE'D LOVE TO HEAR FROM

We're always interested in connecting with curious, talented people who are excited about solving meaningful problems.

Our work brings together expertise across:

 - Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning — Developing novel models and applying AI to complex physical systems.

 - Software Engineering & Product — Building the technology, platforms, and experiences that bring our work to life.

 - Geoscience & Earth Sciences — Combining scientific expertise with new approaches to understanding the subsurface.

 - Project Management & Operations — Turning ambitious ideas into successful, real-world execution.

 - Commercial, Strategy & Investments — Building partnerships, developing opportunities, and helping translate technological innovation into lasting value.

 - Business Operations & Corporate Functions — Creating the infrastructure that allows a growing company to do extraordinary work.

Don't see your background represented? That's perfectly fine. Some of the most interesting contributions come from people whose experiences don't fit neatly into a predefined category.


WHAT MAKES SOMEONE A GREAT FIT AT TERRA AI?

We value people who are intellectually curious, collaborative, comfortable challenging assumptions, and willing to roll up their sleeves.

We're building a company where good ideas matter, thoughtful debate is encouraged, and people have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

You don't need to check every box or have worked in our industry before. We care about what you've accomplished, how you approach problems, and what you're excited to build next.


LET'S STAY CONNECTED.

If Terra AI sounds like a place where you'd enjoy doing your best work, we'd love to hear from you.

Tell us a little about yourself, what interests you about Terra, and where you think you could make an impact.

A quick note: This is a general interest application, not an active opening for a specific position. While we may not be able to connect with everyone individually, we'll keep your information on file for consideration as relevant opportunities emerge.

Thank you for taking the time to introduce yourself. We appreciate your interest in being part of what we're building.


EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Terra AI is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to an inclusive, respectful workplace.

jobs.title: Senior Associate, Corporate Security
jobs.description:
About the Company

Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all — bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Real Estate and Corporate Security

In the emerging industry of digital assets, there is nothing more important than trust (which is why Gemini’s very first hires were Security experts). The Gemini Security team forms the backbone of all that we do and is as diverse as the number of challenges we tackle in the crypto space. From intelligence and investigations, to physical security technology, to securing cold storage systems and data centers to travel security and new office openings, enterprise risk security, and litigation support, security at Gemini ensures that our customers, clients, and employees are safe, secure, and supported.

The Role: Senior Associate, Corporate Security

Gemini seeks a highly skilled Senior Associate to join our Real Estate and Corporate Security team, dedicated to ensuring the safety and security of our employees, physical locations, assets, and brand reputation at our 24/7 Operations & Support Center in Arizona. Ideal candidates are seasoned security professionals with a strong background in law enforcement, exceptional customer service skills, and advanced expertise in technology and hospitality to protect personnel, sensitive information, and facilities. The Senior Associate will oversee on-site security operations, supervise contract guard staff, and maintain a safe, compliant workplace while serving as a front-line security presence and a representative of Gemini’s culture, balancing firm policy enforcement with professionalism and hospitality. Exceptional communication skills, adaptability, and a commitment to listening, learning, and problem-solving in response to shifting priorities and challenges are essential. Our office is currently in Tempe, AZ with a planned transition very soon to our Scottsdale, AZ office upon its opening. Join Gemini to contribute to a secure, welcoming environment while upholding our values of integrity and service excellence.

This role is required to be in person five days per week at our Scottsdale, AZ office.

Responsibilities:

General

• Employee and Visitor Safety: Oversee the security of the Operations & Support Center by monitoring entry points, verifying and maintaining employee credentials, and conducting thorough check-in and screening processes for all visitors to ensure a safe workplace.

• On-Site Presence: Maintain a consistent on-site presence five days per week during standard daytime hours, with flexibility to work after-hours or weekend shifts as needed to support the Center’s 24/7 operations, with appropriate compensation provided.

• Policy Enforcement: Uphold physical security standards, including the Center’s clean desk policy and electronic device restrictions, to safeguard sensitive customer and company data.

• Primary Security Liaison: Serve as the primary point of contact for all physical security matters within the Center, addressing concerns promptly and professionally.

• Security Patrols: Conduct routine and ad-hoc security patrols to ensure compliance with physical and procedural safeguards, identifying and mitigating potential risks.

• System Operations: Manage and monitor CCTV and Access Control systems, ensuring proper functionality, timely response to incidents, and accurate logging of all security events.

• Global Security Culture: Contribute to the development of Gemini’s global security culture by collaborating with the Corporate Security team to refine strategies, policies, and best practices, fostering a cohesive approach to security across the organization.

• Professional Development: Participate in regular training to enhance security-related skills and stay current on industry best practices.

• Decision-Making: Exercise sound judgment and demonstrate an appropriate sense of urgency in addressing security matters, ensuring effective and timely resolutions.

• Additional Duties: Perform other responsibilities as assigned by the Head of Real Estate and Security Operations or the Associate Director, Corporate Security, supporting the broader objectives of the team.

Guardforce Management

• Manage the 24/7 security guard team assigned to the Arizona Operations & Support Center.

• Coordinate directly with the third-party guard vendor to adjust staffing, update post orders, and ensure coverage and quality control.

• Train and mentor contracted guards to maintain consistent professional standards and response protocols.

• Oversee shift briefings, incident reporting, and escalation processes. Provide incident and activity reports to the Associate Director, Corporate Security.

Credentialing & Visitor Management

• Manage the credentialing process for all personnel working at the facility to ensure proper badge issuance, retrieval, and deactivation in compliance with company policy.

• Facilitate the screening of contractors and visitors and verify identification, validate authorization, and maintain accurate logs of all entries and exits.

• Coordinate closely with People Operations and the Arizona Office Services Associate for new hire onboarding validation and security orientation.

Health, Safety & Emergency Preparedness

• Maintain and enforce compliance with OSHA and corporate Health & Safety requirements for the Operations & Support Center.

• Support emergency response, evacuation, and crisis management efforts as part of the Physical Security Operations team.

• Ensure readiness for fire, medical, and active threat scenarios through preparedness checks and periodic training.

Cross-Functional & Administrative Support

• Collaborate daily with the Arizona Office Services Associate to support office operations such as mailroom duties, office event setup, and logistics coordination.

• Support internal Gemini training sessions or security briefings across Arizona, California, or Washington offices as needed.

• Travel up to 10% of the time as needed.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Experience in physical security, federal or local law enforcement, military police, or corrections.

• Demonstrated experience in supervising guardforces or small security teams.

• Strong technical aptitude, and experience with CCTV, access control, and alarm monitoring systems, visitor management systems, and security hardware integration.

• Proven capability to conduct investigations and situational assessments.

• Be eligible to obtain a current Arizona license to carry a weapon.

• Knowledge of OSHA, Health & Safety, and Emergency Management protocols.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a balance of firmness and diplomacy.

• Experience in policy enforcement, investigative work, or compliance monitoring in a corporate setting. Ability to tactfully enforce policies while maintaining a professional and approachable demeanor.

• Strong writing skills for clear, accurate reporting and incident documentation.

• Adherence to strict privacy/confidentiality guidelines and policies.

• Ability to work independently, adapt to various work environments, and maintain a high level of situational awareness.

• Ability to learn and use new software platforms.

• Remain flexible and responsive to changing conditions.

• Ability to remain calm in a crisis.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Previous experience working within a corporate or financial services environment.

• Preferred possession of HR218 as a former law enforcement officer.

• Certifications such as ASIS PSP (Physical Security Professional) or CPP (Certified Protection Professional, though not required.

• Understanding of data protection and privacy best practices related to physical environments.

It Pays to Work Here

The compensation & benefits package for this role includes:

• Competitive starting pay

• A discretionary annual bonus

• Long-term incentive in the form of a new hire equity grant

• Comprehensive health plans

• 401K with company matching

• Paid Parental Leave

• Flexible time off

At Gemini, we strive to build diverse teams that reflect the people we want to empower through our products, and we are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. Equal Opportunity is the Law, and Gemini is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. If you have a specific need that requires accommodation, please let a member of the People Team know.

jobs.title: Float Phlebotomist / Administrative Assistant (Fenway)
jobs.description:
About Us

One Medical is a primary care solution challenging the industry status quo by making quality care more affordable, accessible and enjoyable. But this isn’t your average doctor’s office. We’re on a mission to transform healthcare, which means improving the experience for everyone involved - from patients and providers to employers and health networks. Our seamless in-office and 24/7 virtual care services, on-site labs, and programs for preventive care, chronic care management, common illnesses and mental health concerns have been delighting people for the past fifteen years.

In February 2023 we marked a milestone when One Medical joined Amazon. Together, we look to deliver exceptional health care to more consumers, employers, care team members, and health networks to achieve better health outcomes. As we continue to grow and seek to impact more lives, we’re building a diverse, driven and empathetic team, while working hard to cultivate an environment where everyone can thrive.

The Opportunity

As a Float Medical Assistant (internally called Lab Services Specialist/ Member Support Specialist) at One Medical, you’ll provide an exceptional experience for our patients and help them accomplish an important part of their care journey by providing venipuncture as well as other clinical support services. You will be an ambassador for patients, with a mastery of human connection and a strong drive for service. You will remove barriers to care, resulting in a truly exceptional in-office patient experience. You are the steward of the space and ensure the look and feel of the office lobby are on brand with the One Medical experience. You will be the first point of contact for our patients, as well as provide any other support as requested by the Practice Coordinators, Operations Manager, or providers.  Our Flex Lab Services Specialist/Member Support Specialist support multiple offices in a Market.

You are a strong team player and use your innovative problem solving skills to tackle various tasks and challenges. You combine excellent specimen collection technique with tactful interpersonal skills during every interaction with your patients, at both the front desk and in the lab. You have a strong grasp of verbal and written communication. You are able to identify opportunities and deliver on customer-centric solutions while using empathy, focus, and compassion in all interactions with patients and teammates. You bring self-awareness to your daily work to utilize your strengths and develop your areas of opportunity. You thrive in cultures that focus on feedback and growth and are nimble in their approach to respond to the needs of the patients and team. You have an unwavering drive to help and serve others and create amazing moments for our members and teammates. If this sounds like you, we would love to connect.

What you’ll likely work on:

• Use impeccable C-I-CARE (a framework containing the key elements of a great interaction and effective communication that we use with patients and each other) in all patient interactions, both clinical and administrative, and ensure a fluid and positive in-office experience through patient intake, same day schedule management, appropriate follow up scheduling, strong knowledge of billing and insurance, monitoring patient feedback and assisting with outreach as necessary

• Provide best in class venipuncture services on a population ranging from pediatrics to geriatrics, depending on the office location

• Perform and assist with extended scope duties such as, but not limited to non-blood specimen collection, EKGs/ECGs, vitals, ear lavages, vaccines, PPD tests, and swabs

• Maintain high standards of in-office care through proper specimen labeling, handling and processing, inventory upkeep, and tool sterilization

• Continue to care for our members beyond the lab room by answering patient messages, following up on lab cases and assisting our providers and virtual medical team with clerical duties such as, but not limited to biometric screening forms, medical record and consult review, billing inquiries, and DOH reporting

• All front of house duties including check in/check out, insurance verification, printing/paperwork tasks, prepping tests, tasking to service level expectations etc

• Contribute to team development through rounding, attending team huddles, participating in team problem solving, supporting in office providers with ad hoc asks, etc.

• Perform opening and closing duties/daily office upkeep as required, including maintaining the look and feel of both patient and employee facing spaces, restocking supplies, and organization

• Master our technology suite including, but not limited to Slack, G-suite, Zoom, Circulation, RingCentral, and our Electronic Medical Record System, in order to interact with team members and complete daily work

These responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by personnel assigned to this job classification.  They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of job duties performed by personnel in this classification.  Other job related duties may be assigned by management.

What you’ll need:

• At least 6 months of relevant experience as a Medical Assistant or Phlebotomist outside of a training/externship environment

• Strong customer service skills, including ability to establish and maintain effective customer relationships and deliver customer-centric solutions

• Strong written and verbal communication skills

• Proficiency in computer technology such as typing, navigating the internet and using multiple software systems simultaneously

• Experience working on collaborative, diverse, multi-disciplinary teams (additional experience with remote teams a plus)

• A proven ability to display confidence and instill trust during the collection process while delivering individualized, human-centered, customer-focused care

• A proven track record of persisting through change, consistently stepping up to take action on challenges, and learning quickly and effectively when faced with new situations or task

One Medical is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices.

The range for this role is $25.75 to $27.75 per hour based on a standard full-time schedule. Total compensation packages may be based on factors unique to particular candidates, such as skill sets, depth of experience, and work location. The total compensation package for this position may also include benefits. For more information, visit https://www.onemedical.com/careers/

This is a full time role (40 hrs/week) with 8 hr shifts generally taking place Mon-Fri between 7:30a-6:30p based in our Fenway office location primarily and would provide support to South End, Kendall Square, Copley Square, and FiDi 53 State offices in Boston, MA.   Flex Lab Services Specialists/Member Support Specialists lend support to multiple One Medical locations in a market. Location and schedules are subject to change.

One Medical offers a robust benefits package designed to aid your health and wellness.  All regular team members working 24+ hours per week and their dependents are eligible for benefits starting on the team member's date of hire:

Taking care of you today

• Paid sabbatical for every five years of service

• Free One Medical memberships for yourself, your friends and family

• Employee Assistance Program - Free confidential services for team members who need help with stress, anxiety, financial planning, and legal issues

• Competitive Medical, Dental and Vision plans

• Pre-Tax commuter benefits

• PTO cash outs - Option to cash out up to 40 accrued hours per year

Protecting your future for you and your family

• 401K match

• Credit towards emergency childcare

• Company paid maternity and paternity leave

• Paid Life Insurance - One Medical pays 100% of the cost of Basic Life Insurance

• Disability insurance - One Medical pays 100% of the cost of Short Term and Long Term Disability Insurance

In addition to the comprehensive benefits package outlined above, practicing clinicians also receive

• Malpractice Insurance - Malpractice fees to insure your practice at One Medical is covered 100%.

• UpToDate Subscription - An evidence-based clinical research tool

• Continuing Medical Education (CME) - Receive an annual stipend for continuing medical education

• Rounds - Providers end patient care one hour early each week to participate in this shared learning experience

• Discounted rate to attend One Medical’s Annual REAL primary care conference

One Medical is an equal opportunity employer, and we encourage qualified applicants of every background, ability, and life experience to contact us about appropriate employment opportunities.

One Medical participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.  Please refer to the E-Verification Poster and Right to Work Poster for additional information.

Your work schedule could be subject to change based on business direction at any time.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Customer Operations
jobs.description:
Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.

More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.

We’re a high-growth fintech company changing the retirement industry. We are backed by a number of investors. This includes funding from Marshall Wace and Baillie Gifford, as well as top investors such as BlackRock, TPG (The Rise Fund), SoftBank, Glynn Capital, NewView Capital, USVP, Wing, Uncork, and more.

About the role

As a Senior Manager of Operations within Customer Success & Operations, you will lead a multi-team organization of Operations Managers responsible for the accurate, compliant, and timely execution of multiple money movement flows on behalf of our clients and their participants. Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Operations, you will translate high-level organizational strategy into actionable operational plans, driving a culture of continuous improvement, strict risk mitigation, and client-centric execution.

In this role, you will serve as a critical strategic link between frontline operations and cross-functional leadership—including Product, Engineering, Data, Legal, and Sales/Onboarding. You will mentor and develop direct-report managers, scale high-volume transaction operations, and leverage data-driven insights to elevate customer experiences while maintaining a lean operational footprint.

About the team

The CS Operations organization sits at the heart of Human Interest's mission to make retirement savings accessible. Our teams ensure high-value financial transactions for thousands of participants every day are handled seamlessly—ensuring every dollar lands in the right place, on time, and in full compliance with regulatory requirements. We operate in a highly regulated environment where errors carry real and substantial financial risk, so precision is non-negotiable. We maintain data integrity through rigorous review, quality control, and escalation protocols, and we collaborate closely with Customer Success, Engineering, Product, and Compliance to optimize workflows, surface operational insights, and continuously improve the customer experience. We partner tightly with peer teams across Operations to share best practices, understand shared challenges, and strengthen Operations as a whole.

What you get to do every day

• Coach & Develop Leaders: Directly manage, mentor, and build leadership bench strength across multiple Operations Managers. Establish high performance standards, hold leaders accountable to ambitious KPIs, and cultivate a robust pipeline of future operational talent.

• Drive Vision & Strategic Alignment: Translate company strategy into departmental goals across multiple money movement flows. Maintain a broad business perspective, ensuring team priorities align directly with company objectives and broader operational effectiveness.

• Operational Excellence & Performance Monitoring: Own high-level metrics for SLA adherence, quality, accuracy, and cycle times. Utilize data, capacity modeling, and optimization reports to continuously elevate throughput and set ambitious goals across teams.

• Cross-Functional Strategic Partnership: Build collaborative relationships with leaders in CS&O, Product, Data, Legal, and Sales. Act as an operational translator, channeling frontline customer insights to shape product roadmaps while seamlessly operationalizing technical and regulatory changes.

• Risk Management & Control Environment: Maintain a rigorous control environment across all transaction lifecycles. Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate operational risks to prevent financial loss and ensure full compliance in a highly regulated landscape.

• Client Experience & Root Cause Analysis: Foster a client-first mindset that looks beyond vanity metrics to evaluate true customer experience. Lead deep-dive root cause analyses on operational trends and complex escalations to implement long-term structural fixes.

• Process Optimization & Innovation: Drive a culture of innovation by identifying and scaling opportunities for workflow automation, process standardization, and system enhancements to maintain a lean operational footprint.

• Change Leadership & Transparent Communication: Lead teams through change with clarity and empathy. Maintain clear, concise, and solution-oriented reporting cadences with executive leadership and internal stakeholders.

• Other duties as assigned.

What you bring to the role

• Experience: 4+ years of operational management experience in financial services, fintech, retirement services (401k), or banking, with 2+ years specifically managing other People Managers/Leaders.

• Domain Expertise: Deep understanding of money movement processes, transaction lifecycles, and risk controls within a regulated environment.

• Leadership Development: Proven track record of developing direct-report managers, setting clear expectations, managing performance, and building high-performing operational teams.

• Data-Driven Decision Making: Demonstrated ability to leverage complex data reports, staffing models, and SLA metrics to drive strategy and prioritize trade-offs.

• Cross-Functional Influence: Exceptional ability to partner with cross-functional leadership (Product, Engineering, Legal, CS) to align on shared goals and advocate for operational priorities.

• Change & Process Management: Experience designing end-to-end operational improvements, scaling processes, and leading large teams through organizational change.

• Communication & Integrity: High ethical standards with outstanding written and verbal communication skills tailored for executive leadership.

Nice to have

• Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, or a related field.

• Direct experience with 401(k) recordkeeping systems, payroll integrations, or complex financial reconciliations.

• Formal certification in process improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) or continuous improvement frameworks.

• Experience in high-growth, fast-paced fintech environments.

Why you will love working at Human Interest

Human Interest is tackling one of our country's biggest challenges - closing the retirement gap. You'll be instrumental in architecting and scaling solutions that bring financial security to employees at small and medium-sized businesses nationwide. We’ve made significant progress, but there is still growth ahead, offering you a unique opportunity to solve complex problems, drive innovation, and advance your career alongside a dedicated, mission-driven team. We value hard work and recognize that our team's contributions are key to our continued success.

Join Human Interest and make a lasting impact by shaping the future of retirement.

Our operating principles define how we work together as a team. They reflect Human Interest’s unique view on what’s important and what’s right. Documenting this core aspect of our culture helps employees make good decisions on their own. It also helps candidates considering career opportunities critically evaluate whether they will thrive at Human Interest.

• Customer obsession: We're all about creating amazing experiences for our customers. We put their needs first and go the extra mile to make them smile.

• Long-Term Orientation: We're not just playing for today; we're building a legacy. We think big, plan strategically, and invest in our future.

• Autonomous and Accountable Teams: We trust our team members to take ownership and make smart decisions. We empower you to be your best self!

• An Escalating Bar for Talent and Performance: We're constantly raising the bar and challenging ourselves to be better. We believe in growth and continuous improvement.

• Fundamental Optimism: We see the glass as half full (and then we fill it up with more amazing ideas!). We believe in the power of positivity and the potential for greatness.

Compensation - At Human Interest, there are a number of factors that are used to determine the appropriate pay range for each position. We take into account the cost of labor for each position in various markets across the U.S. The base salary for this position spans $125,000 - $150,000 and represents the minimum in our lowest geographic region to a maximum in our highest geographic region. The salary we offer to a new employee within this range is based on their location within the U.S., their relevant job-related skills, and experience. At Human Interest, base salary is one component of the overall total rewards package. Depending on the position, additional compensation components such as bonuses, commissions, and equity may be offered. All of our employees are offered a robust suite of physical, financial, and mental wellness benefits. In compliance with applicable laws, we do not inquire about salary history, or about criminal history prior to a conditional offer of employment.

Benefits -

• A great 401(k) plan: Our own! Our 401(k) includes a dollar-for-dollar employer match up to 4% of compensation (immediately vested) and $0 plan fees

• Top-of-the-line health plans, as well as dental and vision insurance

• Competitive time off and parental leave

• Addition Wealth: Unlimited access to digital tools, financial professionals, and a knowledge center to help you understand your equity and support your financial wellness

• Lyra: Enhanced Mental Health Support for Employees and dependents

• Carrot: Fertility healthcare and family forming benefits

• Candidly: Student loan resource to help you and your family plan, borrow, and repay student debt

• Monthly work-from-home stipend; quarterly lifestyle stipend

• Engaging team-building experiences, ranging from virtual social events to team offsites, promoting collaboration and camaraderie.

We’re a great place to work (but don’t take our word for it)

Here’s a list of our awards and accolades:

• Certified as a Great Place To Work® (2023-2025)

• Fortune Best Place to Work in the Bay Area (2024)

• Best Places to Work by Built In (2023-2024)

• America’s Best Startup Employers by Forbes (2020-2022, 2024)

• A Top Company by Y Combinator (2020-2023)

• Inc. Fastest Growing Companies (2021)

Human Interest is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran or military status, pregnancy, or any other characteristics protected under federal, state, or local laws. Employment with Human Interest is at-will, meaning either you or the company may terminate employment at any time, with or without cause or notice, except as otherwise provided by law or written agreement.

We are committed to making every stage of our application process fully accessible to all individuals. If you need a reasonable accommodation at any point in the process, please let us know at applicantaccommodations@humaninterest.com.

Protect yourself against fraud and identity theft. Apply to our open positions directly via our careers page on Greenhouse. Human Interest will never ask applicants for their financial or banking information as part of our application process. All legitimate communication will come from a @humaninterest.com email address. If you have questions, please reach out to us directly at careers@humaninterest.com

Please note Human Interest does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from candidates. We will not consider resumes from vendors, including and without limitation search firms, staffing agencies, fee-based referral services, and recruiting agencies.

jobs.title: Human Resources Business Partner
jobs.description:
Overview

Our HR business partners are creative problem solvers, relationship builders, and strategic partners who understand the intricate dynamics of the teams they support. We're seeking a seasoned human resources professional to be an integral part of our team of recruiters and HR business partners who support efforts across multiple lines of our business. You will partner with business leadership to implement change, influence talent management, and increase division performance as well as improve the employee experience for colleagues. We’re looking for a driven individual who wants to add value, solve problems, and impact our company culture.

Esri has a Relocation Assistance Program and can provide support with relocating to the Redlands area for this position.

Responsibilities

• Drive results. Design and lead equitable and inclusive talent management, workforce planning, retention, and job and organizational design practices. Partner with talent acquisition to ensure delivery of a coordinated recruitment efforts that achieve workforce planning goals and builds diverse teams. Support full-cycle recruitment as needed, most frequently to fill high-priority, high-impact positions.

• Be an expert. Stay connected to the competitive landscape, including compensation and employment brand trends, and recommend strategic changes within the division. Serve as a consultative thought partner to leadership to align business needs with talent management objectives. Proactively manage and resolve employee relations and mitigate legal risk.

• Influence change. Provide expert guidance to business leaders on coaching, change management, and career development. Further define and implement strategic programs such as onboarding, career pathing, and leadership development to align the workforce and achieve company goals.

• Collaborate with stakeholders. Participate in and lead key meetings with business leaders and the HR team. Collaborate with business leaders to interpret business needs and identify talent priorities. Build strong partnerships with HR specialists in the areas of employee relations, organizational development and training, and compliance.

• Solve problems. Leverage your project management skills to identify opportunities and suggest creative solutions to improve results. Solicit and analyze employee feedback to identify opportunities for training, new skill acquisition, and advancement of workforce.

Requirements

• 2+ years of professional experience in a similar position or supporting similar HR generalist responsibilities

• Outstanding creativity, maturity, flexibility, and sound judgment in complex situations

• Demonstrated track record of building successful relationships and partnerships at all organizational levels

• Ability to work proactively and help build systemic processes and methods in all areas of human resources

• Excellent communication (written and verbal), interpersonal and leadership skills

• Proven conflict resolution and negotiation skills, with the ability to manage diverse perspectives and achieve consensus

• Ability to make data-driven decisions, leveraging analytics to inform business strategies and improve outcomes

• Knowledge of ADA, EEO, FMLA, Title VII, and wage and hour laws and benefits

• Bachelor’s degree in human resources, business, marketing, or communications

Recommended Qualifications

jobs.description:
As a Pharmacy Technician, you will help manage prescription preparation, accurate medication labeling, secure storage, and replenishment of pharmaceutical supplies within your authorized scope and applicable pharmacist supervision. Your work will also support the approved formulary, long-lead inventory planning, patient-facing pharmacy questions within scope, and documentation in the electronic health record.

The pharmacy function includes accountability for controlled substances and appropriate escalation of discrepancies, with responsibilities limited to what your authorization and supervision permit. Maintaining accurate stock records, following approved storage requirements, and communicating supply needs early are especially useful when medications have long replenishment lead times. Clinical questions remain with authorized prescribers or pharmacists. This separation between technical pharmacy support and clinical decision-making helps maintain accurate, safe medication services. Pharmacy quality controls support the same objective.

Employment Type: Full-time

Assignment Details: This position requires relocation to Diego Garcia, British Indian Ocean Territory, for the duration of the assignment.

Key Responsibilities

• Receive prescription and refill requests, verify completeness, and refer prescribing or clinical questions to an authorized pharmacist or clinician.
• Measure, count, package, and label medications under approved procedures while supporting accurate dispensing and professional patient service.
• Maintain formulary and pharmacy stock records, monitor secure storage, and coordinate long-lead pharmaceutical forecasting and replenishment.
• Protect patient records, document assigned pharmacy activity, and maintain required medication and controlled-substance inventory logs.
• Follow safe handling, applicable cold-chain, infection prevention, and medication accountability controls; immediately report suspected loss or diversion.
• Work with clinicians and logistics personnel to resolve pharmacy needs and escalate safety or compliance concerns through established processes.

You will help keep medication services organized and dependable while working within a clearly defined pharmacy support scope.

Requirements

• Current, unrestricted pharmacy technician license, professional registration, or other authorizing document issued by a recognized regulatory authority in the candidate's country or jurisdiction of licensure, permitting practice within the assigned scope; qualifications are subject to approval.
• Minimum of two (2) years of experience as a Pharmacy Technician or equivalent.

• Availability for established clinic hours, assigned on-call arrangements and emergency response requirements; ability to read, write, and speak English for effective communication.
• Ability to work seated or standing for prolonged periods, with bending, stooping, and lifting up to 15 lbs as required.

Preferred

About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary
The Materials Coordinator is responsible for overseeing material flow, inventory accuracy, receiving, warehousing, shipping, and logistics activities to support ongoing operations and project requirements. This role coordinates daily inbound and outbound deliveries, schedules transportation services, manages interstate shipments, and ensures materials are delivered to the right location at the right time. The ideal candidate has strong experience in material control, logistics coordination, inventory management, and transportation scheduling within a construction, industrial, or manufacturing environment.

Essential Job Responsibilities

• Coordinate and schedule daily inbound and outbound truck deliveries to support project and operational needs.

• Arrange, track, and monitor shipments to job sites, vendors, and locations throughout the United States.

• Serve as the primary point of contact with freight carriers, delivery services, vendors, and internal stakeholders regarding material deliveries.

• Prioritize and coordinate material movement based on project schedules and operational requirements.

• Monitor shipment status and proactively resolve transportation, delivery, and inventory issues.

• Receive, inspect, and verify incoming materials for accuracy and completeness.

• Maintain accurate inventory records and ensure material inventory levels support business needs.

• Coordinate material transfers between warehouses, shops, fabrication facilities, and project sites.

• Maintain shipping and receiving documentation including bills of lading, packing slips, freight records, and transfer documentation.

• Assist with cycle counts, physical inventories, and inventory audits.

• Ensure materials are properly staged, stored, identified, and distributed.

• Operate material handling equipment, including forklifts, as required.

• Collaborate with project management, procurement, warehouse personnel, and field teams to ensure material availability and timely delivery.

• Maintain compliance with company safety policies and material handling procedures.

Other duties may be assigned as needed to support business operations.

Minimum Qualifications

Required:

• High School Diploma or GED required; Associate's degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, or related field preferred.

• Minimum 3-5 years of experience in materials coordination, logistics coordination, transportation scheduling, warehouse operations, or supply chain management.

• Experience scheduling daily truck deliveries and coordinating freight transportation.

• Knowledge of shipping and receiving processes, freight carriers, logistics operations, and inventory management practices.

• Experience coordinating material deliveries to multiple project locations.

• Strong organizational and multitasking skills with the ability to manage competing priorities.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and inventory management systems.

• Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively with vendors, drivers, warehouse personnel, project teams, and leadership.

• Forklift certification or ability to obtain certification preferred.

Preferred:

Work Environment:
