Our Operations team is critical to our success and we are looking for a committed, diligent, and passionate part-time Operations Supervisor to help support our in-store lottery ticket operations. Reporting to our Operations Manager, you will be based on-site in Columbus, OH. This may be the perfect opportunity if you’re interested in operations management, growing your career at a start-up and playing a key role in the growth of a business!

Schedule: Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, & Thursday 5pm-11pm and open availability on the weekends.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

• Lead and ensure successful day-to-day lottery processing operations by overseeing and training a team of Operation Associates, proactively making recommendations for operational improvements, and providing general technical support

• Serve as the first point of contact for our Operations Associates and support escalations in the absence of the Operations Manager including facility issues, product outages, and staffing gaps

• Support back-end operations and general quality control by maintaining ticket equipment, ensuring the integrity and streamlining of processes, and monitoring execution of processes by team members

• Prepare SOS (Start of Shift) & EOS (End of Shift) reports on a daily, weekly, and monthly basis; report shift performance metrics and escalate issues to Operations Manager

• Assist with other various ad-hoc duties and projects as needed

YOU IDEALLY HAVE:

• 1-3 years of supervisory/lead experience

• Prior experience in retail, warehouse, or restaurant operations

• Medium-level technological know-how with the ability to troubleshoot and solve basic technical issues with equipment, operate basic systems and platforms, etc.

• The ability to lift up to 40 pounds as needed

ABOUT YOU:

• You have grit, tenacity, and what people describe to be a “get it done” mentality. You don’t believe any task is too big or too small for you

• You are known for your ability to pivot on the fly with changing priorities and remain calm under pressure

• You don’t mind if there isn't an existing playbook for you to follow; you are resourceful and self-reliant

• Your team members describe you as available, helpful, and a problem solver. You feel proud when you’re able to help others succeed in their roles

• You have a high attention to detail and are organized in how you work and get things done

• You fully own and are committed to your work. You don’t believe in cutting corners and it shows in the quality of your work

One of Jackpot’s core values is Lifelong Learning. We don’t believe we are ever finished products and strongly believe in growing and developing to improve ourselves. If what you’ve read so far sounds exciting but your experience doesn’t quite match what we’re looking for, we strongly encourage you to apply anyway! We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive team where everyone can feel proud to contribute to.

WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU:

• $20-$24 hourly pay rate

• 401k

• Sick Time

• Dedication to Lifelong Learning through our Monthly Speaker Series

• Monthly cultural and social events

• A culture of trust and accountability

jobs.title: Laboratory Test Technician
jobs.description:
At IEM, we’re not just building innovative electrical distribution systems, we’re shaping the future. IEM is dedicated to delivering world-class solutions for complex power needs. After 75 years, we continue to push the boundaries of what’s possible. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting out, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a lasting impact on industries that power the world’s most dynamic markets.

Location: Tualatin, OR

Reports To: Test Lab Manager

Salary Range: $66,560 - $ 93,600

Position Summary:

We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Test Technician to join the team at our new IEM Power Lab facility, specializing in the testing of low and medium voltage power distribution equipment. The ideal candidate will have at least 2 years of experience in a similar role, a strong mechanical aptitude and excellent attention to detail.

This role will be responsible for fabricating, assembling and setting up equipment and assisting Test Engineers with conducting tests on low and medium voltage power distribution equipment. The role also includes assisting in fabricating new test articles, modifying existing test articles, performing routine maintenance and loading, unloading and handling equipment and supplies.

Key Responsibilities:

• Assemble and set up test equipment and instrumentation according to specifications and test plans.

• Assist Test Engineers in conducting tests on low and medium voltage power distribution equipment.

• Record and document test results accurately and comprehensively.

• Identify and troubleshoot issues during testing procedures.

• Assemble, disassemble and modify test articles including installing or modifying wiring and control circuits according to provided design drawings.

• Fabricate and install new parts made of steel and copper or aluminum busbar.

• Set up, and operate fabricating machines, such as press brake, laser/punch machine, horizontal bend machine, and CNC router for various metals including steel, aluminum copper.

• Contribute to continuous improvement efforts to enhance testing processes and methodologies.

• Perform routine maintenance and calibration of testing equipment and facilities.

• Ensure a safe work environment and adhere to all applicable safety standards and protocols.

• Assist with packaging, loading and unloading of equipment and supplies.

• Maintain a clean and organized laboratory area. Assist with general facility upkeep.

• Maintain a limited inventory of materials, parts and supplies necessary for testing operations.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including R&D engineering, manufacturing engineering and quality teams to drive product improvements and resolve technical issues.

Competencies:

• Basic understanding of electrical principles and testing methodologies. Or the ability to learn quickly.

• Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with cross-functional teams.

• Ability to interpret design drawings and electrical schematics.

• Ability to follow written and verbal work instructions and procedures.

• Excellent problem-solving skills and an ability to troubleshoot technical issues.

• Strong mechanical aptitude with an ability to assemble, disassemble and modify equipment with limited instruction using a variety of hand and power tools.

• Experience fabricating metal parts using press brakes, shears, and forming/bending machines is preferred.

• Experience with safely loading, unloading and handling large equipment and machinery using sit-down lift trucks.

• Excellent computer skills and an ability to quickly learn new software tools and systems. Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite a must.

• Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.

• Strong commitment to safety and adherence to safety protocols.

Qualifications:

• Certification or Associate’s degree in a technical field.

• Minimum 2 years of experience as a Test Technician or similar role in a testing, manufacturing or service environment.

• Basic knowledge of electrical principles and power distribution concepts.

Workplace Conditions:

• Ability to lift and move equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds.

• Ability to stand, walk, and perform tasks requiring manual dexterity for extended periods.

Why Join IEM

At IEM, you’ll join a team that powers some of the world’s most ambitious projects. We’re engineers, makers, and problem-solvers who thrive on tackling complex challenges and delivering solutions that keep industries moving forward. If you’re driven, collaborative, and ready to make an impact, we’d love to hear from you. Your creativity and passion can help us achieve great things—come be part of the journey.

Learn more about IEM at https://www.iemfg.com

We offer comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support our employees' well-being, growth, and long-term success. View a snapshot of our benefits at https://www.iemfg.com/careers

Therefore, Uncommon Schools seeks teachers who are committed to becoming best-in-class educators, who are continuously improving instructional practices through collaboration and targeted development within their school community. We are currently seeking both experienced and apprentice teachers for all grades and all subjects for the 25-26 and 26-27 school years.

SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES

• Implement curricula and activities to meet our high academic standards
• Analyze assessments that measure progress towards these standards and use this assessment data to inform and differentiate instructional practices
• Focus constantly on student learning, thinking critically and strategically to respond to student learning needs
• Create a positive, structured learning environment to ensure that students observe the school’s core values, high expectations, and code of conduct
• Communicate effectively with students, families, and colleagues
• Commit to continual professional growth, participating actively in our annual, three-week staff orientation training in August and instructional training throughout the school year
• Participate and support grade-level activities and school-wide functions throughout the school-year

Strong applicants for all teaching roles (new and experienced) will possess the following:

• Relentless drive to improve the minds, characters & lives of students both in and out of school
• Unwavering commitment to urban youth achieving greatness
• Belief in and alignment with Uncommon’s core beliefs and educational philosophy is a must
• Mastery of and enthusiasm for relevant academic subjects
• Evidence of self-motivation, willingness to be a team player, and a strong sense of personal responsibility
• Ability and desire to implement feedback from school leaders and colleagues to become a more effective educator in service to our students.
• A background in education is not required for new teachers, but strong candidates should show a demonstrated passion for working with K-12 students and prior experience working in schools and/or urban communities is preferred.

Additional qualifications for experienced teachers:

• Proven track-record of high achievement in the classroom
• Minimum of two years teaching experience in an urban public school or charter school setting preferred
• Valid State Certification and Master’s degree are helpful but not required.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Candidates must have received a Bachelor's degree from a college or university before employment begins
• Candidates must have also earned a cumulative Grade Point Average (GPA) of 2.75 or higher by the time employment begins
• All Commonwealth charter teachers must either have an appropriate MA educator’s license or pass required the MTEL(s) including the Communications and Literacy MTEL , Subject Specific MTEL, and the MTEL SEI (Sheltered English Immersion) Endorsement within first year of employment. All core academic teachers* assigned to teach English learners are required to earn the SEI endorsement. #ZR

jobs.title: Marketing Technologies Director
jobs.description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Marketing Technologies Director

The Marketing Technologies Director, leads PlayStation's global marketing technology organization across engineering, product management, UX, measurement and experimentation, audience activation, and marketing data. This leader owns the technology vision, architecture, product strategy, and roadmap for platforms used by marketers worldwide to reach hundreds of millions of players. The role is accountable for building secure, scalable, AI-enabled capabilities that improve marketing effectiveness, speed, and customer experience.

We are seeking a technology leader with direct software or data engineering experience building marketing technology products and platforms. The successful candidate can lead engineers and technical product teams, make architecture and build-versus-buy decisions, and translate marketing needs into durable systems. Experience limited to administering vendors or managing a marketing technology stack without direct engineering experience does not meet the requirements of this role.

Key Responsibilities

Technology Engineering and Product Leadership

• Lead multidisciplinary teams responsible for marketing technology engineering, product management, and UX, with clear goals, operating rhythms, and accountability for delivery.

• Own end-to-end delivery and operation of global marketing platforms, from discovery and architecture through launch, adoption, reliability, and continuous improvement.

• Set the architecture for marketing platforms, APIs, data pipelines, audience services, orchestration, and activation integrations.

• Define the marketing technology product vision and prioritize a multi-year roadmap based on customer value, technical feasibility, business impact, risk, and platform health.

• Establish engineering standards for security, privacy, reliability, observability, scalability, and the management of technical debt.

• Lead product discovery and UX research with marketing teams globally, converting user needs into intuitive workflows and measurable product outcomes.

• Evaluate build, buy, and partner options with technical rigor, and ensure third-party platforms integrate into a coherent, maintainable architecture.

Measurement Experimentation and Audience Activation

• Lead the measurement and experimentation function, including test design, measurement frameworks, platform capabilities, and the use of results in marketing decisions.

• Lead audience activation and marketing data teams responsible for identity, segmentation, consent-aware audience management, data quality, governance, and activation readiness.

• Connect audience, measurement, and activation capabilities across marketing channels so teams can plan, execute, learn, and optimize through shared data and platforms.

• Partner with Data Science and Analytics leaders to embed experimentation, causal measurement, predictive models, and decision support into marketing workflows.

• Assess and scale AI and automation use cases that improve marketer productivity, decision quality, and customer relevance.

Strategy and Transformation

• Serve as the technical and strategic partner to Media, Creative, Brand Marketing, Product Marketing, Marketing Operations, Data Science, and Business Analytics leaders.

• Align SIE teams that own or influence the marketing technology stack around a single architecture, product vision, roadmap, and set of investment priorities.

• Lead high-priority transformation initiatives, managing execution, organizational dependencies, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

• Partner with marketing leaders to redesign workflows, processes, decision rights, and operating models around new platform capabilities.

• Balance global platform standards with appropriate local and product-level flexibility while maintaining security, privacy, and architectural integrity.

• Define success measures and post-launch KPI tracking for platform performance, adoption, marketing effectiveness, and business impact.

Skills and Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in software engineering, computer science, data engineering, or a related technical field; equivalent practical experience is acceptable. An advanced degree is preferred.

• 12+ years of experience across software or data engineering, technical product management, and marketing technology, including leadership of global teams.

• Direct software or data engineering experience and a record of leading engineering teams that built and operated production marketing technology systems.

• Demonstrated success building, launching, and operating enterprise SaaS products or internal platforms, beyond implementing or administering third-party tools.

• Technical depth in cloud architecture, APIs, systems integration, data pipelines, identity and audience systems, security, privacy, reliability, and scalability.

• Experience leading multidisciplinary organizations spanning engineering, product management, UX, measurement and experimentation, analytics or data science, and audience activation.

• Strong command of experimentation methods, marketing measurement, analytics, and the use of data to improve product and marketing decisions.

• Experience with AI-powered products, machine learning platforms, or automation in production environments.

• Experience owning multi-year technology and product roadmaps and making investment, architecture, and build-versus-buy decisions.

• Ability to influence senior leaders, communicate technical tradeoffs clearly, and lead transformation across teams and regions.

At SIE, we consider several factors when setting each role’s base pay range, including the competitive benchmarking data for the market and geographic location.

Please note that the base pay range may vary in line with our hybrid working policy and individual base pay will be determined based on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, and location.

In addition, this role is eligible for SIE’s top-tier benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, matching 401(k), paid time off, wellness program and coveted employee discounts for Sony products. This role also may be eligible for a bonus package. Click here to learn more.

This is a flexible role that can be remote, with varying pay ranges based on geographic location. For example, if you are based out of Seattle, the estimated base pay range for this role is listed below.

$207,400—$311,200 USD

jobs.description:

We believe every child should be able to be whatever they want to be in life regardless of where they were born.

Our Early Learning Academies (learning centers) focus on providing high-quality early childhood education that prepare children for kindergarten and provide the foundation for long-term academic success. As the population of children with two working parents grows, so does the demand for childcare where families are engaged in their child’s learning experiences. Parents increasingly focus on early education rather than simple “day-care” – this secular trend is resulting in a shift in consumer preference towards more educationally focused childcare offerings.

The Senior Financial Analyst will support the Early Learning Academies division and serve as a key strategic partner in financial planning, resource allocation, operational performance management, and growth initiatives. This role will work closely with leadership, operations, accounting, and finance teams to deliver actionable insights that drive informed business decisions and support the organization's continued expansion.

The ideal candidate combines strong financial modeling and analytical capabilities with the ability to translate complex data into meaningful business recommendations. This individual will play a critical role in budgeting, forecasting, performance analysis, operational improvement, and evaluating strategic growth opportunities.

This is a hybrid position located in McLean, Virginia

Specific Duties and Responsibilities:

• Partner with multiple departments to curate information, deliver key insights and provide strategic perspectives; provide actionable recommendations based on data and performance objectives

• Build financial models and sensitivity analyses to determine forecasted revenue, costs, and profitability for various scenarios and new growth initiatives

• Prepare and coordinate materials for Executive management to effectively communicate company’s strategy and performance

• Lead monthly rolling forecasts, quarterly outlooks, and annual budget process. Perform analysis to understand and communicate variances while working to improve forecasting methods

• Identify and implement opportunities to improve efficiency, accuracy, and scalability of work through AI-driven solutions

• Proven track record of translating complex and fragmented data sets to meaningful insights and recommendations

• Independent and able to thrive in a fast-paced work environment fueled by inorganic growth

jobs.title: Research Scientist - Post-Training
jobs.description:
Pluralis Research works on Protocol Learning: training and serving large models in a fully decentralized way on small consumer-grade devices connected via the internet. Despite being dismissed as infeasible, we have made significant advances on this problem, most recently Agora, a permissionless run that pretrained an 8B model from scratch on consumer GPUs spread over the internet, with no single participant ever holding the full weights (tech report https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13332). While many of the core research problems have been solved, Protocol Learning unlocks a series of new challenges. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning https://pluralis.ai/blog/a-third-path-protocol-learning/.

Agora gave us a pretrained 8B model. Post-training is how we make it useful for agentic use-cases. But every post-training stack you've seen assumes a datacenter — synchronous rollouts, fast interconnects, trusted workers. Ours gets none of that. It has to run on consumer GPUs, and Macs spread across the public internet, training a model whose weights no single participant ever holds, with rollouts arriving from a geo-distributed inference pipeline at high latencies. Your primary role is to make RL post-training work here anyway — the algorithms and the system, end-to-end.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build the post-training stack: You build the RL training loop end-to-end: rollout ingestion from the geo-distributed inference pipeline, reward computation, policy updates, and getting updated weights back out to the network. You set the direction, and you make things happen.

 - Invent the algorithms: Standard RL recipes assume on-policy rollouts from fast, trusted hardware. You adapt them to asynchronous, high-latency, partially trusted generation: staleness tolerance, off-policy corrections, and communication-efficient policy updates.

 - Ship first post-trained models: You build the evals that show the models are improving, and you take the first decentralized post-trained release from run to public artifact.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Hands-on RL post-training: You've run RL post-training on large language models — RLHF, RLVR, or reasoning-focused RL — and touched the systems layer yourself: rollout generation, async training loops, weight synchronization. Not just launched jobs on someone else's stack.

 - Strong engineering: Production-quality Python and PyTorch: concurrency, failure handling, profiling before optimizing.

 - Research ability: Publications in RL post-training, asynchronous or distributed RL, or nearby fields are a strong signal. So is unpublished work you can defend in detail.

 - Mission alignment: You believe Protocol Learning is the viable third path for collective, trustless, and sovereign AI.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience training over slow networks, or with decentralized or federated setups.

 - Familiarity with serving-engine internals such as vLLM or SGLang — our rollout pipeline is a serving system.

 - Experience with reward modeling or building verifiable-reward datasets.

 - Experience with P2P networking and NAT traversal.

 - Experience at proprietary, open-weight and open-source AI labs


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Equity-Heavy Package: We offer significant ownership for key technical contributors in addition to a high base salary.

 - Remote-First Culture: Flexible work environment with team members distributed globally.

 - Visa Sponsorship: Optional full visa sponsorship and relocation support to either Australia or the US.

 - Open Problems: Training and serving frontier models on hardware you don't control, over networks you don't own, mostly has no published answers yet. You'll write some of the first ones.


FYI'S

 - We work remotely across the world, with the main teams in Australia and North America. You'll need to be comfortable working across timezones.

 - Applicants must have professional-level English proficiency (written and spoken).

 - Recruiters: we aren't looking for agency support at this time. We'll reach out if we need help.

We are backed by Union Square Ventures https://www.usv.com/ and other tier-1 investors, and we are a world-class, deeply technical team of ML researchers. Pluralis is unapologetically ideological. We believe AI, and the world, end up on a better path if we succeed in implementing the protocol for intelligence. If this resonates, please apply.

Who We Serve

We serve family-owned and owner-operated home service businesses (plumbing, HVAC, and other trades) that run on FieldPulse, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan, and similar field service platforms. We give them the operational infrastructure and talent to run day-to-day operations, so the owners can focus on the field, sales, and growth.

About the Role

You’ll be the remote office manager for a family-owned plumbing company in the US. The owners need one person who runs the office end to end. That means answering every customer call and text, owning the dispatch board, and closing out jobs. At the end of each day, you tell them what was sold, what was collected, and what’s scheduled next.

By your 90th day, you’re the administrative backbone of the business. The owners trust the board because you run it. Plumbers send schedule changes through you instead of moving jobs themselves.

What You’ll Own

• Call intake and customer communication: Answer every incoming call, text, and Google Local Services lead from one shared inbox. Enter each one in the field service software the same day, tagged with its lead source. Give customers arrival windows, leave pricing to the plumbers, and call back when you said you would.

• Scheduling and dispatch: Own the dispatch board as the single source of truth. Book arrival windows and assign plumbers, helpers, and equipment (excavator, hydro jetter). Handle every reschedule.

• Job tracking and return visits: Review every open job’s status daily, from booking through completion and invoicing. Make sure plumbers post status updates and notes. Book return trips on the original job, and flag jobs at risk of slipping.

• Estimate follow-up: Review open estimates every morning and confirm whether the office or the plumber follows up. Update the status after each touch, and close out estimates that go cold.

• Job closeout and payments: Each morning, check yesterday’s paid invoices for job costs, the correct commission rate, fees, referral tags, and deposits. Flag anything that doesn’t add up.

• Payroll and time tracking support: Verify plumber commissions and helper hours each pay cycle, and chase missing clock-ins before payroll runs.

• Permits and compliance: Track every job that needs a permit. Send certificates of insurance (COIs) to cities that require them before the work is scheduled.

• Daily reporting: Send the owner an end-of-day summary every business day covering what was sold, what was collected, and what’s on tomorrow’s board.

• Process documentation: Turn every recurring task into a simple written process so the office runs the same way every day.

How Success Is Measured

• 95% of calls answered, with under 5 minutes to respond to new leads

• 75%+ of qualified leads booked

• Every lead entered the same day with its lead source

• A dispatch board that matches reality at the end of every day

• Open estimates followed up every day, per the follow-up process

• Paid invoices checked every morning, with deposits collected on scheduled work

• Hours and commissions verified before every pay run

• Permits and COIs sent before the job is scheduled

• End-of-day summary sent every business day

What You Bring

Must have:

• 2+ years as an office manager, dispatcher, customer service rep (CSR), or operations coordinator, ideally for a plumbing, HVAC, electrical, or other field service company

• Experience answering customer calls and texts as a core part of your job

• Experience owning a schedule or dispatch board for a team working in the field

• Hands-on experience with at least one field service platform: FieldPulse, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan, Jobber, Workiz, or similar

• Clear, confident written and spoken English for US homeowners on the phone

• A reliable remote setup: stable internet, a quiet workspace, and a backup plan for outages

Nice to have:

• Direct plumbing or HVAC experience

• QuickBooks Online or QuickBooks Time

• Podium or another customer messaging inbox

• Experience checking commissions or hours before payroll

• Experience handling permits or certificates of insurance

• Basic job costing familiarity

How You Work

• Detail first: Tags, rates, fees, and notes are right the first time.

• You own it to the end: Every call, job, and estimate goes from first contact to close without the owner stepping in.

• You bring solutions: When something breaks, you raise it early with the problem, three options, and your recommendation.

• You write it down: Recurring work becomes a documented process.

• You live in the system: Every customer conversation is logged on the job, not in side texts.

Compensation & Benefits (to be provided by Offshore Launch):

• Up to $1600/mo depending on experience

• Guaranteed annual bonus of one month's salary

• Performance-based annual bonus up to 1.5x one month's salary contingent on quarterly performance scores

• Comprehensive health benefits, including dependents: health, life, vision and dental insurance.

• 16 days PTO

Note:

The Client is not involved in compensation or benefits. As an employee of Offshore Launch, all compensation and benefits are to be provided by the Agency.

jobs.title: Solutions Engineer, Ledger
jobs.description:
New York (SoHo) · Hybrid, 3 days/week onsite · Full-time




ABOUT FORMANCE

Formance builds open-source financial infrastructure. Our core product is a programmable double-entry ledger. Fintechs, crypto platforms, and financial institutions use it as the source of truth for their balances: every movement of money is recorded as a transaction between accounts, and every balance can be traced back to the postings that produced it.

Around the ledger, we connect to banks and payment providers and reconcile what the ledger records against what actually moved.

We are a team of 30+ people, mostly engineers, working across New York and Paris. Our systems support real money movement, so correctness is not optional.


WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON

Our customers are engineering teams building financial products. They come to us with questions like “how do we track user wallets, pending funds, and fees so that every cent is accounted for?” or “what happens to our balances when a payment fails halfway through?”

You help them answer those questions, from the first technical conversation through proof of concept and into a successful transition to implementation.

 - Design money flows. Turn a customer's product into a ledger model: which accounts exist, how funds move between them, and how balances are queried. Typical use cases include user wallets, pending vs. settled funds, fees and revenue sharing, refunds and chargebacks, and multi-currency.

 - Lead the technical sale. Partner closely with our NYC sales team to run technical discovery and architecture sessions with CTOs, VPs of Engineering, and Heads of Payments. Build proofs of concept around real customer use cases and explain architectural trade-offs clearly, including what the ledger guarantees and what remains the customer's responsibility.

 - Build trust with technical buyers. Challenge assumptions, answer complex engineering questions, and help prospective customers evaluate how Formance fits into their existing infrastructure. You are comfortable engaging directly with senior technical decision-makers.

 - Support the transition to production. Work with our implementation team to ensure a smooth handover, sharing technical context, architectural decisions, and customer requirements. Stay involved when your expertise is needed to resolve complex technical questions.

 - Bring the field back to the product. Turn recurring customer patterns into reference models, examples, and documentation, and share structured feedback with our engineering team in Paris.

 - Support customers beyond the initial sale, helping with technical onboarding, implementation, and a smooth transition to ongoing customer support.

You will join a small Solutions Engineering team and work closely with our founders, NYC sales team, and engineers.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years of experience in software engineering, solutions engineering, or technical implementation, ideally within payments, banking, fintech infrastructure, or digital assets.

 - A strong understanding of how money is tracked in software. You know what double-entry means in practice, or you have worked on systems where balances, transactions, and reconciliation matter.

 - Familiarity with real payment flows, including settlement delays, returns, partial failures, and mismatches between internal records and external providers.

 - Hands-on technical experience with APIs, databases, and at least one programming language.

 - Confidence working with technical buyers. You are comfortable leading technical conversations with engineering leaders, challenging architectural assumptions, and building credibility with highly technical stakeholders.

 - The ability to explain complex systems clearly to engineering, finance, and product stakeholders, and an interest in working directly with customers.

 - An independent approach to problem-solving. You learn unfamiliar systems quickly and use modern development tools, including AI, where they improve your work.


STRONG SIGNALS

 - You have built or maintained a ledger, wallet system, or reconciliation process.

 - You have worked with a banking-as-a-service provider, card issuer, or core banking system.

 - You have supported technical evaluations, proofs of concept, or architecture discussions with prospective customers.

 - You have moved from a software engineering role into a customer-facing technical position.


HOW WE INTERVIEW

Part of the process is a working session in which you walk us through how you would track money for a simple product, such as a marketplace with fees, refunds, and delayed payouts.

We look at how you reason about accounts, edge cases, and architectural decisions, as well as how clearly you communicate your approach.

No prior knowledge of Formance is expected.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - $165–175k OTE 

 - Equity

 - 401(k) with 4% employer match

 - Health insurance (medical, dental, vision)

 - Unlimited PTO

 - Annual team offsite in Europe

jobs.title: Research Scientist - Pre-training
jobs.description:
Pluralis Research works on Protocol Learning: training and serving large models in a fully decentralized way on small consumer-grade devices connected via the internet. Despite being dismissed as infeasible, we have made significant advances on this problem, most recently Agora, a permissionless run that pretrained an 8B model from scratch on consumer GPUs spread over the internet, with no single participant ever holding the full weights (tech report https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13332). While many of the core research problems have been solved, Protocol Learning unlocks a series of new challenges. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning https://pluralis.ai/blog/a-third-path-protocol-learning/.

This setting breaks nearly every assumption of datacenter training: communication-efficient training across different parallelism axes, fault tolerance as nodes join and drop mid-run, heterogeneous compute and networks, and robustness to malicious participants. Our published methods include Subspace Networks https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01260, Factored Gossip DiLoCo https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22768, AsyncMesh https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22442, and Sentinel https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03592.

As a Research Scientist you'll build the training system that takes Protocol Learning from the 8B run to frontier scale: large models on heterogeneous hardware, in physically different regions, connected by ordinary internet.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Distributed pretraining: Implement and optimize model-parallel training. Data, pipeline, and tensor parallelism for large models on heterogeneous GPUs under low-bandwidth, high-latency links.

 - Performance optimization: Implement techniques that reduce communication overhead while maintaining model convergence in challenging network environments.

 - Elasticity and fault tolerance: Make runs survive node churn. Robust checkpointing, state synchronization, and recovery as participants join and leave.

 - Run instrumentation: Build the monitoring that shows throughput, bottlenecks, and model quality across hundreds of devices.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Hands-on distributed training (required): You've trained models across many devices in PyTorch with FSDP, DeepSpeed, Megatron, or your own implementation. You understand data, tensor, and pipeline parallelism.

 - Strong engineering: Production-quality Python. Concurrency, failure handling, profiling before optimizing.

 - Evidence of execution: Shipped systems, research code, open-source work, or serious personal projects.

 - Mission alignment: You believe Protocol Learning is the viable third path for collective, trustless, and sovereign AI.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Hands-on experience training or serving large language models such as Nemotron, Qwen or OLMo.

 - Experience with P2P networking and NAT traversal.

 - Experience with post-training and RL.

 - Experience with inference and serving systems.

 - Experience at proprietary, open-weight and open-source AI labs


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Equity-Heavy Package: We offer significant ownership for key technical contributors in addition to a high base salary.

 - Remote-First Culture: Flexible work environment with team members distributed globally.

 - Visa Sponsorship: Optional full visa sponsorship and relocation support to either Australia or the US.

 - Open Problems: Training and serving frontier models on hardware you don't control, over networks you don't own, mostly has no published answers yet. You'll write some of the first ones.


FYI'S

 - We work remotely across the world, with the main teams in Australia and North America. You'll need to be comfortable working across timezones.

• Telemetry competency

jobs.title: Senior Financial Systems Analyst
jobs.description:
Opportunity at a Glance

The Senior Financial Systems Analyst is a highly skilled individual contributor who leads technical process improvement across the Finance systems landscape supporting Accounting and FP&A. This role serves as the primary owner of automation, data transformation, and solution design initiatives, with a strong focus on improving efficiency, reliability, and scalability across financial processes and reporting. The analyst partners closely with Accounting, FP&A, IT, and other stakeholders to identify opportunities to simplify work, reduce manual effort, and strengthen controls through better system and process design. A core philosophy for this role is Eliminate → Automate → Optimize: challenge existing processes, remove non-value-added work, automate recurring and manual activities, and continuously improve performance and user experience. This role is expected to operate with a high degree of independence, resolve ambiguity, and apply strong technical judgment to deliver practical, scalable solutions.

Responsibilities

• Process Improvement and AutomationIdentify opportunities to eliminate, simplify, automate, and optimize Finance and Accounting processes across the financial systems ecosystem.Lead the design, development, and maintenance of automated workflows to support journal entries, reporting, reconciliations, and data transformation activities.Apply structured problem-solving and technical analysis to improve process efficiency, reduce manual effort, and increase solution reliability.Establish and promote development standards, documentation practices, and sustainable automation approaches that support long-term maintainability.
• Data Engineering and Technical DevelopmentWrite, troubleshoot, and optimize SQL queries across financial systems and data sources, including Lawson SQL Server and Google BigQuery.Analyze, reverse engineer, document, and validate data structures, business logic, and reporting outputs where source processes or models are not well defined.Support report rebuilds, data validation, and analytical reporting needs across Power BI and other reporting tools.Maintain and enhance existing VBA-based solutions where appropriate, while introducing more scalable tools such as Python for data extraction, transformation, file handling, automation, API integration, and controls-related processes.Evaluate and apply emerging AI-enabled development tools and coding assistants, where appropriate, to accelerate development, improve documentation, and enhance solution delivery.
• Solution Design and GovernanceTranslate business requests into well-defined technical solutions that balance user needs, control requirements, and long-term supportability.Assess request complexity, dependencies, and technical feasibility to help prioritize automation and process improvement efforts.Maintain technical documentation, solution designs, runbooks, dependencies, and change logs to support knowledge transfer and operational continuity.Partner with IT, external vendors, and business stakeholders to troubleshoot system and data issues, support implementation efforts, and resolve technical challenges.
• Operational Support and Backup CoverageProvide backup support for critical financial systems administration and operational activities as needed, including user access changes, month-end journal processing, key master data updates, and actuals refresh support.Help strengthen operational resilience by ensuring recurring processes are documented, scalable, and not dependent on a single resource.

jobs.title: Private Client Services – Trust & Estate Administration – Counsel
jobs.description:
Barnes & Thornburg LLP is seeking an accomplished, senior-level attorney to lead trust administration, probate, and estate settlement matters for its Private Client Services Group in Indianapolis. The role involves counseling individual and corporate fiduciaries, beneficiaries, high-net-worth families, and closely held business owners through every stage of trust and estate settlement.

The primary focus of this position is trust and estate administration and settlement. The successful candidate will serve as the day-to-day point person on fiduciary administration matters, managing client matters with a high degree of autonomy. Estate planning experience is valued as a complementary skill set, and the practice offers opportunities to advise on planning matters as well.

We welcome interested attorneys from a range of professional backgrounds. Along with law firm practitioners, we encourage applications from licensed attorneys who have served as trust officers, estate or trust settlement officers, fiduciary counsel, or senior fiduciary advisors at banks, trust companies, or family offices and who want to return to, or move into, private practice. The firm is open to a Counsel or partner-track arrangement, depending on the candidate’s experience and career goals. Hybrid work arrangements are available for the right candidate.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own and manage a full docket of trust administration, probate, and estate settlement matters from intake to closing, serving as the primary attorney and day-to-day contact for fiduciaries and families

 - Guide personal representatives and trustees through all phases of administration, including marshaling, valuing, and retitling assets; paying debts, expenses, and claims; and making interim and final distributions

 - Handle supervised and unsupervised estate administrations and trust-related court proceedings. This includes petitions, statutory notices, inventories, accountings, petitions for distribution, and closing filings

 - Interpret wills, trust instruments, and related governing documents. Advise on fiduciary powers, duties, and discretionary distribution decisions

 - Counsel individual and corporate fiduciaries on fiduciary duties, beneficiary communications, conflict avoidance, and risk management, including releases, receipts, and settlement agreements

 - Coordinate post-mortem tax planning and compliance, including estate tax returns (Form 706), fiduciary income tax returns (Form 1041), portability and other elections, basis issues, and gift and GST tax matters. Work closely with CPAs, fiduciary accountants, and appraisers

 - Identify and resolve administration issues such as trust modification, decanting, nonjudicial settlement agreements, disclaimers, and beneficiary or creditor disputes. Work with the firm’s litigation colleagues when matters become contested

 - Oversee the administration of closely held business interests, real estate, and other complex or illiquid assets held in estates and trusts
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - J.D. from an accredited law school and strong academic credentials

 - Substantial, senior-level experience (generally 10 or more years) in trust and estate administration, probate, and estate settlement, gained in a law firm, bank or trust company fiduciary department, family office, or similar sophisticated fiduciary setting

 - Proven ability to independently manage a high-volume, complex administration and settlement docket at a level comparable to a trust and estate administration partner or senior trust/estate settlement officer

 - Deep working knowledge of probate procedure, trust law, fiduciary duties, and post-death administration. Experience with Indiana probate and trust practice is strongly preferred

 - Strong command of estate, gift, generation-skipping transfer, and fiduciary income tax principles as they apply to administration

 - Experience advising individual and corporate fiduciaries, beneficiaries, and high-net-worth families, including those with closely held business interests

 - Estate planning drafting experience is a plus but not required

 - Exposure to fiduciary litigation, tax audits, or tax controversy matters is a plus

 - Excellent judgment, communication, and client-service skills, with the ability to handle sensitive family dynamics tactfully and discreetly

 - Admission to the Indiana bar, or eligibility to obtain admission promptly after hire
   
   


ABOUT THE FIRM

Barnes & Thornburg LLP is an AmLaw 100 firm with 26 offices. The firm and our Private Client Services Group have an exceptional reputation for having an inclusive, collegial, and supportive atmosphere, where members of the firm can thrive, learn, and advance in their career.



We will not consider resumes submitted by external agencies or recruiters for this position. Recruiters and agencies will not be compensated for assisting Barnes & Thornburg LLP in recruiting for this position, regardless of whether such party has a recruiting contract with us.

jobs.title: Assistant General Counsel, Americas
jobs.description:
Telix Pharmaceuticals is a dynamic, fast-growing radiopharmaceutical company with offices in Australia (HQ), Belgium, Japan, Switzerland, and the United States. Our mission is to deliver on the promise of precision medicine through targeted radiation. At our core, we exist to create products that seek to improve the quality of life for people living with cancer and rare diseases. You will be supporting the international roll-out of our approved prostate cancer imaging agent and helping us to advance our portfolio of late clinical-stage products that address significant unmet need in oncology and rare diseases.

See Yourself at Telix

Telix Pharmaceuticals is a dynamic, fast-growing radiopharmaceutical company with offices in Australia (HQ), Belgium, Japan, Switzerland, and the United States. Our mission is to deliver on the promise of precision medicine through targeted radiation. At our core, we exist to create products that seek to improve the quality of life for people living with cancer and rare diseases. You will be supporting the international roll-out of our approved prostate cancer imaging agent and helping us to advance our portfolio of late clinical-stage products that address significant unmet need in oncology and rare diseases.

The Assistant General Counsel, Americas serves as the lead attorney and strategic legal partner for Telix's Phase 3 and go-to-market activities in the Americas region, the company's largest market by revenue and headcount. The role covers the full Phase 3-to-commercial product lifecycle: Food and Drug Administration labeling and promotional/advertising review, Medical-Legal-Regulatory (MLR) review committee participation, healthcare fraud and abuse compliance (Anti-Kickback Statute safe-harbor analysis, False Claims Act risk), patient support program design and compliance, market access and government pricing (Medicare, Medicaid, 340B Drug Pricing Program, state drug pricing transparency laws), specialty distributor and specialty pharmacy contracting, commercial medical affairs activities, antitrust and unfair competition law as applied to commercial activities, and litigation/dispute management. The role is designed for an experienced life sciences attorney who can operate with substantial autonomy as the primary, trusted legal point of contact for Americas commercial and medical affairs leadership, proactively partnering with the business rather than merely providing reactive legal review, while escalating high-risk issues appropriately.

This is a growth role for a lawyer who wants to build a career in pharmaceutical product counseling while embedded with Americas commercial, medical affairs, and market-access leadership. It offers meaningful autonomy, close business partnership, and the opportunity to shape commercial legal support in Telix’s largest market.

We are a dynamic, fast-growing biopharmaceutical company where everyone counts. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer health and wellbeing incentives, bonus incentives, and support for learning and development. You will be part of an engaged and supportive group of colleagues who all have a shared purpose: to help people with cancer and rare diseases live longer, better quality lives.

Key Accountabilities:

• Serve as the primary legal business partner to Americas commercial, marketing, sales, and medical affairs leadership, providing strategic and solutions-oriented counsel on all downstream legal matters from Phase 3 development through commercial product lifecycle management.

• Advise on Food and Drug Administration labeling strategy, post-market commitments, Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies, expanded access, and pipeline submissions; counsel on regulatory compliance requirements for Telix's approved and near-approval radiopharmaceutical products.

• Serve as legal lead on Medical-Legal-Regulatory (MLR) promotional review committees; assess promotional and non-promotional materials (including digital, social media, and field-force content) for off-label risk, fair balance, claims substantiation, and compliance with Food and Drug Administration advertising and promotion requirements.

• Advise on Anti-Kickback Statute safe-harbor analysis, False Claims Act risk, healthcare fraud and abuse compliance, Sunshine Act/Open Payments transparency obligations, and interactions with Healthcare Professionals, Key Opinion Leaders, patients, patient advocacy organizations, and payers.

• Counsel on patient support program design and compliance, including co-pay assistance, hub services, specialty pharmacy relationships, and patient engagement programs, ensuring consistency with federal and state healthcare fraud and abuse frameworks.

• Advise on market access, government pricing (Medicare, Medicaid, 340B Drug Pricing Program, Veterans Health Care Act pricing obligations), state drug pricing transparency laws, payer/group purchasing organization contracting, specialty distribution arrangements, and commercial launch readiness for the Americas market.

• Draft, review, and negotiate complex commercial agreements with healthcare-community counterparties including hospitals, clinics, payers, specialty pharmacies, pharmacy benefit managers, diagnostic partners, and patient/professional advocacy organizations.

• Advise on antitrust and unfair competition law as applied to commercial activities, pricing strategies, distribution arrangements, and competitive intelligence programs.

• Manage and oversee litigation and dispute matters in the Americas, including coordination with outside counsel, budget discipline, and reporting of material litigation risk to the Group General Counsel.

• Coordinate with Compliance on field activity compliance risks, speaker programs, advisory boards, Medical Science Liaison interactions, and evolving healthcare enforcement trends; monitor government enforcement actions and settlement developments relating to pharmaceutical promotion.

• Develop and maintain playbooks, templates, escalation guidance, and compliance training materials for recurring Americas commercial legal matters; proactively identify process-improvement and efficiency opportunities to strengthen the legal function's service delivery.

• Effectively manage outside counsel relationships and budgets for Americas commercial and litigation matters with spend discipline and measurable outcomes.

• Provide Americas clinical trial support, including CTAs, site agreements, investigator relationships, IITs, publications, medical affairs programs, advisory boards, and MSL frameworks.

• Structure HCP/KOL engagement programs with appropriate design, value-exchange, antitrust, distribution, and compliance considerations.

Position Requirements

Education and Experience:

• Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school; active bar admission in at least one United States state required.

• 8-12+ years of legal practice with significant Food and Drug Administration promotional/labeling, healthcare compliance, pharmaceutical commercialization, market access, and/or commercial healthcare litigation experience; at least 4 years of in-house experience at a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or life sciences company strongly preferred.

• Substantive knowledge of United States healthcare fraud and abuse laws: Anti-Kickback Statute and its safe harbors, False Claims Act, Sunshine Act/Open Payments, Stark Law (as applicable to pharmaceutical arrangements), and relevant Office of Inspector General compliance guidance and Department of Justice enforcement precedent.

• Experience with promotional review processes (Medical-Legal-Regulatory/Promotional Review Committee), Food and Drug Administration advertising and promotion requirements, and labeling/claims substantiation for pharmaceutical or biologic products.

• Experience advising on market access, government pricing (Medicare, Medicaid, 340B Drug Pricing Program), state drug pricing transparency and reporting laws, and/or specialty distribution/pharmacy contracting preferred.

• Experience managing outside counsel, adhering to litigation and advisory budgets, and driving measurable spend efficiency.

• Familiarity with antitrust/unfair competition law in the pharmaceutical commercial context, patient support program compliance, and/or life sciences litigation (product liability, government investigations, commercial disputes) preferred.

Key Capabilities:

• Commitment to excellence: Take pride in your work and consistently strive for excellence in everything you do

• Results-oriented: Driven to achieve goals and objectives, with a strong focus on delivering measurable results

• Creativity and innovation: Possess a willingness to think outside the box and come up with unique and creative solutions to challenges

• Strong communication skills: Able to communicate effectively with colleagues and stakeholders at all levels, using clear and concise language

• Collaboration: Work effectively as part of a team, actively sharing knowledge and expertise to achieve common goals

• Resilience: Demonstrate the ability to bounce back from setbacks and persevere in the face of challenges

• Inclusive mindset: Demonstrate an understanding and appreciation for diversity, and actively work to create an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and respected

• Adaptability: Comfortable working in a dynamic environment, able to adjust to changing priorities, and willing to take on new challenges

• Ethical behavior: Act with integrity and demonstrate a commitment to ethical behavior in all interactions with colleagues and stakeholders

The Aide works collectively with teachers, school leaders, students, and family members to meet the needs of our students, ensuring their social and academic growth as they gain the skills needed to excel in school and beyond. Aides are crucial in the growth and success of the students on their caseload and work collaboratively with the Lead Teacher to ensure that all students engage in instruction at a level that is rigorous and accessible. Together, we seek to create a professional and authentic environment of joy, excellence, care, and community where educators make long term transformative outcomes for students.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Classroom Responsibilities

• Guide and assist individual students (1:1 support) and/or group of students with the requisite attention needed, which is separate from the general class
• Under the direction of the Lead Teacher and/or Supervisor, complement classroom instruction to help maximize the learning opportunities for students on a caseload including, but not limited to:Assist classroom teachers in creating curriculum modifications for specific studentsProvide support to Lead Teachers, Residents, and/or Fellows by carrying out lesson plans and assisting with learning materialsProvide testing accommodations, including supervising students completing tests in a separate location or during an extended timeReview and correct student work assignmentsAssist in the implementation of behavioral intervention plans which may involve use of positive reinforcement strategies, behavior modification, and other skills or knowledge to ensure safety and success for individual studentsAssist individual students with self-advocacy about particular needs while in the classroomFacilitate and support social interactions and foster the development of positive relationships between students on the caseload and their peers and teachersConstantly assess progress, communicate results clearly, and use data to inform decisions and set goalsFollow and record data for prescribed toilet training protocols as necessaryCollect, record, and summarize data on observable student behaviorMaintain student confidentiality (in consultation with Board Certified Behavior Analyst, as required)Attend staff professional development sessions, special education team meetings, IEP meetings, and grade level team meetings
• May physically assist with physical needs of students, as needed

School and Professional Responsibilities

• Obtain required requirements for an Aide within one year of hire, which includes one of the following:Associate’s Degree OR48 college credit hours ORPass the ParaPro Assessment with a score of 464 with study resources and support from KIPP MA
• Provide aide coverage and support to other classrooms and grade levels as needed
• Be available for an extended workday, as needed, to support colleagues, students, and families outside of school hours
• Perform necessary support duties including, but not limited to, coverage, bus, lunch, and dismissal duties
• Collaborate with grade level teams to provide support, guidance, and advocacy concerning the students on the caseload
• Utilize safe and appropriate handling procedures when working with students including becoming trained in crisis prevention and nonviolent intervention
• Dependable attendance according to our school calendar

Regional Responsibilities

• Embody KIPP MA’s Code of Conduct by acting with integrity, leading with humanity, centering self-awareness and critical consciousness, taking personal responsibility, and engaging productively
• Participate and engage in regional professional development and community events as required
• Demonstrated ability to collect and interpret data, evaluate, reason, define problems, establish facts, draw valid conclusions, and make reasonable judgments and decisions in a timely manner in accordance with the needs of the school
• Self-awareness, flexibility and emotional intelligence to navigate a setting with students who express diverse needs
• The consistent use of interpersonal and self-management skills to effectively support behavioral and emotional needs of students to ensure a safe and inclusive environment, as well as build relationships and manage conflict with students, staff, and caregivers
• Effective communication skills to perform assigned duties and to meaningfully exchange information with students, staff, families and others in person, through written communication, in front of groups, and on virtual platforms
• Physical mobility to move self in various positions in order to execute duties effectively, which may include kneeling, walking, pushing/pulling, squatting, twisting, turning, bending, stooping and reaching overhead
• Physical strength sufficient to periodically lift and/or carry 20 pounds of materials or supplies and to physically restrain a student to keep from harming themself and/or others in an emergency situation
• Manual dexterity sufficient to perform repetitive hand/wrist/arm motions and to operate a computer and office equipment

KIPP MA aides are supported in their demanding work by experienced and dedicated leadership and staff who have themselves proven successful in the teaching role. Our leaders maintain consistent school-wide systems and procedures - academic, behavioral, cultural, logistical - designed to permit aides to do their best work.

In addition to the responsibilities listed above, there will occasionally be other duties as assigned that aides will engage in to help promote a positive and safe learning environment and culture.

QUALIFICATIONS

• Demonstrated ability to drive student growth and achievement and to create a warm, inclusive, rigorous learning environment (preferred)
• Possess an Associate’s Degree OR have completed 48 college credit hours OR pass the ParaPro Assessment with a score of at least 464 within a year of hire
• Experience and/or training in proper physical/tactical restraint procedure (preferred)
• Experience and/or training in proper ABA techniques for student support (preferred)
• Computer literacy and baseline familiarity with Google Suite
• Pass Criminal Background Checks

We believe in building a vibrant and welcoming school community that advances our mission of ensuring that all KIPP students graduate with the skills and confidence to lead fulfilling lives. This includes a commitment to attracting and developing individuals who understand the experiences of the students and communities we serve. We hire without consideration to race, religion, creed, color, national origin, age, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, or disability.

The minimum base salary for this exempt position is $37,000 to $50,000 (per 1.0 FTE/45 hours per week). The role includes a $1,000 signing bonus—and an annual $2,000 retention bonus in subsequent years, as well as other bonuses, when eligible. This role follows our School Year calendar. jobs.title: Family Medicine Physician
jobs.description:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.




ROLE PURPOSE

Physician to deliver Neko's preventive-care model to members in Aventura, FL— using advanced, non-invasive technology and clinical expertise to identify health risks early and translate findings into action plans that genuinely change what a member does next. This is a deeply collaborative role at the intersection of clinical excellence, member experience, and a conviction that catching things early changes lives. You'll work closely with Operators, APPs, and cross-functional partners to deliver a seamless, insight-driven member experience.


WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS

 - Comprehensive preventive health screenings delivered using Neko's high-resolution skin imaging, cardiovascular assessments, and AI-powered decision support — with consistent quality across every member visit.

 - Personalized, action-oriented health plans created from screening data, translated into next steps the member actually takes — measured by member follow-through and downstream outcomes.

 - Member education on dermatological and cardiovascular risk factors and lifestyle strategies that lands — measured by how the member felt about the consultation, not just the clinical findings.

 - Clinical oversight and escalation support provided to APPs, raising the bar for clinical quality and team performance across the clinic.

 - Cross-functional collaboration with Operators, APPs, and care teams that improves continuity of care and the end-to-end member experience.

 - Serve as supervising or collaborating physician to APP colleagues, raising the bar for clinical quality across the clinic.




WHAT WE’RE HIRING FOR

 - Genuine, personal commitment to preventive medicine — not just as a specialism, but as a way of practicing. You think it's wrong that this isn't how everyone practices medicine.

 - Member-first instinct — you take the member experience personally, not just procedurally, and measure a consultation's success by how the member felt, not only by the findings.

 - Team-lifting collaboration — you make the people around you better by showing up consistently, sharing what you know, and caring how the team performs as a whole.




MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

 - Active Florida State medical license.

 - Board certified in Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, or equivalent.

 - At least 1 year of post-residency experience.

 - Recent outpatient experience (at least a year in the past 5 years).

 - Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross,

 - Comfort working in a tech-forward, fast-moving clinical environment.




BENEFITS

 - Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and mental health coverage.

 - Complimentary full Neko scan for you and eligible family members.

 - CME benefit and broad state licensure support.

 - Flexible time off.
