jobs.title: Senior Insurance Business Analyst
jobs.description:
QUICK SUMMARY

Turn P&C product decisions into build-ready requirements, then confirm they shipped right. Forms, rating, state launches? Yes. 5+ years BA, 3+ in P&C required.




WHO WE ARE

Kin makes life simpler, more affordable, and better for homeowners — especially in the places where climate risks, rising costs, and outdated systems make it harder. We start with smarter homeowners insurance and expand to everything homeowners need to thrive.

Using data, technology, and thoughtful human support, we’re building products that are clear, fair, and help homeowners feel confident — so homeowners aren’t left behind when they need help most.

Founded in 2016, Kin is a remote-first employer with Kinfolk across more than 35 states. We serve customers in 14 states (and counting). Our disciplined growth, strong customer satisfaction, and focus on long-term sustainability fosters outstanding growth, attracts marquee investors, and earns recognition and accolades, including:

 - Built In Chicago's Best Places to Work, Midsize Companies (2021-2026)

 - Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers (2026)

 - Inc. 5000 Fastest-Growing Private Companies

 - Forbes’ Fintech 50 (2023-2026)

 - Great Places to Work Certified (May 2024-May 2027)

Most importantly, we’re building Kin to be a place where people do meaningful work with real impact — for our customers, our communities, and each other. We're excited to tell you more about how you can contribute to our rapid growth, strong unit economics, profitability, and excellent customer ratings. To learn more about how we work and what we’re building, visit kin.com http://kin.com and see how we work https://www.linkedin.com/company/kin-insurance/life/kin/.




THE OPPORTUNITY

We're looking for a Senior Insurance Business Analyst to help us turn insurance product decisions into systems that work exactly as intended. Kin keeps entering new states and expanding its products. Each launch, filing, and coverage change depends on clear translation between the people who design insurance products and the engineers who build them. This role sits at that intersection of insurance product development, operations, and technical delivery. It's built for someone who knows P&C insurance products deeply and asks the right questions early.

You'll sit within the Project Management Organization and own the requirements lifecycle for new products, state launches, endorsements, coverage changes, forms, rating updates, and compliance requirements. You'll work across Insurance Product, Actuarial, Underwriting, Compliance, Claims, Operations, Engineering, and Tech Product to define what needs to be built and confirm it was built correctly. As your ownership grows, you'll become the go-to resource for teams that depend on accurate, implementation-ready requirements. Your work will directly shape how quickly and reliably Kin brings products to homeowners.




YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the requirements lifecycle for insurance product and state-configuration changes, from initial discovery through an implementation-ready handoff to Engineering and Tech Product

 - Translate business decisions on new products, insurance filings, forms, endorsements, coverages, rating algorithms, eligibility rules, and state-specific configurations into clear business requirements and functional specifications

 - Partner with Insurance Product, Actuarial, Underwriting, Compliance, Claims, Operations, Tech Product, and Engineering to gather inputs, resolve ambiguity, confirm decisions, and maintain alignment from business decision through system deployment

 - Document current-state processes and system behavior, define future-state workflows, and manage requirements changes throughout delivery

 - Identify gaps, edge cases, dependencies, compliance requirements, and downstream impacts across rating, policy administration, billing, claims, servicing, and reporting before development begins

 - Assess the customer, operational, and system impact of proposed product rules, and recommend alternative approaches when a requirement would create unnecessary friction, cost, or unintended consequences

 - Build user stories, process flows, decision tables, data mappings, and acceptance criteria that let developers build accurately, while maintaining traceability from approved decisions through implementation and testing

 - Own requirements questions during development as the primary point of contact, documenting clarifications and decisions as they're made

 - Lead UAT planning, test scenarios, business review, and the product review and beta-validation process to confirm product changes are implemented correctly before broader release

 - Drive launch readiness and repeatable delivery through process documentation, stakeholder communication, handoff guidance, and continuously improved templates, checklists, and documentation standards


SUCCESS IN THIS ROLE

In your first 6–12 months at Kin, success is less about checking boxes and more about the impact you create. You’ll use your skills and judgment to take ownership of meaningful work, improve how we operate, and help move Kin’s mission forward. Along the way, you’ll deliver outcomes that make a real difference for both Kinfolk and the homeowners we serve.

By the end of your first year, you should feel confident in your role, trusted as an owner, and proud of the progress you’ve helped make.

 - Engineering and Tech Product treat your business and functional requirements as the definitive source of truth for product builds

 - Product decisions move to implementation-ready requirements faster, supporting quicker product and state launches

 - Clarification cycles, rework, and UAT delays have dropped because gaps and edge cases now surface before development starts

 - Requirements and implementation-review processes are consistent and scalable as Kin enters new states and expands its products


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 5+ years of experience in a business analyst, systems analyst, or similar role, including 3+ years in P&C insurance

 - Experience translating insurance product concepts (coverages, forms, endorsements, rating structures, eligibility rules, and state variations) into structured business and functional requirements for Engineering and Tech Product

 - Working knowledge of the insurance product lifecycle and how product decisions are configured and implemented in policy administration and related systems

 - Experience producing user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, decision tables, data mappings, and current- and future-state documentation

 - Experience partnering with Engineering or IT teams in an Agile or iterative delivery environment, including requirements clarification, UAT, and implementation validation

 - A track record of synthesizing input from multiple stakeholders into clearly documented decisions, and asking questions that surface ambiguity early

 - Experience managing requirements across multiple products, states, and concurrent initiatives at the same time

Bonus if you have

 - Experience at a direct-to-consumer insurer, insurtech, or managing general agent (MGA)

 - Knowledge of policy administration systems and how rating, forms, rules, and eligibility are configured in production

 - Industry designations or coursework (CPCU, AINS, or similar)

 - Proficiency with project management or requirements tools (Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, or similar)


HOW WE HIRE

We believe a great hiring experience should be clear, respectful, and human. We’ll accept applications for this position until November 14th, 2026. While our recruiting team uses AI tools for efficiency, resumes are still screened by Kin’s in-house recruiters, and candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are made by recruiters and hiring teams. Rest assured, real people make real decisions.

The hiring process and timeline for each role will vary, depending on the position. However, here are some things you can expect from us:

 - Prompt updates and feedback following interviews

 - Interviews with recruiters, hiring managers, and members of teams

 - Skills assessment relevant to the position, if applicable

 - Genuine, thoughtful human interaction at every step


HOW WE SUPPORT YOU

We offer a comprehensive, competitive benefits program, allowing you to choose the benefits that are best for you and your family, starting on the first day of the month following your start date.

Core Benefits

 - Competitive salary and company equity through Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), granted as part of our standard compensation package and based on role and level

 - 401(k) with company match up to 4% of eligible earnings

 - Multiple medical plan options, plus dental and vision coverage

 - Company-funded HSA contributions (based on medical plan selection)

 - Company-paid life insurance and short-term disability

Health & Wellbeing

 - A variety of supplemental benefit options, including long-term disability, critical illness, accident, legal, and pet insurance

 - Access to mental health support and confidential counseling resources

 - Flexible PTO for exempt employees (most employees take 15–20 days per year), plus 8 company-observed holidays

 - Paid parental leave, including up to 14 weeks at 100% pay for birthing parents and 8 weeks at 100% pay for non-birthing parents

Growth & Development

 - Career mobility and internal growth opportunities across the organization

 - Professional development budgets for certifications, conferences, and learning available, subject to management approval


HOW WE WORK

We don’t just hire for skills. We hire for alignment. Kinfolk bring diverse perspectives, but we’re united by a shared set of values that shape how we work and how we show up for each other and our customers.

Run through walls, together - Every one of us is responsible for creating the culture we want to work in. High performance. Low drama. Always respectful. We assume the best in each other and challenge ideas, not intentions. We show up, work hard, and play to each other's strengths — because that’s how great teams win.

Raise the bar. Drop the ego - Attitudes are contagious. Every one of us is responsible for creating the culture we want to work in. High performance. Low drama. Always respectful. Like professional sports teams, we win by working in sync. We show up, work hard, and play to each other’s strengths.

Act like an owner - We are owners, fully accountable for achieving Kin’s mission. That requires positive, proactive, big-picture thinking well beyond our job descriptions. Ask questions, Take ownership. Do the right thing, even when it‘s hard. Because when Kin thrives, so do you. And so do our customers.

Operate lean. Deliver more - We build efficiency into everything we do. Each dollar we save gets reinvested to deliver more to our customers: better pricing, more products, and new innovations. We work smarter by relentlessly prioritizing and using technology, including AI, to multiply our impact. Lean is about focus, not deprivation. Lean isn't a limitation — it's our competitive advantage.

Keep asking ‘What if?’ - We value curiosity. To make insurance better for our customers, we experiment. We embrace insights. And we base decisions on data rather than assumptions. We see setbacks as opportunities for growth and are always learning and improving. Both individually and as a company.




WHERE WE WORK

We are a remote-first company with offices in Chicago, IL and St. Petersburg, FL where teams can come together for collaboration.

For Sales Agents and Customer Service Agents: These roles sit in any of the following 32 states: AL, AZ, CO, FL, ID, IL, IN, KS, KY, LA, MA, MD, ME, MI, MO, MT, NC, NE, NM, NV, NY, OH, OK, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VT, VA, WA, and WI.

For all other positions, these roles can sit in any of the following 41 states: AL, AR, AZ, CA (exempt only), CO, CT, FL, GA, ID, IL, IN, IA, KS, KY, LA, MA, ME, MD, MI, MN, MO, MT, NC, NE, NJ, NM, NV, NY, OH, OK, OR, PA, SC, SD, TN, TX, UT, VT, VA, WA, and WI. Please only apply if you are able to live and work full-time in one of the states listed above.

For remote technical positions located in Canada, we are only able to hire individuals who reside in Ontario. Applicants must be able to live and work full-time in Ontario to be considered.

State locations and specifics are subject to change as our hiring requirements shift.




EEOC STATEMENT

Kin is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. We don't just accept difference – we honor it, nurture it, and celebrate it. We don’t discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Growth
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments and other OpenAI products worldwide. We work across the full funnel—from awareness and acquisition through activation, retention, and expansion—using experimentation, data science, machine learning, and product engineering to help more people discover and realize durable value from OpenAI’s products.

Our team partners closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Design, Finance, Lifecycle, and Growth Marketing. We move quickly, test rigorously, and hold a high bar for measurement, privacy, reliability, and user trust.




ABOUT THIS ROLE: 

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to build the models and decision systems that optimize paid marketing investment for ChatGPT and other OpenAI products. You will develop budget allocation and control algorithms that determine where to invest, how quickly to spend, and how to adjust as performance changes.

The challenge is to make reliable decisions from noisy, delayed, and incomplete signals. You will combine machine learning, optimization, and experimentation to improve incremental growth and long-term user value within budget and efficiency constraints. You will own this work from problem formulation and prototyping through deployment, evaluation, and ongoing operation.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to eligible employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build budget allocation algorithms. Decide how to distribute investment across channels, campaigns, and markets using estimates of marginal returns, while accounting for diminishing returns, uncertainty, and business constraints.

 - Develop spend pacing and adaptive control systems. Adjust budgets and spending rates as performance changes, balancing responsiveness with stability when feedback is delayed or noisy. Build in spend limits, monitoring, and safe fallback behavior.

 - Model marketing response and user value. Develop forecasts and models of conversion, long-term value, and saturation that help determine where the next dollar can have the greatest impact.

 - Evaluate decisions rigorously. Use simulations, backtesting, and online experiments to test allocation and control policies. Partner with Data Science to measure incrementality and validate whether offline improvements translate into better investment outcomes.

 - Own reliable production systems. Build data pipelines, training and inference workflows, and integrations that turn model outputs into budget decisions. Establish data-quality checks, monitoring, and retraining with thoughtful treatment of privacy and consent.

 - Turn business goals into optimization problems. Partner with Growth Marketing, Data Science, Engineering, and Finance to define objectives and constraints, communicate tradeoffs, and use evidence to improve investment decisions.

 - Help build a diverse and inclusive culture where people feel welcome, challenge assumptions, and collaborate with candor and respect.




You might thrive in this role if you:

 - 5+ years of experience as a Machine Learning Engineer, Applied Scientist, Data Scientist, or in a comparable quantitative engineering role, or an equivalent record of impact.

 - Experience building and operating production ML or quantitative decision systems, from problem formulation and data pipelines through deployment, experimentation, and monitoring.

 - Strong software engineering skills, proficiency in Python and SQL, and hands-on experience with ML frameworks and large-scale data systems.

 - Strong foundations in machine learning and statistics, with experience applying optimization or control methods to decisions under uncertainty.

 - Experience evaluating models or algorithms with noisy, delayed, or incomplete data, and the judgment to balance model quality, causal impact, and operational reliability.

 - The ability to turn ambiguous goals into focused experiments, interpret mixed results, and communicate clear decisions with technical and non-technical partners.

 - A collaborative working style and a commitment to deploying AI responsibly, in service of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. 

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf.

In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

jobs.description:

In 2011, Dollar Shave Club didn’t just shake up the shaving aisle—we reinvented it. A viral video put us on the map, and our direct-to-consumer model challenged an entire industry by making great razors accessible, affordable, and actually fun to buy.

Since then, we’ve grown far beyond blades. Today we’re building something bigger: a multi-brand personal care platform serving distinct shoppers across the full price ladder — with a modernized supply chain, deep retail relationships, and an AI-native way of working behind it.

DSC is expanding into new categories, new consumers, and new markets, but our DNA hasn’t changed. We’re still here to cut the BS, deliver real value, and bring a little humor to the everyday routine.

So what are you waiting for? Join the Club.

ROLE SUMMARY:

Dollar Shave Club is seeking a Maintenance Supervisor to oversee and optimize the performance of all on-site equipment and machinery. In this role, you will be responsible for maintaining the cleanliness and proper functioning of production machinery and components, as well as owning the site’s preventative maintenance program. You will troubleshoot machine and equipment issues as they arise, resolving them promptly to minimize operational downtime. Additionally, you will manage parts inventory, coordinate with vendors to ensure timely ordering and delivery of necessary parts, and be responsible for the training and development of the Machine Technician I.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Perform preventative and reactive maintenance on lift equipment jacks, chargers, and batteries

• Perform preventative and reactive maintenance on all conveyors, bar code readers, labeler machines, sensors, photo eyes and weigh scales

• Perform general building maintenance including dock overhead doors, construction repair, roll carts, floor repair and second level gates, doors, etc. Performs light plumbing maintenance on occasion

• Monitor and accurately maintain spare parts inventory

• Maintain all tools and equipment used for maintenance and repairs in good working order

• Submit tool purchase requests to manager

• Support automation to operate at its maximum efficiency ensuring delivery of contracted key performance indicators

• Perform various carpentry assignments as needed

• Ability to work at heights

• Use personal vehicle to pick up parts, tools and equipment

• Make decisions that positively impact our business goals, metrics and results

• Work as a team member by interacting and communicating with fellow associates in a cooperative, constructive manner

• Demonstrate understanding, support and execution of the company’s policies

• Act as a champion of our values, demonstrating them and holding your team to the same high standards

• Relay direction from Manager or Director to Maintenance technician I and assistants

• Use initiative to ensure efficient assignments of junior technicians/assistants to projects/tasks

QUALIFICATIONS:

Why EquipmentShare?

Because we do things differently — and we think you’ll feel it from day one. We’re a people-first company powered by cutting-edge technology. That means our proprietary T3 platform doesn’t just run our business — it also makes your job easier, safer, and more connected. Whether you’re behind the wheel, under the hood, leading a branch, or closing deals — tech supports you, and you drive us forward.

We’re a team of problem-solvers, go-getters, and builders. And we’re looking for teammates who take pride in doing meaningful work and want to be part of building something special.

About You

You want to be part of a team that’s not just changing an industry for the sake of change — we’re transforming it to make it safer, more secure, and more productive. You bring grit, heart, and humility to your work, and you’re excited about the opportunity to grow within a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

jobs.title: Founding Account Executive
jobs.description:
HELP BUILD THE NEXT CATEGORY-DEFINING AI COMPANY

AI has transformed how we write (chat), communicate (voice), and build software (code). The next frontier is even bigger: transforming how businesses actually operate (enterprise wide automation). That's what we're building at Sola.

Sola is an AI-native platform reinventing enterprise process automation and disrupting legacy RPA tools. Our AI agents can execute complex workflows across any application, browser, desktop, or legacy system—free from the limitations and fragility of traditional automation tools. Users simply record their screen, and Sola creates a custom agent to run that process at scale.

The opportunity at hand is enormous. Nearly every enterprise, across every industry, runs on processes that are still painfully manual. We're building the technology to change that. And we're just getting started.

We're hiring a small group of Founding Account Executives to help bring Sola to the world's largest enterprises and build the foundation of our go-to-market organization.

This isn't a role where you inherit a playbook. It's an opportunity to help write one.

 


WHY SOLA? WHY NOW?

 


A MASSIVE MARKET READY FOR REINVENTION.

Enterprise automation is one of the biggest opportunities in AI. Legacy RPA platforms have been constrained by rigid rules, complex implementations, and brittle workflows. Sola is changing that with AI agents that can reason, adapt, and execute work across enterprise systems: the next generation of a massive software category.

 


REAL TRACTION. SERIOUS MOMENTUM.

We've grown the business 10x in 2026, deployed across 20+ enterprise customers—including Fortune 500 companies—and demonstrated rapid expansion, with customers growing 2–5x in their first year. We've closed seven-figure enterprise deals, all with a lean, primarily founder-led sales motion. The product is proven. The market is responding. Now we're building the team to scale it.

 


BUILD ALONGSIDE LEADERS WHO'VE DONE IT BEFORE.

You'll report directly to our CRO, Alex Latraverse, who spent seven years at Flock Safety helping scale the business from $5M to $500M+ ARR and growing the AE organization from two sellers to more than 200.

You'll work closely with Alex and Sola's founders to shape our sales strategy, playbook, culture, and team. This is an opportunity to learn from experienced operators while having a direct voice in how the company grows.

 


EARLY-STAGE OWNERSHIP. EXCEPTIONAL UPSIDE.

Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Conviction, and Y Combinator, Sola has raised more than $20M to build the future of enterprise automation.

We're still early enough that individual contributions can meaningfully influence the company's trajectory. You'll own a largely greenfield opportunity, participate in the equity upside, and shape the organization you could one day help lead.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

As a Founding AE, you'll own the full enterprise sales cycle while helping define how Sola goes to market.

 - Win new enterprise customers. Build pipeline, open doors, and close complex six- and seven-figure opportunities.

 - Land and expand. Establish new customer relationships, prove value quickly, and grow accounts across business units.

 - Sell transformative technology. Help enterprise leaders reimagine how their organizations operate with AI.

 - Build the playbook. Partner directly with the CRO and founders to refine our positioning, sales process, and go-to-market strategy.

 - Help build the team. Shape the standards, culture, and practices that will define Sola's sales organization.

You'll have the autonomy to operate like an owner, direct access to leadership, and the opportunity to make an outsized impact from day one.

 


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for exceptional enterprise sellers who combine a track record of winning with the ambition to build something from the ground up. You'll likely be a strong fit if you have:

 - Approximately 5+ years of closing experience in enterprise SaaS or technology sales, or an equivalent track record of success.

 - A proven ability to self-source pipeline and consistently win net-new enterprise business.

 - Experience navigating complex sales cycles and closing six-figure deals.

 - A history of exceeding targets and performing at the top of your team.

 - An entrepreneurial mindset and excitement for the pace, ownership, and ambiguity of an early-stage company.

Experience selling AI, automation, data, security, or software into finance, operations, IT, legal, or risk teams is a plus.

We care more about what you've accomplished and what you're capable of building than where you've worked or how your résumé looks.

 


COMPENSATION

We believe exceptional performance deserves exceptional rewards.

 - Base salary: $137,500–187,500 annually

 - On-target earnings: $275,000–375,000 annually (50% base / 50% variable)

 - Uncapped commissions with accelerators for overperformance

 - Quarterly performance bonus opportunities in addition to commissions

 - Equity participation as a founding member of our sales team

On-target earnings reflect base salary plus target variable compensation at 100% quota attainment and are not guaranteed. Actual compensation depends on job-related qualifications and experience. Commissions and bonuses are subject to applicable compensation plans.

 


BENEFITS

We offer comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits, 401(k) matching, daily meals together in the office, flexible PTO (4 weeks per year), and relocation support for candidates not already based in NYC or Atlanta.

 


LET'S BUILD SOMETHING EXCEPTIONAL

The best career decisions come at moments of inflection—when a market is changing, a product is gaining momentum, and a small team has the opportunity to build something much bigger. Sola is now in one of these moments.

If you're an exceptional enterprise seller who wants to help define a category, build alongside experienced leaders, and participate meaningfully in the value you create, we'd love to meet you.

Come help us build the future of enterprise automation.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Quality
jobs.description:
The future of aerospace and defense starts here.

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.

Role Overview

The Senior Director, Quality is the senior quality leader for Ursa Major. This leader is accountable for product quality, quality compliance, and the effectiveness of the Quality Management System across all sites and product lines, including solid rocket motors, hypersonic propulsion, in-space propulsion, and avionics. Reporting to the Chief Safety and Risk Officer, the Sr. Director serves as the company’s senior quality representative to DCMA, government customers, and prime contractors. They will build the program and customer-facing quality capability Ursa Major needs as it scales from development into rate production and operates as a public company.

This role leads the full quality organization, including quality control, inspection, metrology and calibration, quality systems, and product quality engineering, with full authority to shape its structure as the business grows. The ideal candidate knows what prime-level quality looks like and how to deliver it at startup speed, scaling rigor to risk rather than adding bureaucracy. This is a senior leadership role, but it is also a hands-on one: we expect this leader to roll up their sleeves, lead from the front, and work in the trenches alongside the team as we scale.

Key Responsibilities

Quality Leadership & Strategy

• Own Ursa Major’s quality strategy, objectives, budget, and organization, structuring and developing the quality team to support growth across all product lines and sites.

• Build a culture of quality where every function owns quality and builds it into design, sourcing, manufacturing, and delivery.

• Match quality rigor to program maturity: move at the speed development programs require while meeting the full expectations of mature defense and prime customer programs.

Government & Prime Customer Quality

• Serve as Ursa Major’s senior quality representative to DCMA, government customers, prime contractors, and certification bodies, building trust-based relationships with DCMA quality assurance representatives and customer quality organizations.

• Lead quality across Ursa Major’s business models: all-up-round deliveries directly to the U.S. government, SRM and propulsion deliveries as a supplier to defense primes, and in-space propulsion systems for satellite and spacecraft customers.

• Build an organization capable of reviewing proposals and contracts for quality requirements, including FAR/DFARS quality clauses and customer-specific requirements, and ensure they flow down and implemented across design, purchasing, manufacturing, inspection, and delivery.

• Own government source inspection, product acceptance, and customer audit readiness, including WAWF acceptance, government first article approval, and witnessed lot acceptance testing.

• Partner with material control to 3nsure effective control of government-furnished property and material under FAR 52.245-1, and support DCMA property management system reviews in partnership with Supply Chain and Contracts.

• Lead the company’s response to customer corrective action requests, audit findings, and quality escapes.

Program Quality

• Build Ursa Major’s program quality function, providing dedicated quality ownership for major programs and customers from contract award through delivery.

• Own contractual quality deliverables and commitments, including first article inspection reports, acceptance data packages, certificates of conformance, as-built records, and customer witness and hold points, and represent quality in program reviews and customer meetings.

Quality Systems & Product Quality

• Own the AS9100 Quality Management System and scale it across sites and product lines, including certification and audits, management review, nonconformance and Material Review Board, corrective action, and Nadcap accreditation of special processes where customers require it.

• Maintain effective controls for configuration, traceability, quality records, foreign object prevention, and counterfeit parts prevention, including GIDEP reporting.

• Partner with Engineering and Mission Assurance on design reviews, qualification, first article, and production readiness, and support a disciplined production rate ramp across solid rocket motors, hydrazine satellite propulsion systems, and potential future liquid-engine all-up rounds.

• In partnership with Safety, ensure quality controls fit energetics manufacturing, including propellant processing, cast-cure operations, and lot control and traceability of energetic materials.

• Ensure quality coverage for avionics and electronics, including electronics assembly workmanship and software and firmware quality, developing the team expertise needed as the avionics business grows.

• Shape supplier quality through influence rather than ownership: partner with Procurement, which owns supplier engineering, to set supplier quality requirements and flowdowns, weigh in on the selection and approval of critical suppliers, and drive resolution of supplier escapes.

Authority & Public Company Governance

• Hold authority to stop production, testing, acceptance, or shipment when product conformity, safety, or contractual compliance may be compromised, with an independent escalation path to the CEO and Business Unit President.

• Lead cost of poor quality reduction and continuous improvement: partner with Finance to accurately capture scrap, rework, and warranty costs in line with public company financial controls and use that data to drive measurable improvements.

• Other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field.

• 10+ years of progressive quality experience in aerospace, defense, or similarly regulated manufacturing, including 5+ years in senior quality leadership building, scaling, and leading quality organizations.

• Direct, hands-on experience working with DCMA, including quality surveillance, government source inspection, and corrective action requests.

• Direct experience serving U.S. government and prime contractor customers, including contract quality requirements, FAR/DFARS quality clauses, requirement flowdowns, and customer audits.

• Demonstrated experience leading and sustaining an AS9100-certified Quality Management System.

• Experience leading quality through the transition from development into production and rate ramp.

• Track record of right-sizing quality rigor to risk, maintaining compliance and product integrity without slowing execution.

• Proven ability to build and sustain a strong culture of quality, where ownership of quality extends well beyond the quality organization.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with solid rocket motors, energetic materials, propellant processing, munitions, or tactical propulsion (strongly preferred).

• Public company experience (strongly preferred), including board-level reporting or supporting public company internal controls; experience through an IPO is a plus.

• Experience in both a traditional prime and a startup or non-traditional defense environment.

• Familiarity with avionics and electronics quality, such as electronics workmanship standards (IPC J-STD-001, IPC-A-610), ESD control, and software and firmware quality assurance.

• Master’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field.

• ASQ CMQ/OE, CQE, or CQA certification, or AS9100 lead auditor experience.

Working Conditions / Physical Demands

• Work performed in office, laboratory, and manufacturing environments, including hazardous and energetic operations areas that require personal protective equipment and adherence to explosives safety and site security protocols.

• Ability to sit or stand for extended periods and work on a computer for prolonged durations.

• Occasionally required to lift up to 25 pounds.

• Ability to travel up to 25% to Ursa Major sites, customers, suppliers, and government facilities.

Colorado law requires us to tell you the base compensation range of this role, which is $225,000 - $275,000, determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. What we can’t quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

Classification: Full-time Exempt

Benefits Include: (Please note, Interns are not eligible for benefits)

• Additional Benefit Options Including Voluntary Life and Emergency Medical Transport

How To Apply:
Interested candidates are encouraged to apply by filling out the application below and clicking "Submit Application". This position will be posted for a minimum of 3 days and will remain open until filled or adjusted based on the volume of applicants.

NOTE: Research suggests that women and BIPOC individuals may self-select out of opportunities if they don't meet 100% of the job requirements. We encourage anyone who believes they have the skills and the drive necessary to succeed here to apply for this role.

Must be a U.S. Person (this includes U.S. Citizens and Permanent Residents).

jobs.title: Underwriting Program Leader
jobs.description:
PROGRAM LEADER

Nirvana is on a mission to harness the power of data to revolutionize commercial insurance and enable a safer world. We're bringing much-needed innovation to the legacy, trillion-dollar commercial insurance industry with an AI-native platform that changes how an insurance company operates, from risk selection and pricing to underwriting, claims and loss prevention.

We proved the model in commercial auto, one of the toughest lines in insurance. Using real-time telematics data from more than 30 billion miles, we built predictive models that understand and price risk better. Since then we've grown to serve thousands of fleets and more than doubled written premium year over year, with a loss ratio, efficiency and customer experience that are redefining what's possible. Now we're taking the same platform (data, technology and underwriting discipline) into new lines of business and new programs.

With $270+ million raised, including our Series D round in December 2025, we’re only accelerating our growth, with strong support from top-tier VCs including Lightspeed, General Catalyst, and Valor. Nirvana’s leadership team has previously helped scale multi-billion-dollar companies from scratch, including Samsara, Glassdoor, and Flexport, and includes industry veterans from Nationwide, The Hartford, and RLI.



About the Role

Are you an underwriting leader with deep expertise in a profitable niche, and a clear view of the program you’d build if you had the capital, capacity, and right platform behind you? We’re opening this role to program leaders across lines of business who want to build and own a program of their choice on Nirvana’s platform. You bring the niche, the underwriting expertise and the relationships. We bring an AI-native platform, data science, engineering, capacity relationships, and the capital to launch and scale the program.”

You’ll be accountable for the program’s P&L, top line and bottom line, and you’ll build it in close partnership with Nirvana’s leadership. We’re not looking to replicate a traditional program. Together, we’ll design one that uses our data, technology and AI-native operating model from day one, and you’ll grow your own team as the program scales. The role comes with meaningful financial upside tied to the program’s success.



What you’ll do:

 - Bring a focused market thesis and develop it into the program’s strategy, risk appetite, underwriting guidelines and operating rhythm in partnership with senior leadership, turning a focused market thesis into a disciplined, profitable program.

 - Be the program’s lead line underwriter to get it off the ground, evaluating and pricing risks in your line and owning both new business and renewals.

 - Own the brokerage relationships that drive the program’s growth: build the wholesale and retail distribution network, set production goals and be the face of the program in the market.

 - Work closely with senior leadership, engineering, product and data science to shape the platform, underwriting workflows and operating procedures, so the program scales with technology instead of headcount.

 - Own the relationship with reinsurers and capacity partners, and be accountable to them for portfolio performance, reporting and renewals.

 - Build and lead the program team (underwriting, distribution and operations) as the program grows.

About you:

 - 10+ years of underwriting in a specialty or commercial line, with deep expertise in a defined niche.

 - A track record of managing a large portfolio, ideally $50M+ in premium, profitably and at scale.

 - A clear program thesis. You can explain the niche you’d target, why it’s profitable, why now, and how data and technology would give the program an edge.

 - Proven underwriting discipline. You’ve written underwriting guidelines and appetite before, and your results show you stick to them.

 - You’ve owned distribution. You’ve built and run broker relationships that drive production, and you enjoy getting on the road to meet partners.

jobs.description:

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE COMMISSIONING TEAM

 - Hold the controls schedule: sequence vendor startup, flag slips early against EFA/FA/FR milestones, and drive punch closure.

jobs.description:
About Upstart

At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.

As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

Upstart’s Solutions and Integrations team builds and scales the technology that connects our lending partners to Upstart. The team owns core banking and API integrations that automate lender onboarding and downstream loan workflows, with a focus on helping our lenders purchase loans seamlessly, supporting new lending products, and building scalable integration and production support models.

We've already built integrations with several major core banking platforms, and our priority now is helping more lending partners go live quickly, reliably, and at high quality. We're a small, collaborative team that works directly with lenders and partners across Product, Engineering, Implementation, and Account Management.

As an Integration Engineer, Lending Partnerships at Upstart, you will help scale adoption of Upstart’s existing core banking and API integrations by owning the technical onboarding of banks and credit unions. You will work directly with lending partners and internal teams to gather requirements, configure integrations, map data, establish connectivity, test end to end workflows, troubleshoot issues, and support successful production launches. Your work adds dedicated implementation capacity, so Upstart can support more simultaneous launches while keeping timelines predictable. This opportunity is a 6 month contract-to-hire role and is not eligible for Upstart’s employee compensation, equity, bonus, or benefits offerings.

How you’ll make an impact

• Own technical onboarding of lending partners from requirements gathering and data mapping through testing, production launch, and initial post launch support.

• Configure and support integrations using Workato, REST APIs, SFTP, and existing core banking connector frameworks.

• Partner directly with lender technology, operations, accounting, and implementation teams to understand requirements, resolve technical blockers, and maintain launch readiness.

• Execute and validate end to end workflows across member and account creation, loan boarding, funding related processes, document transfer, and downstream data updates.

• Troubleshoot production and implementation issues across APIs, data mappings, middleware, core banking platforms, and lender environments.

• Improve integration scalability by optimizing Workato workflows, strengthening production support processes, and turning repeatable implementation activities into standardized processes, templates, and automation.

Minimum Qualifications

• 4+ years of experience in integration engineering, solutions engineering, technical implementation, solutions architecture, or a similar customer facing technical role.

• Hands on experience implementing and troubleshooting REST API integrations, including JSON, authentication, data mapping, error handling, and API testing.

• Experience with systems integration, middleware, iPaaS platforms, or API based implementations.

• Experience gathering technical requirements and translating business workflows into integration requirements.

• Experience working directly with external customers or partners and independently driving technical issues toward resolution.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with Workato, MuleSoft, Boomi, Tray.io, or another integration platform; direct Workato recipe development experience is particularly valuable.

• Knowledge of banking, lending, fintech, or financial services integration workflows.

• Familiarity with core banking platforms such as Jack Henry Symitar, Fiserv DNA, Corelation Keystone, Fiserv Premier, FIS, or similar systems.

• Experience with SFTP, PGP encryption, NACHA files, loan boarding, account creation, or other banking integration workflows.

• Experience using Postman, SQL, or similar tools for API testing, data validation, and integration troubleshooting.

• Experience supporting production integrations, go live activities, monitoring, incident troubleshooting, and post production support.

Position location This role is available in the following locations: Remote

#LI-REMOTE

#LI-Associate

This is a Non-Exempt position. Employees in this position are paid an hourly pay rate, on a bi-weekly basis, and are eligible to receive overtime pay for any hours worked over 40 in a work week, or over 8 in a work day if required by state law.

Your actual base pay will depend on your geographic location–with our “digital first” philosophy, Upstart uses compensation regions that vary depending on location. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

In addition, Upstart provides employees with target bonuses, equity compensation, and generous benefits packages (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k).

United States | Remote - Anticipated Hourly Rate Range

$47.98—$66.35 USD

What you'll love

At Upstart, our benefits for full-time employees are designed to support your health, financial well-being, family, and personal growth. Here’s what you can expect:

• Competitive compensation, including base pay, bonus opportunities, and annual equity grants that vest quarterly

• Retirement benefits to help you plan for the future, including a 401(k) or Group Retirement Savings Plan with a company match of $2 for every $1 contributed, up to $15,000 annually (USD in the US, CAD in Canada)

AIR’s Learning Supports program area is seeking a part-time Tennessee-based Special Education Technical Assistance Provider to lead and deliver evidence-based professional development, coaching, and technical assistance that improves special education services and outcomes for students with disabilities at the local, state, and federal levels. The TA Provider will provide expertise in the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) and effective instructional practices, develop training and implementation resources, build relationships with education leaders and partners, lead project teams and tasks, support business development, and provide virtual and onsite assistance to educators across Tennessee.

This remote position requires residency in Tennessee and the ability to travel throughout the state as needed to support project and client needs.

About AIR:

Founded in 1946 and headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, the American Institutes for Research (AIR) is a nonpartisan, not-for-profit organization that conducts behavioral and social science research and delivers technical assistance to address some of the most pressing challenges in the United States and globally. We generate evidence and apply data-driven solutions that expand opportunities and improve lives for all.

Responsibilities:

The responsibilities for the position include:

• Develop training materials, implementation measures, and protocols for monitoring and providing feedback on implementation.

• Deliver training, professional development, and coaching to support teachers in implementing new programs and/or improving their instruction using structured protocols.

• Provide expertise on literacy teaching and learning to support research activities including, but not limited to, recruitment of study participants, development of implementation and related outcomes measures, data collection, and implementation analyses.

• Contribute to the development of reports that describe and interpret findings for clients, partners, and other relevant audiences.

• Represent the organization in interactions with state, local, and site-based staff; potential clients; and partner organizations.

• Contribute to capacity building efforts within special education organizations and provider networks.

• Work on collaborative project teams, including supervision of research/TA assistants and associates as a task or functional lead.

• Contribute to team efforts to develop new business opportunities including strategic planning, identification and pursuit of opportunities, and proposal development.

• Manage or lead projects or tasks, with assumption of greater responsibility over time.

Qualifications:

Education, Knowledge, and Experience

• Master’s or Ph.D. degree in special education or related field with a minimum of 4 years of relevant experience in education or a Bachelor’s degree with at least 6 years of relevant experience.

• Knowledge of the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) and related special education requirements.

• Extensive experience designing and delivering virtual and onsite professional development and coaching to local educators in Tennessee.

• Experience using evidence-based instructional practices and effective strategies to design and deliver professional development and adult learning.

• Extensive experience providing direct special education-related training, coaching, or technical assistance to local educators or instructional leaders.

• High attention to detail and a strong commitment to accuracy and quality.

• Willingness and ability to travel locally within Tennessee and nationally as needed.

• Ability to lead and collaborate effectively in both in-person and virtual environments.

jobs.title: Head of MyG Core Workflows
jobs.description:
Who we are:

Geotab ® is a global leader in IoT and connected transportation and certified “Great Place to Work™.” We are a company of diverse and talented individuals who work together to help businesses grow and succeed, and increase the safety and sustainability of our communities.

Geotab is advancing security, connecting commercial vehicles to the internet and providing web-based analytics to help customers better manage their fleets. Geotab’s open platform and Geotab Marketplace ®, offering hundreds of third-party solution options, allows both small and large businesses to automate operations by integrating vehicle data with their other data assets. Processing billions of data points a day, Geotab leverages data analytics and machine learning to improve productivity, optimize fleets through the reduction of fuel consumption, enhance driver safety and achieve strong compliance to regulatory changes.

Our team is growing and we’re looking for people who follow their passion, think differently and want to make an impact. Ours is a fast paced, ever changing environment. Geotabbers accept that challenge and are willing to take on new tasks and activities - ones that may not always be described in the initial job description. Join us for a fulfilling career with opportunities to innovate, great benefits, and our fun and inclusive work culture. Reach your full potential with Geotab. To see what it’s like to be a Geotabber, check out our blog and follow us @InsideGeotab on Instagram.

Who you are:

We are always looking for amazing talent who can contribute to our growth and deliver results! Geotab is seeking a Head of MyG Core Workflows who will own the MyGeotab workflows customers depend on, ensuring their usability, reliability, and evolution while enabling other product domains to build on shared capabilities. If you love technology, and are keen to join an industry leader — we would love to hear from you!

What you'll do:

The Head of MyG Core Workflows owns the MyGeotab workflows every customer depends on and is accountable for their usability, reliability, and evolution, both as customer-facing product and as shared capability other domains build on. The scope spans driver messaging; notifications (types, templates, recipients, and delivery channels, including reliability and latency); exception rules, stock rules, and how exceptions appear across reports and the map; system settings; the group hierarchy and its UI; and investigations that reconstruct what happened in context. This leader sets the vision for these workflows and how other domains build on rules, notifications, and groups, and answers to MyGeotab customers, the domain's primary customers, and the product domains that depend on it.

Key Accountabilities:

• People leadership, development, and organizational health.

• AI-native product development lifecycle, including AI-assisted modernization of legacy MyGeotab workflow pages.

• Cross-domain communication and coordination.

• Product ownership and engineering standards for MyGeotab core workflows

• Customer outcomes and reliability, with MyGeotab customers as primary customers and dependent product domains as internal customers

How you'll make an impact:

Product Engineering & Technical Standards

• Define, maintain, and evolve the technical standards, architectural patterns, and shared components for the domain's workflows.

• Own the reliability, scalability, and performance of messaging, notification, rules UI, and exception services; accountable to customer-facing SLOs for notification delivery success and latency. Own regression protection and VIP-customer test coverage so no release silently breaks customers' rules or notifications.

• Lead the identification and resolution of technical debt, security vulnerabilities, and compliance requirements in the domain, including the integrity of group-based data visibility, in coordination with Core API and Security.

• Shape and communicate the vision for core workflows to solution and segment domains; publish and maintain the capability contract for rules, notifications, and groups — intended use patterns, integration standards, and system constraints — so consuming domains can build on reusable platform capability correctly and confidently; keep platform tooling decisions aligned with the needs of consuming domains.

• Modernize legacy MyGeotab workflow pages to the Zenith/React stack, using AI-assisted conversion where practical, while preserving the behaviour customers depend on.

Customer Outcomes & Enablement

• Treat product domain teams as internal customers of rules, notifications, and groups; proactively understand their evolving needs and remove blockers. MyGeotab customers remain the domain's primary customers.

• Own product discovery and the domain roadmap with the domain's product manager and designers; prioritize transparently based on customer impact, reliability, and the needs of dependent domains.

• Define and measure customer and product metrics as primary success indicators: notification delivery success and latency, exception-to-notification time, rules-related incidents and PMIRs, support ticket volume per feature, feature adoption and usage, and investigation escalation accuracy.

• Establish feedback loops with peer Heads of Domain to capture platform gaps and translate them into actionable improvements.

• Provide technical consultation and guidance to product domain teams on the capabilities and constraints of rules, notifications, and groups.

• Manage external delivery dependencies (email, SMS, voice, and webhook providers) and internal dependencies (Gateway/embedded for in-vehicle feedback, Drive and in-cab devices for messaging, the rules engine, Video, and Safety) — integration standards and the risk each dependency creates for reliability and roadmap.

People Development

• Provide career development support.

• Conduct regular 1:1s and performance conversations.

• Support employees through KPA goal-setting and development planning.

• Oversee the hiring, onboarding, development, and performance management of a cross-functional team consisting of product managers, designers, and product engineers or other skills as required.

• Support company-wide strategic initiatives including AI adoption, security posture, accessibility, and compliance programs as directed.

• Identify growth opportunities and training aligned to domain needs.

• Foster a high-trust, high-accountability team culture that values craftsmanship, documentation, and service mindset.

• Manage team capacity and resource allocation across roadmap initiatives, customer commitments, and support obligations.

Domain Strategy & Roadmap

• Translate board-level strategic direction into a coherent domain roadmap and execution plan.

• Own the domain investment portfolio within approved parameters; make principled trade-offs between new capability, reliability, and technical debt reduction.

• Lead annual planning processes including headcount, budget, and OKR input to department leadership.

• Track and report on domain health, customer outcomes, and team delivery through defined KPIs; surface risks and recommendations to board leadership.

Cross-Domain Coordination

• Contributes domain expertise to cross-domain initiatives when assigned. Maintains clear, documented ownership boundaries with adjacent domains — notably the rules engine (evaluation and processing), Safety (collision reconstruction and post-collision workflows), and Geospatial (zones).

• Collaborate with product domain leads to align core workflow capabilities with product roadmaps and delivery timelines.

• Participate in department planning forums as a subject-matter authority for MyGeotab core workflows; represent domain constraints and opportunities clearly to board leadership.

Board Relationship & Accountability

• Own and execute the domain strategy within board-set direction.

• Make investment cases to the board for resourcing, headcount, and capability investment.

• Operate under structured board coaching with increasing autonomy.

Geotab First Mindset

• Champions a Geotab First approach to leadership by putting the success of the broader organization ahead of siloed or individual domain wins.

• Beyond leading their own domain, actively fosters collaboration, builds consensus, and works effectively across diverse internal and external teams.

• Seeks out different perspectives before decisions are made, shares credit and information openly, and treats other domains' priorities as shared priorities.

• Drives collective success through strong interpersonal relationships, shared goals, and a willingness to flex personal or domain agendas in service of the company's broader objectives.

What you'll bring to the role:

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Equivalent combination of education and work experience in a related field may be substituted.

• 5+ years of relevant industry experience.

• 5+ years of experience in SaaS or web product engineering or product management, ideally on configuration-heavy, multi-tenant products.

• 3+ years in technical leadership roles.

• 3+ years of leadership experience.

• 1+ years leading a cross-functional team of product managers, designers, and engineers.

• Deep technical and product expertise in configuration-heavy, multi-tenant B2B SaaS workflows; experience with event, alerting, and multi-channel notification systems (delivery, templating, rate limiting).

• Demonstrated ability to lead through influence in a matrixed or shared-services organizational model.

• Strong product sense and UX judgment — able to make complex configuration (rules, groups, notifications) powerful for large fleets yet simple for small ones.

• Strong systems thinking — ability to anticipate how platform decisions ripple across multiple consuming teams.

• Proficient in defining and tracking SLOs, customer-facing product metrics, and reliability indicators.

• Ability to shape and evangelize a vision for core workflows across consuming domains — communicating intended use patterns, constraints, and trade-offs of reusable capability so solution and segment teams adopt it correctly.

• Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills; able to translate technical concepts into customer and business impact for non-technical peers and leadership.

• Experience operating in evolving organizational structures with ambiguity and shifting priorities.

• Familiarity with modern engineering practices: CI/CD, DevSecOps, cloud-native architecture, observability, and agile delivery. Knowledge of telematics or fleet management is an asset.

• AI Nativity: Ability to redesign the domain's workflows around AI to compress effort.

• Change Readiness: Lead change through a larger domain; manage resistance and sustain momentum.

If you got this far, we hope you're feeling excited about this role! Even if you don't feel you meet every single requirement, we still encourage you to apply.

jobs.title: Software Architect, Plans
jobs.description:
About Wellfit:
Wellfit is a healthcare fintech platform that connects patients, providers, employers, and payors to remove financial barriers to care. Our technology enables healthcare organizations to offer flexible payment and financing solutions that improve patient access while helping providers grow their practices.

As Wellfit continues to scale, we are investing in modern platform architecture that supports innovation, speed, intelligent automation, and highly configurable product experiences.

About Wellfit Plans:
Wellfit Plans is a platform that enables healthcare providers and organizations to offer customizable patient membership plans, discount programs, and treatment-related financial programs.
The platform supports:• Plan configuration
• Eligibility and enrollment workflows
• Provider administration
• Billing and payment integrations
• Reporting across a growing network of healthcare organizations

About the Role:
Wellfit is seeking a Plans Architect to lead the architecture and evolution of the systems that power our Plans platform. This role will focus on the platform capabilities behind plan configuration, eligibility and enrollment logic, provider administration workflows, billing and payment integrations, reporting, and treatment-related financial programs.
This is not a narrowly scoped application architecture role. The Plans Architect will need to think across product workflows, front-end experiences, backend services, APIs, data, integrations, and platform foundations.
This person will help modernize and scale a business-critical product area while bringing structure and clarity to complex technical and business problems.
The ideal candidate is hands-on enough to understand the technical details, senior enough to guide architecture, and able to lead teams through complexity with precision, ownership, and strong technical judgment.

Key Responsibilities:
Plans Architecture & Ownership• Architect and evolve the systems that support Wellfit’s Plans platform, including plan configuration, eligibility and enrollment workflows, provider administration, billing and payment integrations, and reporting.
• Design scalable, maintainable solutions across a hybrid environment of legacy and modern systems.
• Guide the evolution of Plans toward a more modular, service-oriented, and AI-enabled architecture.
• Translate complex business rules and healthcare finance workflows into practical technical designs.
• Identify opportunities to simplify, consolidate, or modernize services, workflows, and configuration logic.

Technical Leadership
• Lead and mentor engineers working across the Plans ecosystem.
• Guide architectural decisions across front-end, backend, API, data, and integration work.
• Establish strong engineering standards for maintainability, reliability, and delivery quality.
• Help teams move quickly while staying aligned to architectural direction and product intent.

Stakeholder Collaboration
• Partner with Product, Engineering, Platform, Operations, and business stakeholders to understand Plans workflows and business needs.
• Communicate architectural decisions clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
• Serve as a technical bridge between product strategy, engineering execution, and platform scalability.

AI-Augmented Development
• Participate in Wellfit’s BMAD environment.
• Use AI-driven development tools and workflows to accelerate delivery and improve engineering productivity.
• Help the team adopt AI as a force multiplier for design, development, testing, documentation, and problem-solving.

Qualifications:
• 8+ years of software engineering experience.
• 3+ years in architecture, principal engineering, or senior system design roles.
• Strong experience with C# and .NET ecosystems.
• Experience with Azure cloud environments.
• Experience designing APIs, service architectures, distributed systems, and integration patterns.
• Familiarity with SQL and enterprise data architectures.
• Experience working in environments with both legacy and modern systems.
• Ability to understand and guide front-end architecture, ideally with Angular or a similar modern framework.
• Experience with complex business rules, configurable systems, eligibility logic, enrollment workflows, billing workflows, or workflow-heavy applications.
• Strong communication skills with technical, product, and business stakeholders.
• Thrives in bringing structure and clarity to complex problems.

Preferred Experience:
• Experience in healthcare technology, fintech, dental technology, insurance, payments, lending, or regulated platforms.
• Experience with provider-facing applications, membership plan platforms, discount programs, treatment planning, plan configuration, eligibility workflows, enrollment workflows, or payor-aligned rules.
• Experience with microservices, containerization, and distributed cloud architectures.
• Experience integrating with external vendors or third-party systems.
• Familiarity with AI-augmented development workflows.

Why Join Wellfit:
• Build business-critical platform capabilities powering a rapidly growing healthcare fintech company.
• Help shape the future architecture of Wellfit’s Plans platform.
• Work in an environment investing heavily in AI-driven development and platform innovation.
• Collaborate with a high-impact engineering organization building modern healthcare finance technology.
• Make Impact: Help expand access to care by improving the systems that connect providers, patients, employers, and payors.
• Hybrid Flexibility: 3 days per week in our Dallas office.
• Competitive Compensation: Salary, bonus eligibility, and 401(k) matching.
• Comprehensive Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, and generous PTO.
• Growth Opportunity: Join a profitable, scaling company building modern, AI-enabled infrastructure.

jobs.description:
Opportunity

What We're Looking For

Ideal Candidate

Why Join Us

Whether you are joining a client facing team, a core services team, or starting out on your professional career journey, joining Brunswick unlocks a range of exceptional employee benefits to support your financial future, health and wellness, family and community and continuous professional development.

jobs.title: Data Scientist II
jobs.description:
At Public Storage, data science sits right next to the decisions. Prices move every day across thousands of locations, and our models help decide them. As a Data Scientist II, you’ll be the go-to data scientist for one part of the business: customer and revenue, capital allocation (acquisitions, development and finance), or operations. You’ll be part of their planning, shape the questions, and build the models they rely on.

We’re a small, senior team that works like a startup inside an S&P 500 company. Ideas get to production quickly, you own your work, and it shows up in the business rather than in a slide deck.

What you’ll do

• Build and own production models. Pricing and elasticity, promotions, marketing effectiveness, demand forecasting, retention, lifetime value and recommendation. You’ll write production-grade Python and SQL, and use LLMs, embeddings and RAG where they’re the right tool.
• Be the data science partner for your business area. Join their planning, turn ambiguous questions into well-scoped problems, and present results as decisions and dollars, not model metrics.
• Run experiments that change what we do. Design and analyze A/B tests, holdouts and quasi-experiments. Set the success metric before launch and report the honest result after it.
• Build once, reuse everywhere. Work from our shared customer and real estate data and certified metrics, and add reusable models to a shared catalog so the next problem starts faster.
• Grow the team around you. Mentor analysts and junior scientists through code review and pairing, and back up a teammate’s business area when needed.
• Own the full model lifecycle. Versioning, retraining, drift monitoring and documentation, meeting our model governance standards before anything goes live.

What success looks like

• Business partners depend on your models every week.
• Your experiments change what the company does, not just what it knows.
• Junior scientists get better because of your code reviews.

• Bachelor’s degree in a STEM or quantitative field, such as statistics, computer science, economics, engineering or applied mathematics.
• 3+ years in a production data science role, or 2+ years with a Master’s, or 1+ year with a PhD.
• Strong SQL and Python in production settings, not notebooks alone.
• Applied statistics in both frequentist and Bayesian frameworks, plus experimental design and causal inference.
• A track record of shipping models that drove measurable business outcomes.
• Experience with a cloud data platform. Google Cloud and BigQuery preferred; Snowflake, AWS or Azure considered.
• Able to turn an ambiguous business question into a scoped problem, and explain uncertainty and trade-offs to non-technical partners.

Preferred

• 5+ years of production data science in pricing, revenue management, marketing, real estate, retail or consumer analytics.
• The modern ML stack: scikit-learn, XGBoost/LightGBM, PyTorch, PyMC, Prophet, and experiment tracking with MLflow or Vertex AI.
• MLOps experience: model registries, CI/CD, scheduled retraining and monitoring.
• dbt and orchestration tools such as Airflow or Cloud Composer.
• Hands-on experience with LLM applications, vector search, RAG or agentic AI workflows.

Workplace

• One of our values pillars is to work as One Team and we believe that there is no replacement for in-person collaboration but understand the value of some flexibility. Public Storage teammates are expected to work in the office five days each week with the option to take up to three flexible remote days per month.

Public Storage is an equal opportunity employer and embraces diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected status. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

**Sponsorship for Work Authorization is not available for this posting.  Candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without restrictions or requiring sponsorship now or in the future. We do not provide training plans or support for F-1 OPT, STEM OPT extensions, or future visa sponsorship.**

jobs.title: Senior Electrical Engineer
jobs.description:
At Serve Robotics, we’re reimagining how things move in cities. Our personable sidewalk robot is our vision for the future. It’s designed to take deliveries away from congested streets, make deliveries available to more people, and benefit local businesses. 

The Serve fleet has been delighting merchants, customers, and pedestrians along the way in Los Angeles, Miami, Dallas, Atlanta and Chicago while doing commercial deliveries. We’re looking for talented individuals who will grow robotic deliveries from surprising novelty to efficient ubiquity.




WHO WE ARE

We are tech industry veterans in software, hardware, and design who are pooling our skills to build the future we want to live in. We are solving real-world problems leveraging robotics, machine learning and computer vision, among other disciplines, with a mindful eye towards the end-to-end user experience. Our team is agile, diverse, and driven. We believe that the best way to solve complicated dynamic problems is collaboratively and respectfully.

Responsibilities

 - Design, develop, and validate electrical circuits, PCBs, harnesses, and subsystem architectures for autonomous robotic platforms.

 - Own electrical subsystem development from concept through prototype, validation, production release, and lifecycle support.

 - Lead hardware bring-up, debugging, characterization, and verification activities in partnership with firmware and software teams.

 - Perform root cause analysis and resolve complex electrical and system-level issues identified during development, manufacturing, and field operations.

 - Develop test plans, validation procedures, and performance metrics to ensure subsystem reliability and quality.

 - Collaborate with mechanical, firmware, systems, test, manufacturing, and operations teams to support successful subsystem integration and product execution.

 - Partner with suppliers and manufacturing teams on component selection, DFM/DFT improvements, production readiness, and issue resolution.

 - Support prototype builds, factory activities, engineering investigations, and field issue resolution as needed.

 - Contribute to technical documentation, design reviews, engineering standards, and continuous improvement initiatives.

 - Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers and contribute to knowledge sharing across the team.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or related engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

 - 8+ years of experience designing and testing electrical systems for robotics, consumer electronics, automotive, aerospace, or other electromechanical products.

 - Strong experience with schematic design, PCB development, subsystem integration, and electrical system validation.

 - Hands-on experience debugging and testing electrical subsystems using laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, electronic loads, and function generators.

 - Experience with embedded systems development, hardware bring-up, debugging, and failure analysis.

 - Experience using industry-standard ECAD tools, preferably Altium.

 - Experience working with common hardware interfaces such as CAN, SPI, UART, I2C, and USB.

What Makes You Stand Out
